Web (composer, one bubble with each file and its text) = session 12 after (a). **Debts:** `Message.content` is still the only text that search, export, draft and preview read, so the texts under files 2 and later are not searched (7.4); the columns `messages.caption_*` stay for the first file until a later step retires them with `content`; an audio text is refused as before until (b) sends it apart. **Accepted in review (rule 12):** the replay of an idempotency key returns the original message without re-validating the texts, by design of every replay; the negative audit assertion in `conversations.spec.ts` waits a fixed 500 ms (the audit writer has no flush; a deterministic one is due in 7.4); the diagnostic of an unresolved quote counts the customer's messages also for an owner's echo. The text under the FIRST file lives in `messages.content` (an edit settles there) and the view shows it as the caption of place 0.
  - [x] **(b) The worker (PR `feat/caption-steps-worker`):** **[Superseded in part by the cut of the text under each file (owner, 2026-11-09): only a channel with `CAPTION_PER_FILE` carries a text under a file; the state, the echo and the resend of a text apart per file, and the route by file, are gone (PR `refactor/drop-per-file-caption-state`); the columns `media.caption_state` and `media.caption_channel_message_id` are dropped by migration `20261116100000`.]** one job still sends the message, in order, file by file; the state of each file and of each text is in the database (`media.delivery_status`, `media.caption_state`, `media.caption_channel_message_id`), a file already `sent` is never sent again, the sweep resumes from the first file not sent, an attempt that may have reached the provider is `tainted` and not judged again, and the locks are taken for state only, never across a call. **Decision (rule 12), differs from the plan of the coordinator in one point:** the best rejected alternative was one job per step chained (next step queued by the one that ends). It was rejected because the loop already gives order, resume and tainted semantics from the database, and a chain would have moved the in-memory aggregate of the message (`allRefused`, `anySent`, the definitive flag) into a second place to rebuild from rows on every step, in the most delicate code of the sends; if a deployment shows the single job too long, the split is a follow-up. Worst case measured: ten files with ten texts that go after them (twenty calls) add 80 ms of the core around a provider that answers at once (`outbound.spec.ts`); the provider's own time is bounded per call (205 s for a file with its text, 20 s for a text after it), so 10 files are at most about 37 minutes, under the hour after which a reply is given up. The pace is that of the files today (one call after the answer to the previous, no parallelism). Each file carries its own text (`media.caption`; the first file's is the message's): Meta channels keep sending it as a message of its own inside `sendMedia` and the worker keeps its id and state on THE FILE the moment it is answered (the echo finds it), WhatsApp and the widget carry it natively, and a kind with no place for a text on the channel (an audio on WhatsApp) is sent without it and the text follows with `sendMessage`. Before the first file leaves, every text is checked; the window is checked at every file after the first (a closed one fails the rest with `CHANNEL_WINDOW_EXPIRED`, in order). `POST /messages/:id/media/:mediaId/resend-caption` sends only that text again (from `failed` or `unconfirmed`, never automatic, the sweep ends a stale request as `unconfirmed`). `OUTBOUND_CAPTION_PER_FILE_ENABLED` stays off by default and on in the e2e. **Long job, with evidence (coordinator's condition):** BullMQ 6.3.4 defaults apply to the outbound queue (no override in `apps/worker`): `lockDuration` 30 s renewed every 15 s (`lockRenewTime` = half) by a timer for as long as the process lives, and the stalled check every 30 s only takes a job whose lock expired (a dead process or a blocked event loop; the send only awaits network, so the loop is free), with `maxStalledCount` 1; a job that is active is not added again by the sweep (same job id), so the sequence cannot be duplicated while it works. Head of line: the queue runs 20 jobs at once per process, so a sequence of 37 minutes holds one slot of 20 and does not hold up other messages of the same connection (jobs are not serialized per connection). A resume after a death is tested (files 1 and 2 sent, the text of the first in doubt, a worker that comes back sends only file 3 and its text). **Debt with owner (Step 7.3):** if a long sequence ever blocks the queue of a connection, split the job into steps queued one by one (the chain N to N+1 the coordinator asked for first); not done now because the loop already gives order, resume and the tainted rule from the database. **Review of (b) (high), fixed:** one text request at a time per message (the version of the message is the request, two at once left the first job without its turn); an apart text is marked in doubt BEFORE its file goes, so a death between the file and the text leaves it `unconfirmed` and the agent can send it again; a failure to write the state of a text after its file went is logged and never makes the file fail; the echo of an unconfirmed text of a file other than the first finds it; the text of the first file is the message's (an edit settles there) in the resend and its state is also written on the message; the time of a request is cleared only when no other text, edit or deletion of the message waits; a resend needs the file to have gone. Left (7.4): the sweep settles each waiting text in its own transaction (N+1 for a message with many texts in doubt). **Debts (older note):** an apart text whose job died between its file and the text is now resendable (see above), but still not resent by itself (the file is `sent` and the text has no state; the agent sees the file with no text); logging never carries a text, only its length; the plugins (c) and the screen are next.

The audit write stays fire-and-forget like every audit of the api, so the pair is still lost if the process dies between the commit and the write (7.4).

A message with neither text nor a clean file (still scanned, infected) is not shown, in the history or live. The three places that decide what a visitor may read (the history, the live delivery and the download) share one rule, `visitorMessagesWhere` (their own messages, and the store's that the channel took; no note, system line, deleted message or reply still waiting or failed) and `WIDGET_FILES_SELECT` (a file of purpose `message` that is `clean`; the picture of an ad never). **`POST /widget/download-url`** (`ApiRoutes.widget.download`, `WidgetThrottle.DOWNLOAD`, preflight answered like the others): body `visitorToken` and `mediaId`; the token names the site and the visitor, the file must hang from a message `visitorMessagesWhere` lets that visitor read, of the store of the site, and anything else (another visitor's, another store's, a note, a deleted or unsent message, an ad, a missing id) is the same 404. The file must be `clean` (`WIDGET_FILES_SELECT`, the rule of the history), so a pending or infected file is the same 404 and the visitor learns nothing of the scan; the link is signed by the unchanged `MediaService.urlsFor` (`MediaModule` now exports it) and the original is always an attachment download; the answer is `{ url, filename, contentType, previewUrl }`, where `previewUrl` is the medium WebP variant for an image and `null` otherwise. The readers of "Seen" (`readUpTo`) count a message of files. The history query asks for something to show (a text or a clean file) so that files still being scanned do not use the 50 slots of the window, and `sendMedia` refuses video and audio. Cases: `the files of a conversation` and one socket case in `tests/api/widget.spec.ts`, the plugin spec. **Left (PR F3):** the bundle: the paperclip, the upload with progress, the attachment drawn (it asks `download-url` when the visitor opens it), the field error of the phone below, inside the 40 KB gzip budget. **Known limits of F2 (rule 12):** (1) only a file the scan found clean is listed, so a file the visitor just sent appears in the history after its scan, not at once (the bundle shows it from its own state meanwhile); (2) an agent can send images and documents to a visitor, not video or audio (the visitor can send them; declaring them is a task of Step 7.4 with the player); (3) the download throttle (60 a minute) is per address like the other public routes, with no per-visitor counter, and the bundle asks one link per file it opens or previews, so F3 must ask on demand (not one call per history message) and a preview link in the history answer is the fix if that is not enough (Step 7.3, with the other abuse limits of public routes); the media row is read twice per link (the ownership check and `urlsFor`), accepted; (4) a store site that still serves a bundle from before F3 draws a file-only message as an empty bubble. **Known limits of F1 (rule 12, from its review):** (1) the per-visitor cap keys on a `visitorId` the client chooses at the bootstrap, so a script can mint visitors and drain the per-site cap (`UPLOAD_URLS_PER_SITE_PER_HOUR`) for real visitors; the address throttle (`WidgetThrottle`) bounds the rate, and a per-address hourly counter is a task of Step 7.3 with the other abuse limits of public routes; (2) a message must omit `content` when it has only files (`content: ''` is refused as an empty text); the bundle of F3 omits it. (3) the record of an upload and its claim last `UPLOAD_TTL_SECONDS` (1 hour): a resend of an already queued message after that is refused instead of answered again; (4) a message takes its type from its first file, so a PDF followed by an image is a `DOCUMENT` with an image among its media (the inbox draws each file by its own type; the gallery filters by the file); (5) the api checks size and type of the staged object but does not pin its etag as `confirmUpload` does, so bytes swapped through the still-valid signed URL before the fetch are possible; the worker checks type and size again on the bytes it reads and scans the copy, so nothing unscanned is ever served. A file of the visitor shows in the inbox as soon as the worker has it; until the scan ends it is `pending`, like any file **Done in PR F3 (the bundle, 27.2 KB gzip of 40):** a paperclip beside the text field picks files (`accept` is the allowed types; `refuseFile` applies the rule of the api, `refuseUpload`, before any byte leaves, and at most `UPLOADS_PER_MESSAGE` stay staged, each removable), `Session.send(content, files)` writes the message at once and puts the files up one after the other (`POST /widget/upload-url`, then an XHR `PUT` for the progress, shown as a bar that moves in place), then names them in `uploadIds` of `POST /widget/messages`, omitting `content` when there is only files. A retry puts up only what is missing and sends under the same message id; an upload the api no longer vouches for (`FILE_UPLOAD_FAILED`) is put up again. A file is drawn as a name and a size; its link is asked from `POST /widget/download-url` only when the visitor opens it (one call per click, never per history message, so the 60/min throttle is not met) and followed as a download, never shown on the page. The rules `refuseUpload`, `maxBytesFor` and `UploadRefusals` moved to `upload-rules.ts` (re-exported by the same barrel) because they sat beside the zod schemas and importing them put the validation library in the bundle (51 KB gzip). An upload purpose is not added before the code that checks who may attach it: `product` with Step 4.1 and `order` with Step 4.3 (both need a `parentId` that belongs to the store, `TDD_07 §6.3`), `avatar` with Step 3.6 (the key has no store, `StorageKeys.avatar`, so the `confirmUpload` prefix check is by user there)
- [x] **Orphan uploads (PR B2, done):** `OrphanMediaCleaner` and `OrphanMediaScheduler` (`Schedules.CLEAN_ORPHAN_MEDIA`, hourly, one replica) delete the stray objects, requeue the scans that were lost (a finished job with the same id is removed first, or it would swallow the new one), drop a `pending` row whose file is gone once it is past `UNCONFIRMED_UPLOAD_TTL_HOURS`, and delete the file of an `infected` row. It lists `ORPHAN_LIST_PAGES_PER_RUN` pages per run and resumes from a cursor in Redis; the infected rows are looked at for `INFECTED_CLEANUP_WINDOW_HOURS` after their verdict. **Known limits:** a `pending` row whose scan fails for good is queued again every hour (a terminal state for it is a task of Step 3.5, with the notification of an unscannable file; until then 500 such rows can crowd out the rows behind them, the batch is oldest first), and the requester of an upload lives only in Redis (accepted: the member asks again). Speed of a full turn is a task of Step 7.3. The original task: a scheduled job in the worker deletes the objects under `stores/*/uploads/` and under `stores/*/messages/` with no `Media` row (a confirmation that died between the copy and the row leaves one at the final key; deleting it at the time could destroy the file of a concurrent confirmation of the same media) older than `UploadLimits.UNCONFIRMED_UPLOAD_TTL_HOURS` (the signed URL lets a member leave a file in the bucket and never confirm it), and the `pending` rows whose scan never ran, and the object of an `infected` row (the scan marks the row first and deletes the file second, so a failure in between leaves the file)
- [x] **A file an agent confirmed and never sent (OPS-R2-032, fix PR, rule 12):** the cleaner only removed objects without a `media` row, so a message file uploaded and confirmed but never sent stayed (row and objects) until the retention of the store. `OrphanMediaCleaner.dropUnsentMessageFiles` now deletes, once older than `UploadLimits.UNSENT_MESSAGE_FILE_TTL_HOURS` (48), a `message` row with no `message_id`, no `customer_id`, no `delivery_status` (sending sets all three in one transaction, so a sent file whose message or customer was deleted afterwards never matches) and an uploader (a customer's file is made with its message and never matches), in one `DELETE ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED ... RETURNING` so that a message linking the file at that moment wins; the objects (variants included, by `objectKeysOf`) go second and a failure is found by the stray-object sweep. **Known limits:** a file of a deleted message is left to the retention of the store; the other debts are in Step 7.3 ("Left by OPS-R2-032").
- [x] **Downloads never trust the name (PR B1, review finding of PR A):** the extension of `Media.filename` is the client's and may not match its declared type (`x.html` declared `image/png`). Every signed download sets `ResponseContentType` from `Media.contentType` and `ResponseContentDisposition: attachment` (inline only for the image variants, which are re-encoded WebP), so that nothing is ever served as active content by its extension
- [x] **Upload quota (PR B2, with the orphan cleanup; done):** 100 signed URLs per user and 300 per store per hour (`SIGNED_URLS_PER_USER_PER_HOUR`, `SIGNED_URLS_PER_STORE_PER_HOUR`), counted in Redis by hour, answered with 429 `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. `upload-url` records who asked (`CacheKeys.upload.requester`, `PENDING_UPLOAD_TTL_SECONDS`) and `confirm-upload` answers `FILE_UPLOAD_FAILED` to anyone else, also for a media that already exists; a Redis that lost the record makes the member ask again. The original task: `upload-url` persists nothing, so a member with `MEDIA_UPLOAD` can fill the bucket with files that are never confirmed until the cleanup runs. Add a per-store (and per-user) limit of signed URLs per hour in Redis, and `UploadLimits` constants for it. The same step persists who asked for each signed URL (a pending-upload record, or an HMAC in the `mediaId`) so that `confirm-upload` accepts only that user: today any member holding the ids could confirm another's upload and be recorded as its `uploadedBy`. **MED-15 (QA, 2026-11-07):** the hourly quota is the per-person cap of `POST /media/upload-url` (a per-minute one would be weaker than it, so none was added); its 429 now carries `retryAfterSeconds` (the seconds left of the hour). One batch of the multi-file composer (10 files) uses 10 of the 100 asks of the hour, so a person who sends more than ten such batches in an hour waits for the next one: raise `SIGNED_URLS_PER_USER_PER_HOUR` if real use shows it. The composer does not read `retryAfterSeconds` yet, so a person over the limit sees the generic message: a web task (draw the wait, as the team page does).
- [x] **Ad media fetched and stored (PR E4; debt of PR B2, which left it out):** `ConversationOrigin.mediaUrl` and `thumbnailUrl` are stored as links only, and nothing fetches them. Fetch them in a job of the heavy queue, store them as `Media` (scan and variants like any file) and draw them in the origin panel. The fetch is done by the core, not by a plugin, so it must call `assertPublicHttpsUrl` (`apps/worker/src/media/public-url.ts`), follow no redirect, and **pin the address it resolved** for the request (an agent with a fixed `lookup`), which closes the DNS change between the check and the call that B2 left open **Done in PR E4:** `Media.originId` and `originSlot` (migration `20261104120000_media_origin`, with its rollback; purpose `MediaPurpose.ORIGIN`; the row goes with its origin, `ON DELETE CASCADE`, and the orphan cleanup removes the object). `InboundMessageService.queueOriginFetches` queues one `FETCH_ORIGIN_MEDIA` job per slot (`OriginMediaSlots`: `thumbnail`, `media`) after the commit, only for an origin row the message created (the same ad again makes no row and no job), under the job id `fetch-origin-media-<origin id>-<slot>`; the job carries ids only and `OriginMediaFetcher` (`apps/worker/src/media`) reads the link from the row. The request is `pinnedHttpsGet`: `resolvePublicHttpsUrl` checks every address of the host, the socket is opened to the checked address through a fixed `lookup` (the certificate is still checked against the name of the link), no redirect is followed (3xx, 4xx are final; 429 and 5xx are retried), identity encoding, and the body is read with the size limit of an image (10 MB) and must declare an image type. The file is stored under the messages area of the bucket with a deterministic media id (`originMediaId`), `pending`, with no message and no customer (so the gallery and the media ZIP never see it), and queued to the scan and the variants like any file. `GET /conversations/:id/origins` carries `mediaFile` and `thumbnailFile` (`{ id, status }` for `pending` and `clean`; an infected file is left out, a file of another store is never matched); the card draws the signed link of the thumbnail (`GET /media/:id`), or the media when it is an image, and **never the address of the ad** (it expires and tells the ad's CDN who is looking), and the open conversation asks the origins again every 3 s while a picture of an origin under 5 minutes old is `pending`. Cases: `origin-media-fetcher.service.spec.ts`, `pinned-https-get.spec.ts`, `origin-picture.spec.ts`, two in `conversation-history.spec.ts`, two in `inbound.spec.ts` and one in `thread.spec.ts` (e2e). **Known limits (rule 12):** (1) a video of an ad is not fetched (it is the largest file that comes in and nothing draws it); the card shows the thumbnail, and a player is a task of Step 7.4 (visual polish); (2) origins recorded before this PR have no picture and are not backfilled here; the one-off script is the task "Backfill of ad pictures" of Step 7.3; (3) the pin covers the fetch the core makes; the fetch of a customer's file by a plugin (`mediaRef` as a link) keeps the address check of B2 and the plugin's own host list; (4) the file is held in memory while it is stored, as every fetch is (Step 7.3); (5) a picture that was dropped (refused type, unsafe link, 404) leaves no marker: the card has no picture, the origin keeps its title and body; (6) no event announces that the picture of an ad is ready, so the open conversation asks again every 3 s for 5 minutes after the origin was recorded (measured on the clock of the browser against the time of the message) and then waits for the next load: a `MEDIA_PROCESSED` for origin files, invalidating the origins, is a task of Step 3.5 (realtime and notifications). A generic `application/octet-stream` answer is accepted when the first bytes are an image; a link that fails its certificate or does not resolve is dropped without retry
- [x] **A customer file that could not be kept (PR E2b; debt of PR B2):** `InboundMediaFetcher` drops a file it refuses or cannot fetch and the message shows nothing. **Done in PR E2b (decision, rule 12):** the worker, and not `InboundMessageService`, records it when the job gives up: `UnavailableFileMarker` adds `{ index, code }` to `metadata.unavailableFiles` of the message (codes `MediaUnavailableCodes`: `refused`, `unsafe_link`, `fetch_failed`, `channel_cannot_fetch`; under the message row lock, because an album is several jobs on one row; one entry per place) and publishes `MEDIA_UNAVAILABLE`, which refreshes the open thread. Writing a "file expected" count when the fetch is queued was rejected: a file still being fetched would read as lost until the job ends, and the count adds nothing the give-up record does not say. A retryable failure is recorded only on the last attempt. `MessageView.unavailableFiles` carries the list (empty for a deleted message) and `MessageMedia` draws one line per entry, with a text for each code (en and es). The message type keeps its icon placeholder out of the way when a line is drawn

Routes `POST /notifications/push-subscription` and `POST /notifications/push-subscription/remove` (`@MemberOfStore()`, 204; a POST and not a DELETE with a body, which proxies drop). **Decisions of PR C1:** (1) the endpoint is a url the worker will call, so it is accepted only on the host of a known push service (`PushServiceHosts`, exact hosts and suffixes in `libs/core/domain/notifications/push-constants.ts`), never a host the caller names (SSRF); a browser on a push service that is not listed needs its host added there; (2) the keys of a registration must be base64url of 65 and 16 bytes (`isBase64UrlOfBytes`) and the VAPID pair of 65 and 32, so a bad key stops at the door and not as a retry storm; the wait for the queue is bounded by `PushLimits.ENQUEUE_TIMEOUT_MS`; `PushSubscription` belongs to the person and not to a store (no `storeId`, no RLS), so there is no `tenant-isolation.spec` case; the isolation of one person from another (a foreign endpoint is not removed, the same browser moves to the next person who registers it) is in `tests/api/notifications.spec.ts`; (3) at most `PushLimits.MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS_PER_USER` browsers per person, the least recently used dropped; `send` queues no job for a person with no browser registered; each push has a `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`; a refusal that will not pass (401, 403) is logged as an error; (4) a failure of the push service that may pass (429, 5xx, network) fails the job, which the queue retries 5 times; the retry repeats the push to the browsers that already got it, and the shared `tag` makes the device replace it instead of showing it twice; a failure that will not pass (400, 401, 403, 413) is logged and not retried; (5) a queue that is down loses the push and never the action that raised the notification (logged); (6) the keys travel with each call (`vapidDetails`), not through the global state of `web-push`, and `VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY` / `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY` are now required together (`env-schema`); without them the worker sends nothing and says nothing. **Left on purpose (owner: PR F):** registering is not one transaction (two registrations at once may leave one row over the cap until the next); an endpoint already registered by another person moves to the caller without proof (the endpoint is an unguessable url only that browser knows); a subscription the push service refuses for good (400, 401, 403, 413) is logged as an error and kept, with nothing that expires it (drop it after N failures, or by `lastUsed`); the VAPID keys are checked for format but not required in a deployed environment (decide with the deploy config of Step 8); each retry of a failed push repeats it to every browser (one job per browser would stop that); `send` reads the subscriptions once in the api and again in the worker; a push is sent to a person who was suspended in the store between the notification and the job (seconds, text of the notification only); nothing yet reads `lastUsed` to expire a subscription that is alive but never used

- [x] **Debts moved here from Step 3.4 (rule 12; owner: PR F4 of this step, in as many PRs as it needs):** (0) `POST /widget/messages` answers the ids of the media of the message, so the widget can open a file it just sent without waiting for the history; (1) the thread cannot send only the caption of a reply whose caption failed (`captionFailed`): it needs a column for the caption state, with the unscannable-file state above; (2) the thread cannot re-fetch a customer file that was lost (`unavailableFiles`; the dead-letter queue is the only way): keep the provider's media id in the message and add the button; (3) the caption call of Instagram and Messenger turns any failure into `captionFailed`, also a timeout after which Meta may have delivered the text, and the echo is then stored as a message of the owner: use the provider's idempotency for the second call; (4) and (5) are done in PR F4a: the gallery list carries the signed thumbnail link of each image and a tile downloads in the same tab, and the exports center filters by kind and state and draws a progress bar from `Export.progress` (the worker counts first and writes the percent at most every 1.5 s). **Known limits of F4a, left on purpose (owner: Step 7.3):** the list polls every 3 s while any row is pending and a row stuck pending polls for as long as the page is open (the worker gives it up after 24 h); a ZIP bar can stop short of 99 % when files are skipped; the `expired` filter uses an `OR` the index `(storeId, status, createdAt)` does not serve. **Done in PR F4b-1 of Step 3.5 (items (1) column and (3)):** `Message.captionState` (`CaptionState`: `sent`, `failed`, `unconfirmed`; null when the text travels with its file) replaces the `captionFailed` flag of the metadata (migration `20261109120000_message_caption_state` with rollback; old flags and caption ids are backfilled), and the view carries `captionState` instead of `captionFailed`. Meta documents no idempotency key on the Send API, so the second call of Instagram and Messenger cannot be made safe; the plugin now tells a refusal from a call that got no clear answer (`PluginError.outcomeUnknown`, set by `graphFailure` and `graphUnreachable` for a send that is not safe to repeat, and for a 2xx that does not parse): a refusal or throttle is `failed`, a timeout, 5xx, outage code or unreadable 2xx is `unconfirmed`, and the second message is never sent again by the platform. The echo of an `unconfirmed` caption settles it: `InboundMessageService.reconcileUnconfirmedCaption` matches an owner echo of type text with the same text to the oldest unconfirmed caption of the identity's conversations, writes its id and `sent`, and stores no new message. The thread says "may not have been sent, check the chat" for `unconfirmed`. **Decisions of PR F4b-1:** (1) reconcile by text and not by resending or by a time window: a resend risks a double text for the customer, and a match by text is the only link an echo with an unknown id offers; the cost is that an owner who types the very same text in the app while a caption is unconfirmed has that echo taken for it, which only hides a duplicate line, never loses a message; (2) `unconfirmed` is not timed out into `failed`, because no echo can mean "not delivered" or "not echoed" (the app may not subscribe to echoes); (3) the old `captionFailed` key is kept in the reserved metadata keys so a provider cannot draw it. The bubble draws the notice and the button "Send the text again" (`CaptionNotice`); the text of `captionFailed` no longer says to send the text as a new message. **Decisions of PR F4b-2:** (1) the outcome is read as the Meta plugin reads it: a `PluginError` without `outcomeUnknown` is a refusal (`failed`; retried only while it says `retryable` and attempts remain), any other error (timeout, network, 5xx, a 2xx that does not parse) is `unconfirmed` and is never repeated by the job, since Meta has no idempotency key; (2) the sweep never queues a caption again: a request still `queued` after two minutes ends `unconfirmed`, because a job that sent the text and could not write it down looks like a lost job and sending twice is worse than telling the agent to check the chat; the write of every outcome is retried `OutboundLimits.WRITE_ATTEMPTS` times before the job gives up, and `settleCaption` names the `version` of the request so a late job settles nothing; (3) resending from `unconfirmed` may show the text twice, which the agent chose after being told to check the chat, and an echo with the same text settles a caption that is `unconfirmed` or `queued` (a resent text whose echo comes before the worker writes it), within an hour of the reply or of the last request; (4) the request needs the messaging window open and a conversation that is not spam, like any text, but does not reopen a resolved conversation nor record a reply: it completes a reply already sent; (5) one request at a time per message: it is refused while an edit or a deletion is queued or when the file itself failed (that one is sent again whole), and a deletion or a whole resend is refused while the text is queued, because they settle through `changeRequestedAt` or would send the text twice; (6) the thread is refreshed with the existing `message.edited` event, which only invalidates the thread; (7) the route adds no resource, so it has no case of its own in `tests/security/tenant-isolation.spec.ts` (`validate:isolation` accepts only model names); a message of another store answers 404 and stays untouched in `tests/api/caption-resend.spec.ts`, and `route-protection.spec` finds the controller by name. **Left on purpose (owner: Step 7.3):** if the write of `sent` fails three times after the text went out, the sweep marks the message `unconfirmed` (the customer has the text; the thread says to check the chat); the worker does not check the messaging window again when the job runs, only the api when it is asked (a job is at most two minutes old before the sweep gives it up). **Review findings of PR F4b-2 left on purpose (hardening, owner: Step 7.3):** the sweep test asserts the global counts of `requeueStaleChanges` like the edit one does (use a store of its own); the queued notice reuses the warning icon; the echo test of a `queued` caption has no negative control for another text. **Done in PR F4c of Step 3.5 (item (2), a lost customer file downloaded again):** when the worker gives up on a file with `fetch_failed`, `UnavailableFileMarker.mark` now keeps in the entry of `unavailableFiles` where the file came from (`source`: plugin, connection, the provider's media id, type and name; `lostFileSourceSchema` in `libs/core/messaging/src/messages/lost-files.ts`), and the view says `canRetry` (never the source). `POST /messages/:id/files/:index/refetch` (`CONVERSATIONS_VIEW` + `MESSAGES_SEND`, `ApiRoutes.messages.refetchFile`, `MediaRefetchService`) queues the same `FETCH_INBOUND_MEDIA` job from that stored source under a new job id, and stamps `requestedAt` in the entry; the worker fetches as before and `marker.clear` removes the line when the file is stored. The line of the thread shows "Download it again" (`UnavailableItem`, `MessageActions.refetchFile`). **Decisions of PR F4c:** (1) the job is built on the server from what the worker kept; the request carries only the message and the place, so a caller can never name a URL or a provider id; (2) only the plain id of the provider's media is kept (`^[\w-]+$`, the same test the fetcher uses to tell an id from a link): a file named by a link (Instagram, Messenger) keeps no source, because a link is a credential that expires and an address the customer chose, and the fetch-media block of private addresses (`assertPublicHttpsUrl`) stays as the only gate for links; (3) only `fetch_failed` is retryable (`RefetchableUnavailableCodes`): `refused`, `unsafe_link` and `channel_cannot_fetch` give the same answer on every try; (4) one request every `MediaRefetchLimits.COOLDOWN_MS` (2 min) per file, answered 409 inside it, so a double click or a slow job cannot stack jobs (rejected: a new column or a `refetching` state, which would need a migration for a flag that the entry holds); (5) no new column and no migration: the source lives in the metadata, whose reserved key `unavailableFiles` a provider cannot write (`RESERVED_METADATA_KEYS`); (6) only a message of the customer that is not deleted; the messaging window is not needed (nothing is sent to the customer); (7) the route adds no resource, so it has no case in `tests/security/tenant-isolation.spec.ts`; a message of another store answers 404 and stays untouched in `tests/api/media-refetch.spec.ts`. (8) a refusal the provider will repeat (`retryable: false`) is recorded with no source, so it is not offered again; a code of a newer worker is drawn as the generic one but is never retryable; a new answer for a place already listed replaces its entry (a refetch that now fails as `refused` stops offering the button); the job is queued inside the transaction, so a queue that is down fails the request (503) and leaves no wait behind; a `requestedAt` that cannot be read counts as no wait. **Review of PR F4c (two security/correctness passes, 10 then 8 findings; the second was under 10):** fixed, the nine real ones above; accepted and left on purpose (owner: Step 7.3): `canRetry` stays true during the 2-minute wait (the api answers 409 and the thread shows a toast), no event tells another agent's open thread that a request started, the answer of the route has `replyTo: null`, there is no rate limit across files (a holder of `MESSAGES_SEND` can request many files, each one job on a queue of concurrency 2), the source (provider id, connection id, file name, all bounded) lives in the message metadata and reaches no view, and a future export or merge that serialises `metadata` must drop `unavailableFiles.source` (guarded since the PR that added `lost-file-source-readers.spec.ts`: it fails when a file outside its list reads the entry, so a new reader is reviewed on purpose, and `tests/api/lost-file-source.spec.ts` checks that the thread and the answer of asking for a file again carry no part of the source). **Tests/web lens of PR F4c (one pass, 10 findings; ranked ones fixed: marker branches, truncation, positive and owner cases of the action, queue down):** left for Step 7.3: no web component test of the button flow, no concurrent-request test, one mutation set per lost file in the media bundle (use a `useRefetchFile` hook of its own), a 409 shows the generic `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` toast, and an unreadable list makes `mark` log and skip (the thread then shows no line for a later file of the same album). **Known limits, left on purpose (owner: Step 7.3):** a file lost before this PR has no source and cannot be asked for again (the dead-letter queue is still its only way); WhatsApp keeps a media id for about 30 days, after which the request fails again and the line stays; a request whose connection was removed does nothing and the line stays; the thread shows a toast that the download was requested but no state of its own while the job works (the line disappears when the file is stored). **Done in PR F4d of Step 3.5 (item (0), the ids of the files a visitor just sent):** `POST /widget/messages` answers `{ received: true, mediaIds }`, the ids the files of the message will have, in the order of the upload ids (a repeated id counts once, a text-only message answers `[]`). No route, string or constant is new; the bundle stays at 30 KB gzip of 40. **Decisions of PR F4d:** (1) `Media.id` = the upload id, chosen by the api and not by the visitor (a random uuid of `requestUrl`, claimed once by one message), so the answer exposes nothing the visitor did not already hold; the upload staging key is not removed once the file is stored (the orphan cleanup handles it); a visitor who sends the same `clientMessageId` again with other uploads gets `mediaIds` for files the worker never stores (the message is already known), because the claim of an upload accepts the id of the message that holds it: the widget never does it, except after `FILE_UPLOAD_FAILED`, and the fix is to record the upload set of a `clientMessageId` and refuse a different one; no e2e case opens the file in the browser between the send and the scan. **Review of PR F4d (security/correctness pass, 7 findings, under the cap):** fixed, the worker honours a chosen id only for the web widget and only as a uuid, looks for an earlier attempt by id, store and message, refuses with no retry (`refused`, no source) an id that is already a file of something else, checking before it writes the blob, and the schema refuses two files with one id; left on purpose, `mediaIds` repeats the upload ids in the order the api deduplicated them (documented, the widget sends each once) and the resend limit above. **Tests/widget lens (one pass, 8 findings, under the cap):** fixed, a message without files no longer re-renders on `setMediaIds`, empty ids are refused, the retry path, the mixed ids of the schema and the isolation of the plugin check in the fetcher spec are tested; rejected as false positives, the 404 test depending on a worker (the suite captures the queue, no worker runs); left on purpose, the widget does not line up a de-duplicated answer with repeated uploads (it never sends one id twice).
- [x] **Assignment and expired-snooze notifications (QA fix PR Q1, 2026-11-03; the QA found that assigning a conversation notified nobody, against the "Done when" below):** `NotificationsEventsListener` hears `Events.CONVERSATION_ASSIGNED` and `Events.CONVERSATION_SNOOZE_EXPIRED` (new, bridged from the worker with ids only) and sends `NotificationTypes.CONVERSATION_ASSIGNED` and `CONVERSATION_SNOOZE_EXPIRED` to the assignee. **Decisions of Q1:** (1) the assignee is read from the row when the notification is made, not from the event, and must still be an active member who can open the conversation (`conversationReaders`, the rule of the mention); (2) nobody is told of an assignment they made to themselves; the system (a rule, the round robin) does tell; (3) a snooze that ran out on a conversation with no assignee tells nobody, because nothing records who snoozed it: the unassigned queue notification belongs to QA fix PR Q2; (4) `Events.CONVERSATION_SNOOZE_EXPIRED` is published only when the reason is `snooze_expired`, so a customer who writes to a snoozed conversation does not raise it.
- [x] **The rest of the notification types get an emitter (QA fix PR Q2, 2026-11-03; the QA found that nine types of the matrix were never raised):** `Events.CONVERSATION_REOPENED` (published by `applyStatus` for a resolved or archived conversation that becomes open; a snooze waking or a pending wait ending is not a reopening) and `Events.CONVERSATION_UNASSIGNED` (published by `RoutingService.apply` when routing ends with nobody) are new and bridged with ids only; `Events.MEMBER_JOINED` (published inside the transaction of accepting an invitation) is api only. `NotificationsEventsListener` gained `onReopened` and `onMessageReceived`; the new `NotificationsInboxListener` (`notifications-inbox.listener.ts`) raises the queue, `message.failed`, `member.joined`, `invitation.accepted` and `channel.disconnected`. `NotificationsService.sendToUsersOnce` skips who still has the same notification unread. Channels stay the defaults of the table (`NotificationDefaults`); none was changed. **Decisions of Q2 (rule 12):** (1) **Unassigned queue** (`conversation.unassigned_queue`, in-app only): told when routing leaves a conversation with nobody, when a person releases a conversation, when a snooze ends on one nobody owns, and when a person reopens one nobody owns; to the members who can see unassigned conversations and take them (`CONVERSATIONS_RESOLVE` or `CONVERSATIONS_ASSIGN`, the rule of `ConversationsService.assign`), except the person who caused it, and once per conversation until they open or read it (a queue that grows is one line per conversation, never one per message). Rejected: telling every member with `VIEW`, which rings for a Viewer who can do nothing about it. (2) **Reopened** (`conversation.reopened`, in-app and push): to the owner when a person (or the owner's phone, or an agent's reply) brings back a resolved or archived conversation, except when the owner did it themselves. A reopening caused by the customer's message is not announced here: the message is the news. Rejected: announcing both, which is the same alert twice. (3) **Message received** (`message.received`, in-app and sound): only to the owner of an open conversation, only for a message of the customer, and only once until they look (ten messages in a row are one line); also skipped while the owner has the assignment, the wake or the reopening of that conversation unread, since those already say it. A conversation nobody owns is the queue's news, never a message notification to everyone. Rejected: one per message. (4) **Message failed** (`message.failed`, in-app and push): to the person who wrote the reply if they can still open the conversation, else to its owner; the state is read from the row (a reply that went out on the second try is not told), once per message until read. (5) **New member and accepted invitation** (in-app): the person who invited gets `invitation.accepted`; the members who can invite (`TEAM_INVITE`) get `member.joined`; nobody is told twice or about themselves, and nobody who is not an active member. (6) **Channel disconnected** (`channel.disconnected`, in-app, push and email): only when the health check took it down (a person who disconnects knows), to the members with `SETTINGS_MANAGE_PLUGINS`, once per connection until read, and only while the row is still in error. (7) **The reason of a reopening by a reply**: `ConversationStatusReasons.AGENT_REPLIED` (`agent_replied`) is saved on the system line when an agent's reply, a resend, or a message the owner wrote from the phone brings a conversation back; the thread draws it ("an agent replied") and its text for a reopening by the system no longer says the customer replied ("Reopened automatically"). (8) **The email digest groups** the notifications of one store with the same kind, the same `actionPath` and the same parameters into one block with a count (`items[].count`; "N notifications like this"); the limit of 20 counts blocks and `moreCount` counts the notifications left out. Two conversations stay two blocks, each with its link. (9) **Dedup window:** a notification left unread holds back a new one of its kind for the same conversation for `NotificationLimits.DEDUP_WINDOW_MS` (1 hour) at most, so a person who never clears the bell hears again at most once an hour and never goes deaf; the window counts from the first row, it does not slide. (10) The check and the write of `sendToUsersOnce` are serialized per kind and resource inside one api process (a burst of messages is one line); two api instances publishing the same kind at the same moment may send one extra line. (11) If routing itself fails, `RoutingService.announceQueue` tells the team anyway, after checking the conversation is still nobody's. **Known limits (rule 12; the review of Q2 raised them, they are decisions and not bugs):** a customer who keeps writing to a conversation nobody owns does not raise a new line once the queue line was read and the hour passed: the queue line is the news of the conversation, not of each message (rejected: a message line for every taker, which is the noise this PR removes); an owner's reply from the phone that reopens a conversation of an agent tells that agent, because the platform cannot tell which person the phone belongs to; a notification group of the email digest whose type has no text is left out as before, and the rows stay in the center; `CONVERSATION_REOPENED` is published for every reopening and each listener decides, so a new reason added later must be considered in both `onReopened` handlers. **Not done, written in the QA backlog below:** `plugin.error` has no source in v1.2. _Amended 2026-11-08: the queue and the message now push by default (see the entry below)._

Removing a suspended member works. (3) **Effect at once:** `TenantContextService.access()` tells `granted`, `suspended` and `none` apart (the cache entry is one of them; `resolve()` still answers only a grant, so a caller that did not change fails closed); `TenantGuard` answers 403 `TENANT_MEMBER_SUSPENDED` and audits the denial with `reason: 'suspended'`, a stranger still gets `TENANT_ACCESS_DENIED`; the member's cache entry is dropped after the commit, so an access token still valid is refused on the next request. ## Milestone 4 — Commerce

Inventory is robust from the first release (`TDD_16_Inventory.md`): warehouses that serve
several stores, a movement ledger, reservations, transfers between warehouses and physical
counts. Orders depend on it, so it is built first.

- [ ] **Before Milestone 4 starts (QA round 2, 2026-11-06, rule 12):** run the full round of the case matrix (416 cases, `qa-reportes-2026-11-05/matriz-casos.md`) with `/qa-team`. Round 2 covered what was built up to #190 and the connection UX; Milestone 4 adds orders and inventory on top, so the matrix is run complete first, and the P1/P2 it finds are fixed before the first Step of this milestone.

Order: an exact sku, then names or skus that start with the text, then the rest, then by name. A product that matched by itself (its name or its sku) comes with `matchedVariant: null`; the variant is named only when it is the reason the product is in the answer, and among several the one whose sku is the text comes first. ### Step 4.2 — Warehouses and stock
- [x] `Warehouse`, `StoreWarehouse`, `InventoryLevel`, `OrderItemAllocation` models, the changes to `InventoryMovement` and `StoreSettings`, and the raw-SQL constraints and partial uniques of `TDD_16 §2` (with rollback). **Built in PR A1** (migration `20261121100000_inventory_schema`, one additive migration with its rollback, tried twice on a copy; `StockTransfer` and `StockCount` come with Steps 4.5 and 4.6). Beyond `TDD_16 §2`, decided under rule 12: (a) **the tenancy is a rule of the database:** `store_warehouses` names the organization twice (composite foreign keys `(organization_id, store_id)` and `(organization_id, warehouse_id)`), so a store can never be linked to a warehouse of another organization; `inventory_levels` and `inventory_movements` reference `products(store_id, id)`, so stock can never name a product of another store; and one trigger (`check_stock_row_belongs_together`) on levels, movements and allocations refuses a warehouse that is not of the store's organization (a level is not a link: a store may keep stock in a warehouse it was unlinked from, `TDD_16 §4.7`), a variant that is not a variant of the row's product, and an allocation of an order line of another store; (b) **the ledger is append-only in the database:** `platform_app` and `platform_worker` have no UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE on `inventory_movements` (as with `audit_logs`; the security suite checks the privileges, so a later `GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES` fails the build), and nothing deletes it by cascade: a store or a warehouse with stock cannot be deleted (`TDD_16 §4.9`, the foreign keys restrict it); the idempotency key is unique **inside a store** (`(store_id, idempotency_key)`), not across the platform, so tenants never share a namespace; warehouse codes are unique ignoring case (`uq_warehouses_code_lower`) and a code or a name has no stray spaces and keeps the lengths of `InventoryLimits`; (c) `InventoryLevel.valueCents` (BigInt, USD cents) holds what the units on hand are worth at their cost: the weighted average is `valueCents / onHand`, kept by `InventoryService` in the same transaction as the level (PR A2), and FIFO lots can later be built from the receipts (`unitCostCents` of the movement) with no change to either table; (d) variants and products are never deleted or turned into the product by a delete while stock refers to them (`ON DELETE RESTRICT`), and `ProductsService` answers 409 `has_history` with the count `inventoryLevels` for a product or variant that has a level, even at zero; (e) CHECKs: `reserved >= 0`, movement quantity `> 0`, cost and reserved-after `>= 0`, allocation quantity `> 0`, priority `>= 1`, default threshold `>= 0`; (f) the migration locks `inventory_movements` and REFUSES to run if it has rows (nothing wrote to it before this step), instead of inventing a warehouse for them; its rollback is destructive (it drops the stock tables), and says so
- [x] Check that the inventory constants born in Step 0.3 cover `TDD_16 §3`; add what is missing. **Done in PR A1:** every entry of the table of `TDD_16 §3` exists (permissions and role presets, events, audit actions, error codes, notification types, job, schedule, metric, routes, paths, query keys, scopes). Added: `PRODUCTS_VIEW_COST` (below), `InventoryMovementEffects` (what each type does to `onHand` and `reserved`, read by the engine, the kardex and the reconciliation), `InventoryMovementsThatBringUnitsIn` (the types that carry a unit cost), `InventoryManualMovements`, `InventoryLimits`, `DefaultWarehouse`, `FIRST_WAREHOUSE_PRIORITY`, `ProductHistoryTables.INVENTORY_LEVELS`
- [x] **Unit cost on every stock movement (finance requirements of 2026-11-10, `project_finance_module_requirements`):** `InventoryMovement` gets `unitCostCents` (whole USD cents, null when the movement has no cost, e.g. a reserve), written by receipts, returns and opening stock, so that a weighted-average cost is computed from movements now and FIFO lots can be added later without migrating data. **The column and `InventoryLevel.valueCents` are in PR A1; writing and using them is `InventoryService` (PR A2).** `Product.costCents` / `ProductVariant.costCents` (Step 4.1) are only the reference cost that prefills a receipt; they never override the cost a movement carries **Closed in PR A2** (the service writes and averages the cost, and refuses a cost-less receipt where it is needed).
- [x] `InventoryService`: transactional, idempotent movements (row lock, `onHandAfter`/`reservedAfter`), reserve/release/issue/restock, manual adjustments with mandatory reason, low-stock alert, kardex. **Built in PR A2** (`libs/core/inventory`, `@platform/core/inventory`; routes in `apps/api/src/modules/inventory`): `move`, `moveMany` (sorted by warehouse, product, variant so two orders never deadlock) and `reserve`/`release`/`issue`/`restock`, each taking the caller's transaction when it has one. The pure rules of a movement are in `movement-math.ts` (coverage threshold 90%). A key is serialized per store (advisory lock), the level row is created and locked (`FOR UPDATE`), the rules run, level and ledger change together and `inventory.moved` leaves after the commit; the same key with the same request answers the original (`replayed`), with another request it is 409 `idempotency_key_reused`. Rules decided here (rule 12): a movement that **adds** stock or **reserves** needs a warehouse that is linked to the store and on (`INVENTORY_WAREHOUSE_NOT_LINKED`, `INVENTORY_WAREHOUSE_INACTIVE`), one that takes stock out does not (what is stranded in an unlinked warehouse can still be written off); a product with `trackInventory` off is `INVENTORY_PRODUCT_NOT_TRACKED` for what adds stock or promises it, while what it still holds can be released, shipped or written off; release or issue beyond what is reserved is `INVENTORY_RESERVATION_EXCEEDED` even with negative stock on; `TRANSFER_OUT` always needs real available stock; a receipt with a cost fixes it, units that leave take the average of the level and record it (`valueCents / onHand`, rounded half up, the last unit empties the value), units that come in with no cost take the current average, and a deficit is covered before any unit carries value. **Routes** (`GET /inventory/levels` with `warehouseId`, `productId`, `variantId` and `lowStock`; `GET /inventory/movements`; `GET /inventory/kardex` for one item in one warehouse; `GET /products/:id/inventory`; `POST /inventory/adjustments`, 201 and 200 for a retry): `inventory:view` reads, `inventory:adjust` writes, the cost fields come only with `products:view_cost`, every adjustment is audited once (`INVENTORY_ADJUSTED`)
- [x] Warehouses CRUD and store links with priority (organization-scoped, `ORG_MANAGE_WAREHOUSES`). **Built in PR B** (`apps/api/src/modules/warehouses`): `GET/POST /warehouses`, `GET/PATCH /warehouses/:id`, `PUT /warehouses/:id/stores`. The organization is the one `TenantGuard` resolved from `X-Store-Id` (never the body), reading asks `inventory:view`, writing `org:manage_warehouses`. Decided under rule 12: (a) **no DELETE route** (`TDD_16 §6` lists none): a warehouse is switched off with `PATCH {active:false}`, refused with `INVENTORY_WAREHOUSE_HAS_STOCK` (`metadata.reason = deactivate`) while any level of any store of the organization has units on hand, reserved or a negative balance (the TDD says `onHand > 0`; reserved and negative are held to the same rule because a warehouse that still owes or owns units is not empty), and its stock is read, never written, by this module; (b) the code is ASCII `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,19}`, kept as typed, unique per organization ignoring letter case (`409 RESOURCE_ALREADY_EXISTS`, `metadata.conflict = code_in_use`), also under two requests at once (the unique index of the migration decides); (c) **`PUT /warehouses/:id/stores` takes the complete list** `{ stores: [{ storeId, priority? }] }`: a store left out is unlinked (refused, with nothing changed, when that store has units reserved there, `metadata.reason = unlink`, `TDD_16 §4.7`), a priority puts the warehouse at that place of the store's list and shifts the others, one without keeps its place (a new link goes to the end), and every touched store is renumbered `1..n` in the same transaction (the unique `(store, priority)` is DEFERRABLE), so a reorder is one call and two requests on the same store take turns (advisory lock per store, taken in sorted order); a store of another organization, or one that does not exist, is the same 404 and writes nothing; a switched-off warehouse takes no new link (`409`, `conflict = inactive`) but may lose them; (d) an organization holds at most `WarehouseLimits.MAX_PER_ORGANIZATION` (200) warehouses, checked under an organization lock; (e) every list is a cursor page oldest first, and every change is audited (`WAREHOUSE_CREATED`, `WAREHOUSE_UPDATED` with the fields and the before/after of name, code and active, or `change: 'stores'` with what was added, removed and the final order)

It leaves out `ORDER_SUMMARY` too (`conversations.views.ts`, covered in `tests/api/conversations.spec.ts`), and an order line cannot be reacted to (`agent-reactions.service.ts`). Any new query that reads "the last message" must leave the lines of the platform out. (g) The line of an order and the lists draw money with `formatCents` (US dollars) and ignore the `currency` of the line: the same limit as debt (b) of C1. **Owner: Step 7.3.**

(b) **closing needs sight of every short line**: a caller who does not see a short line of another store gets `INVENTORY_TRANSFER_LINES_OUT_OF_REACH` and the transfer waits for someone who does (the owner belongs to every store); (c) **cancelling in transit returns the units that have not arrived**, not "the dispatched quantity" of `TDD_16 §4.5` when a part was already received (returning it too would make stock out of nothing); (d) a transfer in transit needs its destination switched on and the store of each line linked to it (`TRANSFER_IN` is refused otherwise): switching a warehouse off, or unlinking a store from it, is refused with `INVENTORY_WAREHOUSE_HAS_STOCK` (`reason: open_transfer`) while a transfer in transit leaves from or arrives at it; **Step 4.7** shows that refusal in words; (e) the web draws nothing yet: **Step 4.7** draws the routes (`scripts/frontend-coverage-map.ts` already points there), the counts of `transferLines` in the refusal to delete a product or a variant (`metadata.transferLines`, the catalog screen shows the generic refusal until then) and the transfer pages of `/org/transfers`; (f) the notification of `transfer.dispatched` goes to the members with `inventory:receive_transfers` of each store whose lines travel, and links to `/org/transfers` (the detail page is 4.7); (g) `libs/core/inventory` has a coverage threshold on the pure rules of movements and transfers (`transfer-rules.ts`); `TransfersService` is covered by `tests/api/transfers.spec.ts` against the real database

- [x] **QA fix PR 1 (QA of 4.8 to 4.14, 2026-11-12; rule 12 decisions):** (a) **a failed attempt set by hand twice with the same `occurredAt` counts once** (`ShippingService.setManualStatus` finds the twin by status and moment, as the carrier engine does, and answers 200 with the shipment unchanged; a request with no `occurredAt` is its own moment and counts, as before). (b) **Past `maxDeliveryAttempts` nothing happens on purpose:** `failedAttempts` keeps counting, the status stays `failed_attempt` and the team is told at each attempt; the carrier, not a counter of ours, decides when the package goes back, and an automatic return would move stock and money on a guess. Rejected alternative: a warning notification at `failedAttempts >= maxDeliveryAttempts`, which needs a notification type and an emitter and belongs with the carrier's own "returning" status (Step 4.15 re-QA decides whether it is wanted). (c) **The order detail does not offer "Mark as shipped" or "Deliver" while a guide is live** (`offeredFlows(..., hasActiveGuide)`), the same rule as the api (`ORDER_STATUS_DRIVEN_BY_SHIPMENT`: shipped and delivered only; "Start preparing", "Return" and "Cancel" stay, because the api lets them through). It fails closed while the guides load; a member without `shipping:view` is left to the api. (d) **Carrier fee range at guide time needed no code:** `TDD_17 §4.13` says the range of the connection that carries the guide decides *unless the caller holds `ORDERS_OVERRIDE_PRICE`*, and the QA ran as Admin, who holds it (the case without the permission is covered in `tests/api/shipments.spec.ts`, "the fee range of the carrier"); the TDD "As built" paragraph now says so. (e) **Known limits, accepted (review findings, rule 12):** the repeat is recognised only while the shipment still has that status (a retry that arrives after the shipment moved on meets the transition table, as any late request does) and only against a hand-made event (a carrier's event at the same moment is another event); a repeat leaves no audit line. The detail hides shipped and delivered while the guides are unknown or their query failed, with no retry hint: the api would accept the move, so the member waits for the guides or reloads; a server flag `statusDrivenByShipment` on the order would remove the duplicated rule and is left to Step 7.4 (UI pass) if the drift ever shows.

(b) **A guide prefix that is taken answers `SHIPPING_GUIDE_PREFIX_TAKEN`** (409, with its own text in `en` and `es`) instead of the generic `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, both when another courier holds it and when it is printed on guides of another one. (c) **Lines in two warehouses with no `originWarehouseId` answer `SHIPPING_ORIGIN_AMBIGUOUS`** (400, text that says to choose the warehouse); `SHIPPING_ORIGIN_MISSING` stays for a store with no origin, a warehouse with no address and a warehouse that holds none of the lines. (d) **`POST /orders/:id/shipments` for an order that does not exist or is of another store answers 404** (`createShipments` judges the order before the carrier). (e) **An order with nothing to pay collects nothing** (`prepareGuide`: `collects` also needs `totalCents > 0`), so a cash-on-delivery order whose credit covered all of it gets a guide from a carrier that cannot collect cash, and the guide carries no amount to collect. The payment of the replacement is **not** born `COMPLETED` (rejected, review finding: it locks the order against edits of lines, fee and carrier, turns into a `REFUNDED` payment if the replacement is returned, and leaves no payment event or audit line); it stays `PENDING` until the carrier's cash on delivery or the agent records it. The screen that shows what the carrier collects (`order-guide-form.ts`) follows the same rule in the PR 2b. Decisions that changed no code: (f) `local` has no webhook secret and no credentials, and `POST /carriers/:id/webhook-secret` answers 409 for it (already covered by `carrier-status-mappings.spec.ts`); the checklist was out of date. (g) The order of validation stays: the cheap checks (room, repeated name) answer before the carrier is asked to make an account, and a carrier that refuses answers `{ reason }` of a closed list and never names a field, because the words of a carrier never leave the server; rejected alternative: naming the field, which needs every plugin to declare its fields and would hand out what the carrier said. (h) **The credit of an exchange stays capped at the value of the replacement:** the excess is written in the audit entry (`excessCents`) for the owner to settle by hand, as the approval already did; rejected alternative: refund it or keep it as store credit, which moves money without a human and needs a store-credit model that belongs to the finance module. The screens of this group (importer that offers disconnected carriers, message of an amount that is not a number, the caution box of the scanner editor) are the QA fix PR 2b.

The editor ticks the box on the change to a refusal (only from a package that was not one, as the server) and goes back to the saved flag when the reason leaves the refusal; an unticked box is sent out loud (`flagCustomer: false`), because a body without the key would be ticked by the server. The audit entries of the order (`order.cancelled`, `order.updated`) name the guides voided with it (`shipmentsVoided`, and `guideChanges` for an edit). Decisions: **(a)** an edit voids the guide and does **not** make the new one: a guide may cost money, so it stays a person's click (rejected: an automatic recreate, which would spend without a click, `TDD_17 §4.10`); - [x] **Built in PR D3 (split orders in a bulk run; closes (e) of PR D1; rule 12 debts with their owners):** the bulk run (`BulkLabelsRunner`) no longer treats an order as one guide. An order is made of **parts**, one per warehouse its lines are allocated to (`OrderItemAllocation`, read at the start of the run and ordered by the priority of the warehouse in the store, then by id, so the order of the guides never changes between runs) and one for every live guide whose warehouse the allocation no longer names; an order with no allocation and no guide is one part with no origin and the engine picks the warehouse of the store, as before (`partsOfOrder`, pure, in `bulk-labels.rules.ts`). Each part is judged on its own: a part whose guide can be printed is reused (nobody is called), one whose guide cannot yet (`creating`, `requires_review`, `cancel_pending`, `cancel_failed`) is skipped with `SHIPPING_ACTIVE_SHIPMENT_EXISTS`, and a part with no live guide gets a request for **that warehouse** (`originWarehouseId` of `ShipmentRequest`, always the warehouse the run judged, so the engine refuses it if the order no longer ships from there), so a guide that was voided (`CANCELLED`) is made again and its label is never merged. The requests of one order go together: one after another in a standalone or internal lane (the amount to collect of each guide is read after the guides before it, so the parts add up to the total exactly as `TDD_17 §4.4` says, and a lane's concurrency counts orders, not parts) and in the same call of a pickup-bound lane (the engine writes them in that order inside one transaction). The account still has **one entry per order**, so `succeeded + failed = total` holds: `PartsLedger` keeps what each part came to and gives the order once, when the last part has settled (`entryOfParts`): a split order is `created` (some guide made by the run) or `reused` (none) only when every part has its label, and carries `shipmentIds`, the guides whose labels are pages of the file in the order of the parts, with `shipmentId` the first of them; otherwise it says what its first part without a label says (`skipped` or `failed`, with its `errorCode` and the `shipmentId` of that part) and **still lists the labels the other parts have in `shipmentIds`, which are printed** (a guide that exists is never left out of the file because its sibling failed). The file puts the labels of a split order together, in the order of the selection and, inside the order, of the parts; a label that cannot go in the file (`not_ready`, `too_large`, ...) turns its order into `failed` with that `reason`. An order that is not split has no `shipmentIds`: the shape of PR D1 is unchanged for it. "Print labels" (`POST /shipments/labels/merge`) takes shipment ids, so it already prints every label of a split order when the screen sends them all; `tests/api/shipments-bulk.spec.ts` has a case for it. Decisions: **(a)** one entry per order with a list of guides, not one entry per guide (rejected: it would break `succeeded + failed = total`, which the table demands, and a run of a hundred orders would report two hundred lines the agent did not select); **(b)** a split order whose part failed is a failure of the order even though a label is printed (rejected: counting it as a success, which would hide the guide that is missing: the agent must see that a part is still to be made); **(c)** the parts of an order are made one after another and not in parallel, even for a carrier that takes three at a time (rejected: parallel parts, whose amounts to collect would depend on which one the database sees first). **Left, each with its owner:** **(d)** a split order whose part made its guide and whose sibling failed keeps no mark that the run paid for the first one: a later attempt of the same run reports it as `reused`, not `created` (nobody is called twice either way; the report of what the run spent is exact only for orders that ended whole, and a split order that lost a part reads `skipped` or `failed` even when the run made another of its guides: the guide is in `shipmentIds`, printed and on the account): **Step 4.14** if the screen needs the figure per guide, and a fault that stops the run keeps the guides its finished parts made (`PartsLedger.unfinished`) as a `failed` entry with `INTERNAL_ERROR`; **(e)** the entry names only the first part that failed, so an order with two failed parts shows one error: the agent reads the rest in the shipments of the order, and the screen that lists them per guide is **Step 4.14**; **(f)** the parts are read from the allocation when the run starts, so an allocation that changes while the run is under way (a line moved to another warehouse) is judged at the next run: accepted, the engine re-checks the origin inside its own transaction and refuses a warehouse the order no longer ships from (`SHIPPING_ORIGIN_MISSING`); **(h)** a live guide whose warehouse the allocation does not name (the lines moved after the guide was made; the database never lets a guide change its origin) stands for the first warehouse of the order that has no guide, one by one, so the run never pays a second guide for what the order already shipped; the cost is that a stale guide may cover a warehouse that is not really the one it left from, and the agent sees it in the shipments of the order: **Step 4.14**; **(i)** the origins of an order are computed twice, in `prepareGuide` (the engine) and in `BulkLabelsRunner.originsOf`, from the same rows: one shared helper is **Step 7.1** with the other duplicated helpers; a request list longer than the hundred the engine takes (a split order sends more than one request) goes in runs of a hundred; a part that makes the engine throw stops the parts after it, as a single guide did before; **(g)** the `shipments` list of an order that the bulk dialog shows per guide, and the "print all labels of this order" button that sends every shipment id of the order, are **Step 4.14**; asking the carrier again for a label that was not kept (debt (i) of PR D1, (g) of PR C1) stays in **Step 4.15**.

releases the stock once and is refused after pickup.

### Step 4.11 — Pickups
- [x] (PR A; the auto-request time and the reminder are read by PR B) Per-connection pickup rules (days, cutoff, auto-request time, reminder) and `PickupsService.ensurePickup` (the core service of `libs/core/shipping`, not a method of `ShippingService`) with the advisory lock and the one-open-pickup-per-day rule for standalone carriers (a service rule, not a database index, because a pickup-bound carrier may need several per day)
