**Ledger hardening B (migration `20270116100000_finance_ledger_hardening_b`, LED-516 and LED-R2-040, rule 12):** (1) the application roles lose `UPDATE (accounting_start_date, country_code, base_currency)` of `finance_settings` (the setup only creates them; a correction goes through the migration role); `recognize_sale_on` keeps its grant (PATCH /finance/settings); (2) `platform_app` loses `UPDATE (resolved_at)` of `finance_chain_incidents` and only the worker (the weekly job) closes an incident; the auditor's check in the API passes `resolve: false` and reports STILL_OPEN until the job runs; (3) a trigger makes `resolved_at` write-once for the application roles (the owner can correct), and a close is dated no earlier than the detection (the database clamps it, so clock skew never refuses the close). Rejected: a trigger alone (a taken-over application can lie to it). **Debt (Step 7.3):** (a) an incident opened by an API check that was a false alarm (a head that moved during the walk) stays open until the weekly job runs and blocks the close of a month meanwhile: needs a distinct outcome (`pending_close`) and an on-demand run of the job; (b) a taken-over worker can still close an incident; a dedicated verification role that re-runs the TypeScript verifier would close that.
**Decisions of PR 4B.3b (rule 12):** (1) an edit that moves the price recomputes the tax of the order with the rate each kept line was made at, the price mode the
order was made in, the rate of an unchanged shipping fee, and the rounding it was made with (`orders.tax_rounding`, kept by the QA fix PR `small-fixes-qa`, TAX-586: an order made before that column takes today's rounding); a line the edit adds takes today's rate (rejected: freezing every line's
tax cents, which the share of a changed discount makes impossible); (2) an order made before the tax columns is never given a snapshot by an edit (its
total stays the price alone); (3) the report reads the sale day in the store's time zone from `deliveredAt` (or `shippedAt` when `recognizeSaleOn` is `shipped`),
excludes cancelled orders and counts the orders with no snapshot apart (`ordersWithoutTaxSnapshot`) without estimating them; (4) the output base is
rebuilt from the order (the discount share is deterministic, `allocateByWeight`), not stored, so net + tax of the lines adds up to what the customer paid;
(5) the CSV is served by the report route itself (`FINANCE_VIEW`, the cells through the shared CSV writer) and not through `GENERATE_EXPORT`, because it holds
no customer data (rejected: the audited export job, which is the journal's); (6) the preference is written only by `PreferencesService` (the contract of the
cache writers), called by the tax settings route.
**Debts of PR 4B.3b (tracked where they are closed):** (a) the VAT of returns and of refunds (E8) is not in the report: 4B.6 posts it and the report then reads
it, until then a returned order counts as a sale; (b) the report is a read of orders and lines for a range of at most 366 days, in pages of 500: if it is slow at
the owner's volume, 4B.8 moves it to a table kept by the posting (`TDD_18 §10`); (c) the CSV moves to `GENERATE_EXPORT` with `FINANCE_EXPORTED` audit in 4B.8,
which owns the exports; (d) the order screens of the web draw the tax in 4B.9 (the types are in `libs/api-client`).
**Decisions of PR 4B.3a (rule 12):** (1) the tax of a line is computed on the line after its share of the discount (largest remainder, by gross
amount), and the order tax is the sum of the lines and of the shipping fee, so the order, the entry and the document agree to the cent; a stray
cent therefore does not arise in the order, and `ROUNDING` stays for what a remittance or a carrier rounds otherwise (4B.6) (rejected: the tax of the
sum, which the document cannot reproduce); (2) the rounding is a setting of the books (`half_up`, `half_even`, `down`, `up`), `half_up` by default
as `TDD_18 §7` says; (3) `shippingTaxed` is a setting of the books (default true), and the rate the shipping fee was taxed at is kept on the order
(`shippingTaxRateBps`, a column `TDD_18 §7` did not list) so the VAT report can group it by rate (rejected: deriving it from the default rate of today);
(4) an order item also keeps its treatment (`taxTreatment`), because exempt and not subject sales go to different lines of the legal books
**[ACCOUNTANT]**; (5) the tax treatment and the rate of a product need `finance:manage_accounts` on top of `products:edit`, and
`pricesIncludeTax` is written by its own finance route, because both decide what a customer pays and what the books owe (rejected: the
permission of the preferences, which is not the accountant's); (6) the database, not only the service, refuses a product that names the rate of
another organization (a trigger: the keys cannot say it, a product has a store and not an organization), a rate above 100 %, two defaults and a
switched-off default; (7) the default rate and a rate an active product names are not switched off; a rate that was changed moves the orders made
after it, never one that exists; (8) a store with no books (the organization has no finance settings) keeps its orders as they are, with no tax
snapshot (decided here, built in 4B.3b); (9) the 13 % rate is seeded by the SV template and by the migration for the organizations already
set up, and both are editable data.
**Debts of PR 4B.3a (tracked where they are closed):** (a) the web client of the rates, the store tax setting and the tax fields of the product
form is Step 4B.9's (the product form does not send them); a person with `products:edit` and without `finance:view` cannot list the rates
there, which 4B.9 settles; (b) the VAT of returns (E8) is posted and reported by 4B.6, which owns the return entries: 4B.3b's report counts
the sales and says so; (c) the sales book layout, the exempt categories, whether the shipping fee carries VAT, the withholdings and the
perceptions stay **[ACCOUNTANT]** (`TDD_18 §13` rows 2 and 4): configurable here, owner's pending; (d) `FINANCE_TAX_RATE_NOT_CONFIGURED` and the
order fields were 4B.3b's (done); (e) `assertMayWriteTax` refuses a product request that names the tax fields even with the value the product has,
so a client that echoes the whole product needs `finance:manage_accounts`: the web form of 4B.9 sends them only when they change; the preferences column is written only by `PreferencesService` (the contract `cache-writers`), which the tax settings route calls.
**Owner decision (2026-11-15, recorded here by 4B.3a):** `TDD_18` is approved as written. Payroll is a separate module, **Milestone 4C** (not
scheduled in this plan yet; `TDD_18 §14` already keeps it out of 4B); until it exists, salaries enter the books as one manual entry per month
(`finance:post_manual`, E13), on the `Planilla` expense account of the SV chart.
**TDD:** `TDD_18 §7`, `TDD_17 §4.13`, `TDD_16`
**Done when:** an order computes and stores its tax exactly to the cent in both pricing modes and the VAT report adds up to the
orders of a period.

### Step 4B.4 — Expenses, incomes, transfers and bank reconciliation (api)
Split in three PRs, never stacked (each starts from a `main` that has the one before): **4B.4a** the transactions, **4B.4b-1** the
receipts, **4B.4b-2** the bank reconciliation (4B.4b was one PR in the first plan and went past the size a review can hold: it carries a
migration with triggers, a parser of customer files, a matcher and the routes of both). Both use the upload purpose `finance_document`,
built once, by 4B.4b-1.
- [x] **4B.4a:** `FinanceTransaction` (expense, income, transfer) posting E12 through `LedgerService` in the same transaction; void = the
      reversing entry; change = void plus a new one in one request (`replacesTransactionId`); the tax inside the amount computed by the
      server from the rate (creditable input VAT only when the person says the document is valid, [ACCOUNTANT]); permissions
      `FINANCE_MANAGE_TRANSACTIONS` (expense, income) and `FINANCE_MOVE_MONEY` (transfer), narrowed by the kind
- [x] **4B.4b-1:** receipts as `finance_document` media (upload purpose with the parent check on the transaction, scanned, `documentMediaId`
      on the transaction, a column added by its migration, set once by `POST finance/transactions/:id/document`, signed links by the GET of
      the same path)
- [x] **4B.4b-2:** permission `FINANCE_RECONCILE` (already in `Permissions`, held by the Admin preset) on the routes of the reconciliation
- [x] **4B.4b-2:** bank import: `BankImportProfile`, `BankStatementImport`, `BankStatementLine`, `ReconciliationMatch`; deterministic matching,
      strict parsing, no formula evaluation, the file kept as media; suggestions, confirm one or all the exact; "register it" from an
      unmatched line (a prefilled transaction of 4B.4a); the balance-versus-statement difference
- [x] **4B.4a tests:** each kind posts the right entry, a transfer needs two distinct cash-kind accounts, voiding, changing, the closed
      period, retries and races, the permission of each kind, isolation cases, the shape and the immutability held by the database
- [x] **4B.4b-1 tests:** the upload of a receipt (permissions, parent of another organization, type and size), attaching it (once, replay,
      kind narrowing, voided, a file of another organization or purpose), the signed links (clean, pending, other store, other
      organization), the trigger whoever writes, and the isolation of the receipt (no new table: `validate:isolation` keys its cases by model, so the proof is in `tests/api/finance-transaction-documents.spec.ts`: a file of another organization is never attached, a transaction of another organization is a 404 to attach to or to read the receipt of)
- [x] **4B.4b-1, active content in a receipt PDF (PR `fix/finance-document-active-pdf`, QA finding TAX-436):** the worker's scan of a `finance_document`
      PDF now looks, before it can be `clean`, for the names `/JavaScript`, `/JS`, `/Launch`, `/SubmitForm`, `/ImportData`, `/GoToR` and `/RichMedia` IN THE CLEAR
      (`apps/worker/src/media/pdf-active-content.ts`, `findActivePdfNames`): one linear pass over the bytes of a file already limited to 10 MB, `#xx` escapes in
      names decoded, longer names such as `/JSON` not taken for them. `/OpenAction` and `/AA` are not on the list because they carry an action and the action
      is what is named (`/S /JavaScript`); an `/OpenAction` with a destination (`[3 0 R /Fit]`, what Word, LaTeX and Acrobat write) is not refused. A hit ends
      the row as `unscannable` with `scanResult.reason = pdf_active_content` and the names, and keeps the file unserved in the bucket as a quarantine (financial
      evidence is never deleted); attaching it answers 409 `transaction_document_refused` (a refused PDF never becomes clean; the other not-clean states keep
      `transaction_document_not_clean`). A finance document has no thread, so nobody is told by an event: the row and a WARN log are the trace.
      **Decision (rule 12, three rounds of independent security review):** the first versions parsed or inflated the PDF (a byte reader, then `pdf-lib`) and each
      round found a new way round it (a NUL before `stream`, a decoy object stream, an object stream without `/Type`, a parser that takes the last of two
      objects with the same number where the reader takes the one the cross reference points to) and one way to exhaust the worker (a 1.4 MB file that inflates
      to 1.5 GB). A detector that parses with anything but the reader's own parser loses the differential, and inflating is a denial of service; so the check was
      cut back to what cannot be a denial of service and still closes the original PoC. **Accepted limit:** best effort in the clear, not a sandbox; PDFs whose
      objects are compressed or obfuscated are NOT inspected. **The defences that matter:** (1) the original is only ever served as a signed download from the
      bucket host with the type fixed by the signature and `Content-Disposition: attachment` (`StorageService.downloadUrl`; `tests/api/finance-transaction-documents.spec.ts`
      asserts the receipt link), never inline in the origin of the app, and (2) the ClamAV scan that runs before this. Debts (rule 12), owner: Step 7.3
      hardening backlog: (a) the isolated inspector: parse and inflate in a `child_process` with an RSS limit and a hard kill, the day an owner wants real
      detection (a parser library or `qpdf --object-streams=disable` as a dependency); (b) `nosniff` and a CSP sandbox on the bucket host answers belong to the
      bucket or its proxy (a signed URL cannot set them; closed as a documented limit by PR `fix/receipt-pdf-refusal-debts`, see the task of Step 7.3); (c) CLOSED by
      that PR: the web now explains the refusal (`finance.transactions.receipt.refusals.*`, `receiptRefusalOf`: `transaction_document_refused`, `_not_clean`, `_already_set`
      and the 410 `FILE_UNSCANNABLE` that the wait for the verdict throws first, which is the path a person really takes, and whose generic text said "discarded"
      although a finance document is kept). The refused object stays in the bucket ON PURPOSE: a finance document is evidence (`EvidenceMediaPurposes`, TDD_07 §6.5,
      HC-122), no sweep of `OrphanMediaCleaner` deletes it and it is never served; deleting it is a decision of a person, the task of Step 7.3 below keeps the
      question of a deletion tool and of a notification or audit entry for the uploader;
      (d) PDFs of
      other purposes (a customer's message attachment, an order file) are not inspected: whether they should be is the owner's decision; (e) the bytes are read
      from the bucket a second time after the ClamAV read (as `sanitize` does for pictures): a window shared with the sanitizer, to close for both together;
      (f) the worker integration case with a real bucket and a refused PDF needs a finance transaction fixture of its own: the unit cases prove the row,
      `tests/api/finance-transaction-documents.spec.ts` proves the 409.
- [x] **4B.4b-2 tests:** matching rules and every parser error, isolation cases of the new tables
- [x] **4B.4b-2 note (receipt link across stores, RLS enforced):** `GET finance/transactions/:id/document` is `@NoTenantTransaction` and opens three
      contexts (transaction in the organization; owner store of the file by its id in the stores of the organization, one read; signing in that one store).
      A user of a sibling store with `finance:view_journal` sees the receipt of another store of the organization: the books are the organization's and
      the permission is organization-level, the same as with RLS off. Closed by the PR `fix/finance-receipt-attach-cross-store`: `POST finance/transactions/:id/document`
      is `@NoTenantTransaction` too and opens three contexts (transaction and checks in the organization; the file by its id in the stores of the
      organization, one read that writes nothing; the link written in the organization AND the one store of the ROW of the file, because the trigger
      `check_finance_transaction_row` is not SECURITY DEFINER and reads `media` under its store policy). Same parity: a user of A2 with the finance
      permissions attaches a file uploaded in A1 of the same organization, as with RLS off; the answers stay one 404 for a file that is not of this
      transaction, purpose or organization. Known limits (Hardening): the audit entry is written after the unit closes, the standard semantics of `AuditService` (the link is durable and
      immutable; writing it inside the unit would take the detached path, which does not wait for the commit), so a crash between the COMMIT and the insert
      loses the entry; a file that turns infected between the read and the write answers the 404 of the trigger, an equally safe refusal.
      Debt: the sweep of non-definer triggers that read a table with a store policy, assessed by 4B, owner: RLS phase 6 residuals. Read by fc:
      `check_bank_import_row` (reads `media`) is safe today because the service creates the file and the import row in the same call; it becomes a risk
      the day the upload and the import are separated; the fiscal evidence and customer-data triggers and the automatic fiscal writes are safe.
- [x] **4B.4b-2, bank file of the owner's first bank (PR `bank-import-datetime-thousands`):** a date with a time after the day
      (`dd/MM/yyyy hh:mm[:ss]`, an ISO day may use a T) is read on the bank route only (remittances still refuse a time); the time is part of the
      identity of the line (`bankLineKey`) when the row has one, so a statement that overlaps another never doubles a line and two equal
      movements of one day at two times stay two; a row with no time keeps the identity it always had (what was imported is still known); the
      thousands separator may be the delimiter (the quoted `"9,999.99"` of the bank; migration `20270112100000` drops that clause of the
      database CHECK too, with its rollback), an unquoted one is refused (a row must then have exactly the cells of the file, and an amount of one to three digits followed by a cell of
      three digits is the mark of a split amount)
- [x] **4B.4b-2, same bank file (PR `bank-import-skiprows`):** `skipRows` in the profile (0 to 50, default 0, so every saved profile reads as it did)
      leaves out the lead of report lines before the movements. It counts records (rows that are not blank; a title with a quoted line
      break is one), what is skipped is not read at all, and an error still points at the line of the file. Migration `20270113100000`
      (column, CHECK 0..50, rollback), api schemas, preview, web field (es/en), contract and integration tests with synthetic files
- [ ] **Debts of the bank-file PRs (rule 12), owner: Step 7.3 unless said:** (a) a movement that one statement prints with a time and another
      without it is not recognised as the same line (a bank prints it one way; a profile change of a bank mid-history would double the overlap);
      (b) a negative amount in parentheses `(179.60)` is not read (`parseBankAmountCents`): the bank prints them only in its running-balance
      column, which no profile maps; (c) the running balance of each row is not read, so it cannot check that no line was lost or misread: a
      balance column in the profile, with the statement's own closing balance as a control, is a new feature; (d) the time of a line is hashed into its identity but not stored on `bank_statement_lines` (no column, no migration in the PR
      that reads it): the screens show it only in the preview, and two stored lines that differ only by their time cannot be told apart there;
      a `posted_time` column is the fix; (e) a lead whose title opens a quote that never closes (`"Statement of account`) makes
      the whole file an `unclosed_quote` before the skip is applied: the lead is split like any text, so the profile cannot leave it out; (f) the
      profile saves with any `skipRows` and any `hasHeader` (a count one too low or too high shows only in the preview, as `column_not_found` or
      `header_looks_like_data`): a required preview before saving is a screen decision of the owner; (g) the CHECK of the column holds the literal
      50 of `BankStatementLimits.SKIP_ROWS_MAX` (a security spec compares both), raising one needs a migration for the other
**TDD:** `TDD_18 §4.3`, `§4.4`, `TDD_07 §6.3`
**Done when:** a person registers an expense paid from a chosen account with its VAT and a receipt, moves money between accounts, imports
a statement and reconciles it, and every balance follows.

**Decisions of PR 4B.4a (rule 12):** (1) the three kinds share one route (`finance/transactions`) and the permission of the KIND is
checked by the service (`RequireAnyPermission` on the route, `requireTransactionPermission` in the service): rejected, one route per kind
(three times the routes, the same check). A bookkeeper holding only `manage_transactions` cannot register or void a transfer, a treasurer
holding only `move_money` cannot register an expense, and `finance:view_journal` reads. (2) The money source and destination of an expense,
an income and a transfer must be cash-kind accounts (cash, bank or wallet), and the category must be an expense (or income) account:
rejected, any account of the chart (an expense paid out of "suppliers" is a purchase, 4B.5, and out of inventory is a stock adjustment);
checked by the rules, the service and a database trigger. (3) The tax is computed by the server from the chosen rate with the rounding of the
books and is never taken from the body; an expense whose tax is not creditable books the whole amount to the category. Rejected: a tax
amount typed by the person. (4) A transaction is never edited: `replace` voids and registers in one database transaction (either both happen or
neither), keeps the kind, and a retry with the same key answers the replacement without voiding twice. The row can change only by its pointer to
the voiding entry, once (a trigger refuses the owner of the table too; the application roles hold UPDATE on that one column and no DELETE).
(5) The client key (`idempotencyKey`) is stored per organization and compared on a retry: the same content is the same request, other content under
the same key is `409` (`FinanceConflicts.TRANSACTION_KEY_REUSED`), never an overwrite; requests with one key at once wait on an advisory lock
rather than depend on catching a unique violation inside the request's transaction. (6) The accounting date may be at most one day ahead of the
server's day (`FinanceLimits.TRANSACTION_FUTURE_DAYS`): a typed year in the future would open a period years ahead. (7) `LedgerService` now
checks that a tax rate a line names is one of the organization (it refused every rate since 4B.2, before the rate table existed); the supplier check
stays refused until 4B.5. (8) Voiding is a HIGH-tier destructive action (`VOID_FINANCE_TRANSACTION`), like reversing an entry.
**Debts of PR 4B.4a:** (a) the supplier of an expense (`supplierId`, TDD_18 §2.6): the column comes with the `Supplier` table in 4B.5 (additive).
(b) The receipt (`documentMediaId`) and `finance_document` are 4B.4b. (c) A tax amount that the supplier's document rounds differently from the
server by a cent cannot be typed: owner and accountant decide with `TDD_18 §13` row 2; the interface (4B.9) shows the computed amount. (d) The
`finance:` entry of `PermissionsOfUnbuiltAreas` stays until 4B.9, which draws the screens (the permissions are read by the code now).
(e) A fee a bank charges on a transfer is a second expense by hand: a transfer with a fee line is not modelled.
(f) A transaction at a rate of 0 % posts no tax line (a line has one side above zero), so no journal line carries its rate: the VAT report of 4B.8
reads the base of zero-rated expenses and incomes from `finance_transactions` (`tax_rate_id`, `amount_cents`), not from the lines. (g) The list has an
index for its order; the filter by account (three columns) has none until the volume asks for it (4B.9 measures). (h) The permission of a transaction is
the caller's in the store of `X-Store-Id` and the ledger is the organization's (`TDD_18 §9.1`): a store in the body is a dimension and is not compared with
the permissions of that store, by design. (i) A trigger of the table that fires (a race, a bug) surfaces as the error it is, not typed: the service answers
every rule first. (j) The trigger ties a header to its entry by type, source, total and date, not by the entry's lines (accounts and sides per kind, the tax line): the service is the only writer and the
entry is the record of the money; a line-level check is for the reconciliation of 4B.8. (k) Voiding is not keyed: a retry after a lost answer is `409`
(`TRANSACTION_ALREADY_VOIDED`) and the screen reads the transaction (4B.9). (l) The accounts and the rate a request names are read, not locked, like every
post of the ledger: a chart change in the same instant ends in the database's typed refusals or in its trigger. The header of an expense whose tax is not
creditable stores `tax_cents = 0` (the entry books it whole to the category).
(m) A transaction voided after its period closed keeps `occurred_on` in the closed month while the reversal is dated in the open one: a report that reads the headers
(the zero-rated base of (f)) takes the date a void took effect from the reversal entry's `entry_date` (`voided_by_entry_id` joined to `journal_entries`), never from the header's
own date or its voided flag; owner 4B.8. (n) The list orders by `created_at` (the start of the database transaction), so a request that waited on a lock can commit with an older
stamp than one that committed before it: ordering by the entry number is the fix if a screen ever pages while a post waits (4B.9). (o) The header is tied to its entry by type, source,
total and date only, not by the store of its lines nor its tax line (extends (j); the reconciliation of 4B.8). (p) The audit row of a record or a void is written after the commit,
as every audit of the platform is; a crash between the two loses it (the entry and the reversal carry the author and the time): moving it inside the transaction is a decision for the
audit service as a whole, not for this PR.
**Decisions of PR 4B.4b-1 (rule 12):** (1) A receipt is a `Media` of the purpose `finance_document` made FOR a transaction
(`media.finance_transaction_id`, the parent of the upload: one transaction of the organization of the store of the request, 404 for another
organization's or a missing one, the same answer) and the transaction then points at it ONCE (`finance_transactions.document_media_id`,
`POST finance/transactions/:id/document`). Rejected: a `documentMediaId` in the body of the record (the file needs its parent to exist
before the upload, so the transaction must exist first) and a free-floating file that any transaction could claim (the check of the
organization would then be the only one). (2) The pointer is the one column besides the voiding pointer that the table lets move, from null
to a file, once, and never together with another change; the trigger checks that the file is of the purpose of a receipt, was made for THIS
transaction and sits in a store of the SAME organization, so a file of another organization is refused whoever writes (the owner of the table
included). Rejected: leaving the check to the service alone. (3) A receipt is set once and a wrong file is a new transaction (void and
register again, the immutability of the books): rejected, replacing the pointer (it would let the evidence of a posted entry change after the
fact with no trace but an audit row). A retry of the same file answers the transaction and writes nothing. Only a file the scan found
CLEAN can be attached (the trigger checks it too: an infected or unscanned file would be the receipt for ever); the screen waits for the
scan (`409 transaction_document_not_clean`). (4) The permission is the one of the KIND of the transaction (as voiding), narrowed by the
service at the upload (before anything is signed, and a voided or documented transaction takes no upload) and again at the attach; the
upload and the attach ask for the journal's view and one of the two permissions that register (`MEDIA_UPLOAD` is the route's), so an id
never tells more than reading it would. A file that is a receipt keeps its purpose, parent and store (a trigger on `media`), and a
finance file has no other parent (a CHECK). Reading the file asks for `finance:view_journal`
(a receipt shows what the organization paid and to whom). (5) The signed links come from a finance route, through the store the FILE lives in,
because the books are the organization's: a member of another store of the same organization reads it with the same permission and a member
of another organization gets a 404. Only a clean file is served (the scan of the pipeline; a pending or infected one is refused). (6) The
file keeps the pipeline of every upload (signed PUT, ETag-pinned copy, type and magic bytes checked, the scan before it is served): the new
purpose takes the three still images and a PDF, 10 MB, as a file of an order. (7) A receipt restricts the deletion of its media row and of its
transaction (`ON DELETE RESTRICT` both ways), so a store with receipts cannot be deleted while the books name it (the same as its
transactions, whose store link restricts).
**Debts of PR 4B.4b-1:** (a) The replacement of a transaction (`replace`) does not carry the receipt of the one it voids: the new transaction
takes a new file (upload for the new transaction, then attach); the screen of 4B.9 offers the old file to download. (b) A
confirmed `finance_document` file that is never attached stays in its store (the orphan cleanup only settles pending, infected and
avatar rows): bounded by the hourly quota of signed urls, and a cleanup of unattached receipts older than the pending window is owned by
Step 7.4 (the worker's hardening step). (c) The receipt of
a transfer or an expense of a store the caller cannot see is read through the store the file lives in, with the permission of the CALLER's
store (`TDD_18 §9.1`: the ledger is the organization's), without checking that the caller belongs to the store the file lives in: by design,
the books are the organization's and a receipt is read with the journal's permission; a per-store read of finance documents is a decision
with the stores of Phase 2.
(d) The web part (an upload button on the transaction) is 4B.9; `QueryKeys` for the receipt come with it.

**Decisions of PR 4B.4b-2 (rule 12):** (1) A decision is a row of `reconciliation_matches` (`confirmed`, `rejected`, or `undone` once taken back) and the
journal is never touched, so the immutable lines carry no flag; the database holds one confirmed match per statement line and per journal line (partial
unique indexes), that the two lines are of the same organization and account, and that a confirmed pair is the same movement (debit minus credit equals the
statement's signed amount) on an entry that nothing reversed and that is no reversal. Rejected: a `matched` column on the statement line (it would be a mutable
flag that a bug can set without a decision) and a link table with no history (a mistaken confirmation could not be explained). (2) Suggestions are computed
when the lines are read, never stored: rejected, a table of suggestions (stale the moment the books change). A suggestion is the same amount to the cent in the
same direction (a debit of the cash account is money in), within the days window of the profile that read the file (0 to 31, default 3), minus the pairs a
person rejected; the order is the reference first, then the nearest day, then the id. (3) "Exact" means the same day, or a reference of the bank that can be a document number (4 characters or more and a digit: "Pago" is in every memo) inside what the books say (the supplier's document number, the memo of the entry, the memo of the transaction) or the reverse. The bulk
confirmation confirms only a line with ONE suggestion that is exact and that no other line also wants; everything with two possibilities stays for a person.
Rejected: confirming the best-scored suggestion (a score is a guess, and a wrong reconciliation of money is worse than an open line). (4) A person's confirmation
is checked by the server against the same rules whatever the screen sent (a pair outside the window or of another amount is `409 bank_pair_not_allowed`),
and a line of another account or organization does not exist for the request (404). (5) The reading is strict and the whole file is refused with the rows that
failed (a statement is never imported half): amounts are signed cents (one column, or one column of debits and one of credits that must fill exactly one),
no currency symbol, exponent or parentheses, a zero amount is an error, a thousands separator only when the profile names it and then only in groups of
three; dates in the format of the profile and a real day; text with no control, invisible or look-alike character; a cell that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or
`@` is TEXT and is never evaluated (the file is read as text, nothing is exported in this PR; whatever exports it later neutralizes the cell as the VAT CSV
does). A bank is data: delimiter, header, decimal and thousands separators, date format, columns (by header text or position), encoding (UTF-8 or
Windows-1252, named by the profile and never guessed) and window are the profile's; no bank and no fiscal fact is built in or invented. (6) The idempotency of a
line is the sha256 of the account, the day, the amount, the reference, the description and which of the equal lines it is in its file: a statement that overlaps
the last one brings only what is new, a file whose lines are all known is `409 bank_import_nothing_new`, and two identical lines of one statement are two
movements. Imports into one account take turns (an advisory lock) and the unique index of the hash holds when two requests race. (7) The file is kept as the
evidence: a `Media` of purpose `finance_document` with no parent, in the store of the request, scanned like any file from outside, and the import, its lines
and the file are append-only (triggers that hold the owner of the table too, and no UPDATE or DELETE for the application roles). (8) The closing balance of the
statement is typed by the person at the import (`closingBalanceCents` with `closingOn`, both or neither): rejected, a balance column in the profile (banks print
it in different places and orders, and a wrong one would make the difference look right). The difference is the balance of the books of the account up to that
day against it, with what the unmatched lines of each side explain and what no line explains. (9) Every route asks for `FINANCE_RECONCILE`, reading
included (a statement shows the movements of the accounts and the journal's permission is not it); the organization is the guard's. (10) "Register it" returns the
transaction of 4B.4a an unmatched line would be, prefilled, and posts nothing: the person completes it (category, tax) and registers it with the permission of its
kind. (11) A transaction voided and its reversal are never candidates (neither reached the bank); matching is allowed in a closed period because it edits nothing. (12) An entry that a confirmed match names is NOT reversed: `LedgerService.reverse` answers `409 FINANCE_ENTRY_RECONCILED` (so voiding or replacing its transaction, reversing it by hand and the reversal of a remittance entry all wait until the match is taken back), and a trigger on `journal_entries` holds the same rule under an advisory lock that the confirmation also takes (a confirmation and a reversal at the same moment take turns). Rejected: letting the void through and showing the reversal as an open book line (the reconciliation would then say a line is matched to a dead entry). A rejection is refused for a line that is matched, and a repeated rejection writes no audit row; choosing a pair that was rejected retires the rejection, a description over 300 characters is cut (information, not a reason to refuse the file), a reference counts as agreeing only as a whole token that can be a document number, the difference at a day counts an entry reversed after it as still on the books then; the audit row of a bulk confirmation lists each pair and the id of its decision; the doubt of a bulk confirmation is judged among the open lines of EVERY statement of the account that can reach the same line of the books.
**Debts of PR 4B.4b-2:** (a) The web part (upload, mapper, the list of suggestions with confirm, reject and undo, the draft of "register it", the status by account and month,
the difference) and `QueryKeys` / api-client functions are 4B.9. (b) Voiding a reconciled transaction is refused with `FINANCE_ENTRY_RECONCILED` (decision 12): the screen of 4B.9 offers "take the reconciliation back" before it, and shows the code's text; owner 4B.9. (c) One
statement line pairs with one journal line: a bank charge that settles several entries or an entry paid in two deposits is not modelled (the person registers the
difference by hand); a many-to-one pairing is a decision for the accountant ([ACCOUNTANT], §13) before it is built. (d) The draft of "register it" offers an income or an expense
only: a transfer between two of the organization's own accounts is a line on each side, and the screen of 4B.9 offers the transfer. (e) Two genuinely different movements with the same account, day, amount, reference and description in two files that do not overlap (a bank that exports one file per batch of the same day) are the same line to the hash, and a file whose only lines are such is `409 bank_import_nothing_new`: the bank gives no id of a movement, so the import takes whole days (a statement that covers each day it names) and the person registers the missing one by hand; a bank that does give one maps it as the reference. The same hash depends on the text as the profile reads it: after the mapping of the description or the reference is changed, or the bank rewords a memo, an overlapping statement brings the lines as new (a profile is changed for a new statement, not an old one; the rows are append-only and the person sees the new lines). A file's lines that repeat an earlier statement in
a different count (three equal lines now, two before) bring the extra one as new: the hash tells equal lines apart by their order, so a statement that was
corrected by the bank by hand needs a person's eye; the list shows the new lines. (f) The state by account is by calendar month, like the periods (a fiscal year that is not the
calendar one is a template setting, §2.4). (g) The page of lines reads the whole import in memory (the file holds 5000 rows at most) to give the suggestions: a larger import would page
in the database; the limit is `BankStatementLimits.MAX_ROWS`. (h) The audit row of an import or a decision is written after the commit, as every audit of the platform
is (4B.4a (p)). (i) The CSV export of unmatched lines for the accountant, with the formula guard, comes with the reports of 4B.8. (k) The body reader of the import (`readImportBody`) still lives in the remittances module and the bank import takes it with an options bag (code and encoding); moving it to a shared module with the content types as a parameter is a refactor of both imports, owner Step 7.4 (hardening). (j) A statement in a currency other than USD is not read
(TDD_18 §2.8); the amount of a line is whole USD cents.

Fix of the reading of a bank statement (PR `fix/bank-csv-safe-parse`, rule 12, QA PUR-032/026/046/038/110): a statement is never changed once it is kept, so nothing is
dropped or guessed in silence. Decisions: (1) a profile that says the file has a header and maps its columns by position refuses a file whose first row has a
date that reads (`header_looks_like_data`, with the line of the file where the row is): the movement would have been taken for the header and lost; rejected: a
warning only (the statement would still be kept incomplete). (2) A description that spans lines (banks join the memo of a transfer) is read as one line (a run of
line breaks, tabs and line separators is one space) instead of refusing the whole file; the reference stays strict because it is what matches a book line, and any
other control character still refuses the row. (3) A slash date reads in two orders (03/11/2026); a file whose every date reads in both (no date with a number above 12,
and not all the same day and month) answers `409 bank_date_format_unconfirmed` with the format and the days that were read, and is kept only when the person confirms
(`dateFormatConfirmed=true`; the import screen shows the days and a box); a date that can only be read in the other order is still `invalid_date`. Rejected: refusing
every such file (a statement of the first twelve days of a month is legitimate) and guessing from the order of the lines. (4) The length of a description and of a
reference is counted in characters, not UTF-16 units (an emoji is one). (5) `closingBalanceCents` is a whole number of cents and nothing else (a blank no longer reads
as 0 and `1e3` or `0x10` are refused). No data model changed. The count in characters is shared by the remittance import (its guide numbers and references count characters too). One date that can only be read in the order of the profile confirms the order for the whole file, by design (a file that mixes orders is the bank's, and every date that cannot be read is still `invalid_date`); the confirmation is audited (`dateFormatConfirmed`). **Debt:** many-to-one deposits and net-of-fee deposits stay the accountant's decision ([ACCOUNTANT], debt c of
4B.4b-2); the preview of the profile mapper does not yet show the `dateFormatUndecided` warning (the import asks): Step 7.4.

Fix `fix/bank-csv-dash-cells` (HC-125, owner question P-R2-09, decided under rule 12): in a statement with a debit column and a credit column, a lone `-` or `--` in
the column that does not apply is read as nothing, like an empty cell, so a bank that prints dashes no longer needs its file cleaned. Rejected: accepting any dash
text (`---`, `-5.00` still refuse; a sign inside the column is a mistake) and changing the signed `amount` column (a dash there says nothing about the money, so it
refuses). A row with a dash in both columns still says nothing and is refused as `ambiguous_direction`. The other parts of HC-125 (line breaks in a description,
the closing balance) were closed by #582 (PUR-026/110 PASS). The remittance import (`remittance-import.ts`) keeps its stricter reading; its own question stays with the owner.

Review of 4B.4a (rule 12): the generic `POST finance/entries/:id/reverse` now refuses the entry of a transaction
(`FinanceConflicts.ENTRY_OWNED_BY_TRANSACTION`), because it would leave the transaction looking live and skip its kind's permission and audit row.

### Step 4B.5 — Suppliers and purchase orders (api)
- [x] `Supplier`, `PurchaseOrder`, `PurchaseOrderLine`, `PurchaseReceipt` (+ lines), `SupplierPayment`; the transition table;
      the purchase number counter; permission `FINANCE_MANAGE_PURCHASES` and `FINANCE_MOVE_MONEY` for payments
- [x] Receiving (partial or total) calls `InventoryService.receive` per line with the unit cost before tax (the average moves) and posts
      E10; the supplier's document number is kept; a receipt above the ordered quantity is refused; payments (partial or total) post E11
      from the account the person chooses and cannot exceed the open balance; the open balance per supplier (party dimension)
- [x] Tests: receipt raises stock and cost and posts one entry, partial receipts and payments, closing a short purchase, cancellation
      rules, isolation (the lines by store)
- [x] Debts written here (rule 12): returns to suppliers and debit notes, and the allocation of a purchase's freight into the unit cost
      (landed cost): after the MVP, owner decides when
**TDD:** `TDD_18 §2.7`, `§4.2` E10 and E11, `TDD_16 §4`
**Done when:** a purchase order is received into a warehouse (stock and weighted-average cost move), the amount owed appears for the
supplier and is paid in parts from the chosen account, and the ledger agrees with the stock value.

**Decisions of 4B.5 (rule 12), all marked [ACCOUNTANT] where they are the accountant's to confirm:** (1) The module is `apps/api/src/modules/purchases`
(its own, so it does not share files with the books' module); the routes are `suppliers`, `suppliers/payables`, `suppliers/:id/balance`,
`suppliers/:id/payments`, `supplier-payments/:id/void` and `purchase-orders` (+ `order`, `receive`, `close`, `cancel`, `payments`), all organization-scoped
(`finance:manage_purchases` writes and reads suppliers and orders; `finance:move_money` pays and voids a payment; what is owed is read with either).
(2) `InventoryService` has no `receive`: a receipt line is a `RECEIPT` movement through `move`/`moveMany` in the receipt's own transaction, with the unit cost
before tax, the order number as its note and the new reference type `purchase_receipt` (the id is the receipt), so the weighted average moves and the stock value of
the ledger of stock is exactly what the entry debits to `INVENTORY`. (3) The tax of a receipt is computed per line, ON TOP of the cost, with the organization's
rounding (`TaxRounding`); the rate of a line is the one the order names (none = untaxed), and the input VAT account is the rate's `inputAccountId`, like 4B.4a.
(4) **[ACCOUNTANT]** The tax is credited as input VAT only against a supplier document: `taxCreditable` defaults to "a document number was given", can be sent
explicitly, and `true` without a number is refused (a CHECK holds it too). A tax that is NOT creditable is booked to the `UNCATEGORIZED_EXPENSE` role (a visible cost; a
receipt that needs it without the role mapped fails with `FINANCE_ROLE_NOT_MAPPED`), so the stock keeps its cost and the ledger agrees with the stock value. The
receiving of the prepaid-guide model of a carrier (4B.6) does not go through here. (5) The payable account of a supplier is its `defaultPayableAccountId` or the
`PAYABLE_SUPPLIERS` role, and is fixed once the supplier has a bill or a payment (`SUPPLIER_HAS_HISTORY`), so its payments post where its bills did. (6) A payment
is checked against the supplier's open balance and, when it names a bill, against the open part of that bill, with the supplier locked; a payment that names no
bill is applied to the oldest due first when the bills are listed (`billBalances`, pure), so the supplier's open amount is exactly bills minus payments. (7) A payment
is voided only by its own route (`VOID_SUPPLIER_PAYMENT`, HIGH tier): the reversing entry plus a pointer set once; the generic `POST finance/entries/:id/reverse`
refuses the entry of a receipt or a payment (`ENTRY_OWNED_BY_PURCHASE`), like 4B.4a did for a transaction. A receipt is never voided: the way back is a return to the
supplier (debt (a)). (8) The lines of an order and of a receipt carry the store of their product and are read and written only by the members of that store holding
`finance:manage_purchases` (`visibleStoreIds`, like the lines of a transfer); the header is the organization's. (9) A receipt dated before `accountingStartDate` or in a
closed period is refused by the ledger like any entry (`FINANCE_BEFORE_START_DATE`, `FINANCE_PERIOD_CLOSED`); a purchase of goods with no cost (a receipt that owes nothing)
is refused: free goods are a stock adjustment. (10) Rejected alternative for (6): requiring every payment to name a bill; kept optional because TDD_18 §2.7 has the
bill optional.
**Close and cancel of a purchase order wholly the caller's (N-AA-03, QA PUR-R2-011, rule 12):** `POST /purchase-orders/:id/close` and `/cancel` now refuse with `409` and `conflict: line_store_not_visible` (`PurchaseConflicts.LINE_STORE_NOT_VISIBLE`, the same conflict an edit or a receipt of lines the caller does not see already gives, so no new code) when the order has a line STILL TO ARRIVE (`receivedQuantity < quantity`) of a store the caller is not an active member of with `finance:manage_purchases`: ending an order gives up every line still to arrive, so a person who cannot read the lines of another store could end them for the people who can; a line already received in full gives up nothing, so it does not block the tidying of an order received in full (a decision of this PR, from the review: the strict reading would leave such an order open for ever when the other store's buyers are gone). Cancel was included because it has the same hole (a draft with lines of two stores). Rejected: a new 403 code (the edit and the receipt already answer 409, one answer for one rule). **Known limit (Step 7.3):** an order with a line of a store whose only buyers lost the permission can no longer be ended by anyone but a person who holds it in every store of the order; a break-glass path for the owner is not built. **Also left (web and tenancy, Step 4B.9a-4 follow-up / 7.3):** the Close and Cancel buttons are shown by status alone, so a caller who is always refused fills in the reason dialog and meets the conflict afterwards (hide them when the detail shows fewer lines than the order has); the text of `line_store_not_visible` says "a store you do not belong to", which is not true when the person belongs to the store but lacks the permission there; the lookup of the visible stores runs before the lock of the order, as it does in the edit (read it inside the transaction in both).
**Debts of 4B.5 (rule 12):** (a) Returns to suppliers and debit notes, and the landed cost (a purchase's freight into the unit cost): after the MVP, owner decides when
(the plan's own debt). (b) The payables read (`suppliers/payables`, `balance`) sums the bills of the organization (or the supplier) in one pass: bounded by the volume
of an MVP, with no page; a paged and a closed-bills filter come with the reports of 4B.8. (c) The comparison of the payable account (party = supplier) with the
operational payables, and of `INVENTORY` with `InventoryLevel.valueCents`, belongs to the daily `RECONCILE_FINANCE` of 4B.6; 4B.5 proves them equal in the integration
suite only. (d) The web (suppliers, orders, the receive screen, payables with due dates) and the `QueryKeys` and `AppPaths` for them are 4B.9; every route is mapped to that
step in `scripts/frontend-coverage-map.ts`. (e) The model of the carrier charge (prepaid | collected in the remittance | invoiced) and the purchase of prepaid guides stay in
4B.6, as the note on E4 says; nothing here assumes any of the three. (f) The unique-name rule of a supplier is "ignoring case, per organization"; whether the accountant also
wants the tax id unique is asked with the questions of the accountant. (g) Closing or cancelling does not notify anyone: the `PURCHASE_ORDER_RECEIVED` event is api-only
(no listener until 4B.6/7.x needs it). (h) A purchase of a store's product is received into ONE warehouse per order; splitting an order across warehouses is a second
order.
(i) A supplier's document number belongs to ONE order (the same invoice on another order is refused, `DOCUMENT_NUMBER_IN_USE`, because it would credit the tax
twice); several receipts of one order may share it, since an invoice can arrive in parts, and a repeat inside one order is bounded by the quantities ordered. A unique
index per supplier waits for the accountant's answer on what a valid document is (4B.7). (j) The database ties the store of a line to the organization (composite key)
and the line to its product (`store_id`, `product_id`), but not the variant to the product: the service checks it, and a trigger can follow with the chart of the
variants in 7.4. (k) The payables read runs two queries with no shared snapshot when called outside a payment: a payment that lands between them shows one bill too
open for that read only; the payment path reads inside the supplier lock, so it is exact. (l) A receipt updates its order lines one by one (up to 200 statements inside
the lock); a single statement is an optimization for 7.4 if the volume shows it. (m) `PurchaseReceiptLine.movementId` has no foreign key (the ledger of stock is
append-only and its rows are never deleted); the integration suite proves every line names a movement. (n) The ledger now accepts a supplier as the party of a line (it
refused one until this step) and checks it is the organization's. The column `finance_settings.next_purchase_number` is granted to the application roles by this
migration, as the ledger migration asks of every new column.

**PR fix/supplier-document-normalized (HC-124, first part)**
- [x] The duplicate check of the invoice of a supplier on another order compares `documentNumberKey` (letters and digits, in capitals, NFC), not the
      text as typed: `fac-001`, `FAC 001` and `Fac001` are one invoice (`purchase-receiving.service.ts`; unit spec and `tests/api/purchases.spec.ts`).
      A number with no letter or digit is compared as typed. Decisions: numbers that differ only in where the
      separators are (`12-3`, `1-23`) share a key and the second is refused (no override in the receive path): **[ACCOUNTANT]** to confirm
      (P-13); rejected: keeping the separators (the hole HC-124 reports). The check runs under the existing supplier lock, so two receipts
      cannot both pass; receipts are never voided, so a number is never released. A fuller key is NFKC, capitals, letters and digits. Compared in code over the distinct numbers of the supplier, not in SQL, so the
      rule is the same on every database locale; no migration. The replay of the same receipt keeps its exact comparison.
- [ ] **Debt (HC-124, other parts):** a rate switched off after the order was placed blocks the receipt with no way out (own PR, next); a supplier
      payment dated before the invoice is accepted (`supplier-payments.service.ts`) and the bank reconciliation does not compare the supplier
      document number (`finance-reconciliation.service.ts`): both wait for the accountant's answers P-13/P-17 and the owner; closes in Step 4B.9b-5d.
**PR fix/receipt-inactive-rate (HC-124, second part)**
- [x] A tax rate switched off after the order was placed no longer blocks the receipt (there was no way out: a placed order cannot be edited). The
      draft still refuses a rate that is off; the receipt posts the tax with the rate as it is now (percent and input account; a missing rate is
      refused), and the accounts of a rate stay active while the rate exists (`usedBySetting`). **Debt (Step 7.3):** the rate is not snapshotted on the
      order line, so editing a rate between the placing and the receipt changes the tax posted; snapshot it or refuse the edit of a rate in use by a placed order. Decision, **[ACCOUNTANT]** to confirm: the tax follows the invoice the order
      was placed with, not the law of the day of the receipt; rejected: refusing and asking to cancel the order (the stock is already coming).
      Test in `tests/api/purchases.spec.ts`.

### Step 4B.6 — The automatic entries (api and worker)
The step is cut in two PRs by what each needs (rule 12; one session, one PR; the cut is mine): **4B.6a** is the machinery and the entries that
need nothing from the carriers' side; **4B.6b** is everything that waits on the remittance, the return and the carrier's charge model.
- [x] **4B.6a:** the listener (api) and `POST_FINANCE_EVENT` (a job of the heavy queue, name in `JobNames`; the processor in the worker),
      `FinancePostingService` (`libs/core/finance`, one transaction per event, an advisory lock per source, the current rows, the key
      first), the pure builders `libs/core/finance/src/auto-entry-rules.ts` for **E1** (payment), **E2** (goods in transit), **E3** (sale
      recognized, cash on delivery or prepaid) and **E9** (adjustments and count variances), the idempotency keys
      (`FinancePostingKey`), the late-post rule and `accountingStartDate` skipping (`automaticEntryDate`)
- [x] **4B.6a:** "Post again" of a failed source: `POST /finance/postings/:id/retry` (`finance:manage_accounts`) re-runs the same service
      on the rows as they are and closes the `FinancePostingFailure`; `FINANCE_POSTING_FAILED` is an event (ids and a reason code)
- [x] **4B.6a:** tests with exact amounts (a COD sale, a prepaid sale, the cost cleared once whichever entry came first, a missing mapping,
      no tax recorded, no cost, a payment method without an account, sale recognized at shipping, before the start of the books, a
      closed period, each adjustment, the same event twice), isolation between organizations, the job's schema
The rest of 4B.6 is cut in three PRs (rule 12; a session, a PR; the cut is the coordinator's approval of the session's proposal, because the
three parts each need their own owner or accountant decision and the money code is reviewed in small batches): **4B.6b-1** the entries
that follow from a carrier's guide and remittance, **4B.6b-2** the entries that need a new action or a refund decision, **4B.6b-3** the
sweep and the charge model.
- [x] **4B.6b-1:** E4 (the carrier's charges of a delivered outbound guide: `shipment:<id>:charges`, from the guide's own cost or rate and
      its commission), E5 (`remittance:<id>:confirm`, one entry per confirmed remittance) and E6 (`remittance:<id>:void`, the reversal of
      E5 by an entry of the system), the destination account of the money on the confirm of a remittance (`destinationAccountId` on the
      confirm body, default `BANK_DEFAULT`; migration `finance_remittance_destination` with its rollback)
- [x] **4B.6b-2:** E7 (write off the difference of a discrepancy: the action, its permission `FINANCE_MOVE_MONEY`, its status on the
      shipment) and E8 (returns, before and after delivery, with the refund destination); **`FINANCE_VIEW_CARRIER_FEES`** (below)
- [x] **4B.6b-3:** the sweep, its metrics, the notification of a failure and the guard of the close (below); the charge model of a carrier
      connection is **4B.6b-4** (it needs an account role the accountant chooses)
- [x] **4B.6b (done in 4B.6b-3, except the comparison of carrier receivables, debt (ar); the one of inventory is done by the `inventory-ledger-drift` fix below):** `RECONCILE_FINANCE` (daily): the sweep of unposted
      sources (it is what heals an event that was never queued), the recomputation of the balances; the metrics and the notification of
      `FINANCE_POSTING_FAILED` to who can fix it; `FinanceCloseGuard`, which the close of 4B.8 asks before it locks a month
- [x] **Fix `inventory-ledger-drift` (HC-007, HC-123 in part; rule 12):** the books post EXACTLY the value a stock movement moved. `inventory_movements.value_cents`
      (migration `20270114100000_inventory_movement_value`, with its rollback) holds what the level lost or gained; `planMovement` fills it, E2/E3 (`issueCost`),
      E9 units out (`adjustmentLines`), the cost put back by E8 (`restockCost`) and the margin read it, so that the inventory account and the stock value stay equal
      to the cent through issues (3 at 1.00 and 2 at 1.01, two leave: stock 301, books 301; all leave: no residue). The daily `RECONCILE_FINANCE` compares the inventory
      account with the sum of `inventory_levels.value_cents` of the organization (`FinanceSweepService.inventoryDrift`, one statement) and counts a difference in
      `platform_finance_balance_mismatches` with an error log; it posts nothing. Debts, each with its owner: (a) **a receipt over negative stock** (PUR-545): the
      level values only the units above zero while E10 debits inventory for every unit; how the units sold with no cost are booked is the accountant's decision
      (P-24), and so is the same case in `ADJUSTMENT_IN`/`COUNT_IN` over a deficit (the books debit the units times the cost, the level gains only the units above
      zero) and an issue of more units than were on hand (the value covers only the units that were): 4B.8b-4, the sweep shows the difference meanwhile. **A count that finds more units than the system has** (RA-740-4, fix `fix/count-in-without-cost`): the units come in with no cost, the engine values them at the average of the level and records that on the movement, and E9 now posts that recorded value (Dr INVENTORY · Cr INVENTORY_GAIN) instead of refusing them as `cost_missing`; a movement that has neither a cost nor a value still fails, never a zero. Failures already open for this cause close with *post again*. The same case over a deficit keeps the debt above (the value recorded is only the units above zero): 4B.8b-4. (b) **Transfers** bring units in at the rounded unit cost the dispatch recorded, so the stock moves
      by less than a cent a unit with no entry (the debt already noted in 4.5): pass the dispatched value to the `TRANSFER_IN`, prorated by the units received and
      closed to the last unit: Step 7.3. (c) **A return** puts the units back in stock at the current average (the engine) while E8 books the cost the sale took
      out (so that cost of goods sold clears exactly): the difference of the two, when the average moved, needs the accountant's choice of account: 4B.8b-4.
      (d) Rows written before the migration keep `value_cents` null and are valued at units x unit cost, as their entries were posted: no backfill (the journal is
      never rewritten). (e) The sweep still does not compare payables with the purchases (debt (c) of 4B.5), does not mark `truncated` when a preview fails and
      does not fix the zone of its cron (the rest of HC-123): 4B.8b-2c. (h) The inventory check reads after the sweep and compares the account the INVENTORY role points at today: a movement that commits between the two shows as a
      difference for one night, and an organization that remaps the role sees the old account drop out (the remap with history is PR-J of the QA list); it adds
      one to `platform_finance_balance_mismatches` whatever the size (the size is in the log and in the report), and a backlog of inventory events queued for
      several nights holds the check back meanwhile; its own gauge with the figure, and `valueCents` required in the row types of the readers (today an
      optional field that falls back to units x cost, so a new reader that forgets to select it brings the cent back): 4B.8b-2c. (g) `RECONCILE_INVENTORY` replays the ledger without `value_cents`, so a row whose value was edited or written wrong is seen only by the nightly
      total of the books, not at its movement: replay and compare the value of each row: Step 7.3. (f) An organization whose opening entry differs from the stock value at the start of
      its books shows a standing difference; the accountant's opening balance is meant to equal it (TDD_18, opening balances): the screen of 4B.9 shows both figures.
