      `shipping:view` stops showing them; the web of Settings → Carriers shows the boxes only with it)
- [x] **4B.6b (moved to 4B.6b-4, done by #688, #702 and #711; its debts are in the entry "4B.6b-4 done" below):** the charge model of a carrier connection (`prepaid` | `collected in the remittance` | `invoiced`, `TDD_18 §4.2` note on E4,
      owner's information to confirm with the accountant, `TDD_18 §13` rows 2 and 5) decides the entry of E4/E5 and the input VAT of a
      carrier charge; with 4B.5 for the purchase of prepaid guides. Not built by 4B.3 or 4B.6a
- [x] **4B.6b (done in 4B.6b-1, -2 and -3: a remittance that matches, one that differs, one voided, a difference written off, a return before and after the
      sale, a lost event recovered by the sweep, a failure that blocks the close)**
- [ ] Debt (rule 12): the cent of a carrier that rounds otherwise (4.15 (c2)(i)) and the real fee column (4.15 (c2)(iii)) are decided by the
      real C807 file; the entries follow what the remittance confirm recorded
**TDD:** `TDD_18 §4.2`, `§6`, `§11`, `TDD_17 §4.15`, `TDD_16 §4`, `TDD_07`
**Done when:** a delivered COD order, its remittance with the carrier's fee, a return and a stock count each leave the right balanced
entries with no human step, and the ledger's inventory and carrier receivables agree with the operational tables.

**Decisions of PR 4B.6a (rule 12):** (1) The job is `POST_FINANCE_EVENT` on the **heavy queue**, not a queue `default`: the TDD names a queue
that does not exist, and a tenth queue costs a processor, a dead-letter rule and a dashboard for a job that is light; the heavy queue
already carries the finance-like `RECONCILE_INVENTORY`. Rejected: a new queue. (2) The job carries the source and the event, **never an
amount**: `FinancePostingService` reads the current rows, so a late, repeated or reordered job posts the same entry. (3) The **service**
lives in `libs/core/finance` (provided by `LedgerModule`), used by the worker (the job) and by the api (the "post again" route), so a retry
can never post what the job would not. (4) **One advisory lock per source** (not per organization) serializes the events of one order, so
the choice "E2 first, or the sale straight from inventory" is taken on a settled state; the ledger's own lock of the organization is taken
inside it, always in that order. (5) **The cost is never taken out twice**: the sale clears inventory in transit by the total of the E2
entry when one exists, else takes it from inventory; E2 does nothing when the sale entry already exists. This also makes a change of
`recognizeSaleOn` safe in the middle of an order's life (the cut-over debt (f) of 4B.2b): the data, not the setting, decides. Rejected:
forcing E2 before E3 (a lost job would block the sale). (6) The **revenue is posted net of the discount** and `SALES_DISCOUNTS` is not
used: the order stores the tax after the discount but not the net of the discount, so showing it apart would put a figure computed here,
not read from the order (debt a). The order's figures are checked to the cent against its total; one that does not add up is refused,
never forced. (7) An order **without tax recorded** (made before the tax columns) is a failure `TAX_MISSING`, never an invented tax. A
movement that left **with no cost** is `COST_MISSING`, never a cost of zero. (8) A not-COD order delivered **unpaid** is a failure
(`SOURCE_NOT_READY`): a sale on credit is not built in the MVP (`TDD_18 §4.2` E3); the payment event queues the sale again. (9) A cash
on delivery order with **no carrier** (no shipment, none planned) is `CARRIER_MISSING`: the receivable needs a party. (10) A failure of the
books is **recorded and returned, not thrown**: the queue's retries are for the infrastructure; a person fixes a mapping and presses "post
again". The event `FINANCE_POSTING_FAILED` fires on a new, reopened or changed failure, never on the same one again. (11) The entry is
dated by the day of the event **in the store's time zone** (`automaticEntryDate`: the first day of the open period when that day is in a
closed one, `sourceDate` kept); a retry after a close finds its entry by the key instead of being refused for a date that moved. (12)
`INVENTORY_MOVED` now carries the `movementId`, so an adjustment is keyed by its movement. E1 and E3 use `JournalEntryType.SALE`, E2
`SALE_SHIPMENT`, E9 `INVENTORY_ADJUSTMENT`; the memo is a code (`auto:sale`), never a sentence.
**Debts of PR 4B.6a (all in this step):** (a) the discount shown apart on `SALES_DISCOUNTS` (decision 6) needs the net of the discount on the
order and the accountant's view of how it is presented: owner and accountant, 4B.8 (reports) reads the revenue as posted. (b) The sweep that
finds a source whose event was never queued, the metrics, and the notification of a failure to who can fix it are **4B.6b** (the event is
published and logged now). (c) E4 to E8 and the charge model are 4B.6b. (d) A stock adjustment of units **in** with no cost (every count gain and any manual
adjustment without a cost: the engine values them at the level's average but stores `null` on the movement) is a failure no "post
again" can clear: the books must be told the cost. Fix at the source (the engine stores the unit cost it valued the units at, a change of
`libs/core/inventory` and its kardex, with its own tests) or a "resolve without posting" action with a reason: owner's call, 4B.6b.
(h) The cost of an issue is quantity x the rounded unit cost the movement carries, while the engine removes `value x leaving / onHand`
from the level: they differ by up to half a cent per unit, and an issue beyond the stock on hand (negative stock allowed) is charged at the
average for all its units. The daily `RECONCILE_FINANCE` of 4B.6b compares the ledger's inventory with `InventoryLevel.valueCents` and
must carry a tolerance for this; the exact fix is for the movement to carry the value removed. (i) A prepaid order paid **before the
start of the books** has no E1, so its sale waits (a failure that does not alarm) until the accountant's opening balance covers the
advance and the failure is resolved: the "resolve without posting" action of (d). (j) "Post again" queues the job (a request's
transaction cannot roll back in part when the ledger refuses), so it answers `{ queued: true }`; the person sees the failure close, or
its reason change, on the list. (k) `FINANCE_POSTING_FAILED` is published by the worker and nothing consumes it yet: its bridge to the api
and the notification are 4B.6b with the sweep. (l) The failure row stores a reason, not WHICH role is unmapped (the rules know it,
the table has no column): the list says "role not mapped" and the person reads the mapping; a `detail` column with the role is 4B.6b.
(m) Specs still to write in 4B.6b with the sweep: the listener's event-to-job mapping, the `LEDGER_REFUSED` second transaction,
`markUnposted` on the last attempt, and two jobs of one order run in parallel (the advisory lock). (n) The organization of a store is read
on every event (one query) and posting jobs share the heavy queue (concurrency 2): a cache and a queue of their own when the volume asks
(4B.6b, with the sweep). (o) `dayInZone` is a second day-in-zone helper next to `civilDateOf` (`carrier-guide-rules.ts`): one of them
goes at the 7.4 cleanup. (p) The settings are read before the ledger takes its own lock: a close committed in between is a
`LEDGER_REFUSED` that "post again" clears, not a wrong entry.
(e) The transfer shortage written off (E9, third case) has no source row in the MVP: it posts when a transfer write-off exists (Step
4.5 debt). (f) The queued job's de-duplication id is not used on purpose (one id per source would swallow the second event of the same
order); the keys make a repeat harmless. (g) The posting runs after the commit of the source and the sweep (4B.6b) is what heals a lost
queue: until it exists a lost event costs an entry until someone presses "post again" on nothing, so 4B.6b must not slip past 4B.8.

**Decisions of PR 4B.6b-1 (rule 12):** (1) **E4 follows the TDD as written for every charge model**: gross, no input VAT, freight only when the
sender pays, the commission over the cash collected whoever pays (`commissionCents`, the function that estimates the expected amount of the
remittance, so the two never differ by a cent). The charge model of a connection (prepaid, collected in the remittance, invoiced) is NOT built
here: its prepaid case needs an account role that does not exist (the advance of guides) and the accountant chooses the account, so it is 4B.6b-3
with the purchase of prepaid guides, configurable and marked [ACCOUNTANT]; nothing is invented. (2) **E5 per line:** the cash is what the carrier
reported; what it kept is the file's own figure when the file has one, else the estimate E4 posted (only for a connection that deducts its fee,
`remittanceDeductsFee`); the receivable is cleared for reported plus kept; the payable E4 posted is settled up to what the carrier kept; what it kept beyond the estimate goes to `CARRIER_COMMISSION_EXPENSE` (the
file's figure wins over the estimate, TDD_17 §4.15), and what it did NOT keep stays owed (a carrier that invoices the guide apart is not wiped
out: rejected, taking back expense when the file shows less than the estimate). A line that differs clears only what the carrier reported and
kept, the rest stays open on the receivable. Rejected: clearing the receivable by the guide's amount (it would hide a shortfall). (3) **The payable of a guide is settled once:** a guide for which an
earlier confirmed (not voided) remittance already kept a fee takes only the figure of its own file in a later one; if the earlier file said the
carrier kept nothing, the later one may settle it. (4) **E5 waits for E4:** a guide
delivered after the start of the books whose E4 is not posted yet makes the remittance a `SOURCE_NOT_READY` failure (not an alarm), and the
posting of E4 asks the remittances of the guide again; a guide delivered before the start has no E4 (its charges are in the opening balance)
and uses the estimate read from the guide. (5) **E6 reverses E5 with an entry of the system** (`LedgerService.reverse` takes `createdBy: null`,
origin `system`), dated the day it was voided or the first day of the open period, never before the entry it reverses; a bank-reconciled E5 is
refused by the ledger and shows as a failure until the match is taken back. A remittance voided before its E5 was posted posts nothing, and a
late job to confirm a voided one posts nothing. (6) The destination account is checked twice: by the confirm route (an account of the
organization of the store, active, postable, cash-kind: another organization's is a 404) and by the posting service, because the account may be
switched off after the confirmation.
**Debts of PR 4B.6b-1:** (q) the charge model of a connection and its prepaid case (decision 1): 4B.6b-3. (r) E7, E8 and `FINANCE_VIEW_CARRIER_FEES`:
4B.6b-2. (s) The sweep of confirmed and voided remittances and of delivered guides with no E4/E5/E6: 4B.6b-3 (the listener queues them now, a lost
event waits for it). (t) A guide delivered before the start of the books that is remitted after it clears a payable the opening balance must hold:
the accountant's opening entry has to include the carriers' payable and receivable (owner and accountant, before the first remittance after the
start). (u) A remittance that is confirmed with a destination account and then voided keeps the column (the evidence of the choice); the reversal
uses the lines of E5, never the column. (v) E4 is posted for the guide of the outbound leg only; the charges of a return guide are 4B.6b-2 with E8. (w) Voiding an EARLIER remittance
of a guide that a LATER one settled again re-opens the payable the earlier one cleared, and the later entry (immutable, written knowing the
earlier one cleared it) does not clear it: the carriers' payable is overstated until an adjustment by hand (and the same two remittances give different payables depending on whether
the later one posted before or after the void). The recomputation of payables of 4B.6b-3's sweep flags it; the accountant adjusts. (x) The destination account of a confirmed remittance cannot be changed after the
confirmation: one switched off afterwards leaves E5 a failure ("account inactive" or "not cash") until it is reactivated; a route to re-point
it is 4B.6b-3. (y) The payable of a guide whose carrier kept less than the estimate stays open until the carrier's invoice is paid by hand
(`FinanceTransaction` expense): there is no payment of a carrier's payable in the MVP (4B.6b-3, with the charge model). (z) A guide delivered before E4 existed (before this PR deployed) has no E4 and nothing queues it: its remittance waits (`SOURCE_NOT_READY`)
until the sweep of 4B.6b-3 posts the missing E4 (as it does the E3 of every order delivered before 4B.6a). (aa) The refusal of a void for a
bank-reconciled E5 is the ledger's (tested in its spec); a spec of it through E6 and of the dating when E5's day is in a closed period goes with the
sweep's specs (debt (m) of 4B.6a), 4B.6b-3. (ab) Choosing the destination account asks `finance:move_money` (the permission's own comment says so) on top
of `remittances:manage`; the web (4B.9) shows the box only with it.

**Built in PR 4B.6b-2:** (E7) `POST /remittances/discrepancies/:shipmentId/write-off` (`remittances:manage` and, in the service, `finance:move_money`): the guide in
discrepancy gets the terminal `CodStatus.WRITTEN_OFF` (migration `cod_written_off`, which widens two CHECKs, with its rollback), the event
`REMITTANCE_DIFFERENCE_WRITTEN_OFF` queues the entry `shipment:<id>:write_off`, and the books work out the amount themselves: what the carrier had to
collect less what each confirmed remittance of the guide cleared (the settlement E5 made, `settleRemittanceLine`), Dr `COD_DIFFERENCES` · Cr
`RECEIVABLE_CARRIERS` with the carrier as the party (a surplus the other way round); it waits (`SOURCE_NOT_READY`) for the E3 and the E5 it clears
against. A remittance with a written-off guide cannot be voided. (E8) `return:<id>:restock` on `RETURN_RECEIVED` (the share of the revenue and the tax of
the units back, by the running total of units so the returns add up to the sale to the cent; Dr `SALES_RETURNS`, Dr `VAT_OUTPUT`, Cr the customer's
advance, or the carrier's receivable for a COD guide that will never be remitted; Dr `INVENTORY` · Cr `COST_OF_GOODS_SOLD` at the cost of the `RETURN_IN`
movements) and `order:<id>:return` on an order put back as a whole with no return row (before the sale only Dr `INVENTORY` · Cr
`INVENTORY_IN_TRANSIT`); E4 now also charges the guide of a return. `FINANCE_VIEW_CARRIER_FEES` (permission, Admin grant and labels existed since 4B.2) now
gates the commission and the rates of a connection in the answers of the carriers routes (hidden, and not changeable, without it) and the boxes of Settings →
Carriers; the labels of the roles matrix were checked in both languages (nothing missing).

**Decisions of PR 4B.6b-2 (rule 12):** (1) **The amount of E7 is the ledger's, never the request's:** chosen over a body with the amount (a person could write
off more than is owed) and over the difference of the shipment's columns (a fee the file reported differently from the estimate makes those columns differ
while the receivable is cleared). (2) **A written-off guide is terminal and its remittance cannot be voided:** rejected, voiding and letting E6 reopen the
receivable E7 cleared (the books would hold a receivable the guide cannot be matched to). (3) **The refund of a return is the customer's advance, not a cash
account:** a refund that pays money out is a person's decision (`finance:move_money`), so the books record what is owed and the payment is a transfer or an
expense by hand; rejected, picking a cash account for them (it would invent a cash movement). The carrier's receivable is credited only when the guide's COD
is `void` (the carrier will never remit). (4) **Pro rata on the running total of units**, half up, rejected: rounding each return on its own (the returns of a
sale would not add up to it). (5) **The shipping fee of a returned order is not reversed** (the order does not say it was given back), **except** when the carrier's receivable is cleared (a COD guide that will never be remitted) and the order is back in full: E3 debited that receivable for the whole total, so the shipping and its tax go with it or the balance would stay for good. (6) The cost put back is the
cost the `RETURN_IN` movement carries when it has one, else the cost its sale took the unit out at (the engine stores a unit that comes back with no cost, valued at the average of the level), so what E3 took out and E8 puts back match; a unit with neither is `COST_MISSING`; the discard of a damaged unit posts its own E9 loss.
(7) The write-off day is the day of the action (the job's `occurredAt`), the return's the day it was received.
**Debts of PR 4B.6b-2:** (ac) The refund benefit of a prepaid guide (Step 4.16: a guide given back, a count, no money) and the purchase and consumption of prepaid guides
need the account role of the advance of guides and the charge model: 4B.6b-3, with the accountant's choice. (ad) Which account pays out a refund and the entry that
pays it (Dr `CUSTOMER_ADVANCES` · Cr a cash account), and whether an exchange's credit is used by its replacement order: [ACCOUNTANT] and 4B.9 (the screen that chooses
it), until then it is a transfer or an expense by hand. (ae) The shipping fee of a returned order is not reversed (decision 5): [ACCOUNTANT], 4B.6b-3. (af) A
written-off guide cannot be un-written: the accountant's manual reversal of E7 undoes the books but the guide stays `written_off` and its remittance stays
unvoidable; a route that reverses both is 4B.6b-3 or 4B.9. (ag) A movement that does record a cost for a returned unit wins over the cost of the sale: the difference stays in the cost of goods sold, the sweep of 4B.6b-3 compares it. (ak) E7 and E8 wait (`SOURCE_NOT_READY`) for the E5, the sale or the E2 they work against and nothing asks them again when it posts (E4 does it for the remittance): a person's "post again" or the sweep of 4B.6b-3 heals it. (al) E7 takes what the carrier had to collect from the guide's `codAmountCents`, the same assumption E5 makes; an order edited after its guide leaves a residual the sweep of 4B.6b-3 flags. (an) The shipment and remittance views still answer the cost of a guide and the fee kept (`carrierCostCents`, `codExpectedCents`, `feeCents`) to who holds `shipping:view` or `remittances:view`: `finance:view_carrier_fees` gates what was agreed with a carrier (its commission and rates); hiding what each guide cost is Step 7.4 with the screens of 4B.9. (ao) A return received for some units and then an order put back as a whole is refused by the order (an order with returns holding units cannot be set to returned by hand), so the order's own entry never posts for it. (am) A return of a sale from before the books began reverses against the opening balance (contra-revenue and tax debits, the refund owed to the customer): the accountant's opening entry has to hold those sales' tax and receivable. (ah) An order returned before the sale whose units were not
put back posts nothing (the goods are lost in transit): the loss entry is the accountant's, 4B.6b-3. (ai) The button of the write-off and the fee boxes' message
for who cannot see them are 4B.9; the plugin route of the write-off waits for PR E6-2 (the plugin actor). (aj) The guide of a return is charged when it arrives:
a return guide of a prepaid model (consumes the advance) is 4B.6b-3 with the charge model.

**Decisions of PR 4B.6b-3 (rule 12):** (1) **The sweep asks, the job posts:** `RECONCILE_FINANCE` (heavy queue, one job per organization with books, 04:30 UTC,
job id by organization and day) finds the sources that should have an entry and have none and queues `POST_FINANCE_EVENT` for each; it never posts and never writes
outside the idempotency of that job. Rejected: posting inline from the sweep (a backlog would run in one night, in one worker, with no retry per source). (2) **A candidate
is classified by `FinancePostingService.preview`**, the same decision the job takes with nothing written (no lock, no failure row touched): a source the entry of which
would be written is queued; one the books cannot post and nobody was told of is queued so that the job records the failure a person reads; one already listed is left to the
person and counted. So the gauge counts what a job would post or fail on, not every delivered order. (3) **The window is 120 days back or the start of the books**, whichever is
later, oldest first, at most 500 sources per run (`FinanceSweepLimits`): a backlog drains over the days. (4) **E1 (a payment), E7 (a write-off) and the E8 of an order returned with no return row are NOT swept:** none has a date of its own (the job dates it by the day it
runs), and dating a late one by the last change of the row could post an entry that the opening balance already holds (a prepaid order from before the books, updated
since). The one that never reached the queue is on the list of failures (the listener marks it) and a person presses "post again". (5) **The balances are recomputed
from the lines** for every (account, store dimension, period) and compared with `account_period_balances`; a difference sets the gauge `FINANCE_BALANCE_MISMATCHES` (to how many there are now, so it goes back to zero when fixed; the TDD named a `_total` counter, a gauge is the right type
for a current count) and logs an error, and **nothing corrects it** (the journal is the truth; a correction is a person's decision). (6) **The failure notice** (`finance.posting_failed`, in-app and email) goes to whoever
holds `finance:manage_accounts` (the permission of "post again") in a store of the organization, once per person and source until read, in the first store they hold it in; it
names no amount and no source (the list of failures does), and a source that only waits (`SOURCE_NOT_READY`) is no alarm and no notice. The event crosses from the worker to the
api through the bridge. (7) **`FinanceCloseGuard.check`** answers what stands in the way of a close: open failures by reason, sources the sweep would queue, whether it was
truncated; any of them blocks. It is about the whole organization, not one period (a failure row carries no date of its source). 4B.8's close calls it; it reads and never posts.
**Debts of PR 4B.6b-3:** (am) The close itself is 4B.8: the guard is there for it, nothing refuses a close until that step exists. (an) A failure row carries no date of its
source, so the guard also stops an earlier close for a later period's failure: a `sourceDate` column, 4B.8. (ao) E1 healing needs a payment date on the order (a column
and its migration, Step 4.3's owner): until then a lost payment event is a failure a person posts again. (ap) The sweep reads by `updatedAt`/`deliveredAt` with
Prisma pages, not an anti-join: fine for the MVP's volume, a raw `NOT EXISTS` on `journal_entries.idempotency_key` when an organization has tens of thousands of orders in
the window: Step 7.3. (aq) A write-off swept late is dated by the shipment's last change, not by the action's day (the action leaves no date of its own): [ACCOUNTANT], the
first open day anyway. (ar) The comparisons of `INVENTORY` with `InventoryLevel.valueCents` (with the tolerance of debt (h) of 4B.6a) and of `RECEIVABLE_CARRIERS` with
the open guides (the carriers' receivable is gross, the guide's expected amount is net of the fee) are not built: they need the tolerance and the owner's rule for what a
difference means; 4B.6b-4 or 4B.8. (as) The metric `FINANCE_POSTING_FAILURES` counts the events the api receives; a second api instance counts its own, as the other bridged
counters do. (at) Specs still to write: the sweep's cap with several kinds of source, and E6's dating in a closed period (debt (aa) of 4B.6b-1). (au) **4B.6b-4:** the charge
model of a connection and the prepaid purchase and consumption of guides: an account role for the advance of guides that the accountant chooses, off by default and marked
[ACCOUNTANT]; with debts (ac), (ae), (aj) of 4B.6b-2.
- [x] **Fix PR `sale-after-refund` (QA 2026-11-16, HC-105 point 2, AUT-R2-010; no step number).** An order paid (E1 posted) whose payment became `REFUNDED` (a return after delivery marks it so, and so does a
  refund before delivery) left its sale (E3) as `source_not_ready` for ever, with no alarm. `loadSale` now treats `REFUNDED` like `COMPLETED`: with E1 in the books the sale clears the advance as always (the money WAS received;
  E8 reverses the sale and E14 of the fix `refund-entry` settles the refund); without E1 the failure is the new reason `payment_refunded`: an alarm (notification, failure row) that the sweep does not retry, because
  waiting changes nothing (E1 posts only a completed payment). Files: `finance-constants.ts`, `finance-posting.service.ts`, `finance-auto-entries.spec.ts`. **Decisions (rule 12):** (1) **Recognize when E1 exists.** Rejected:
  failing every `REFUNDED` sale (it blocks the common case, a sale delivered and then returned before its job ran, and E8 waits for that sale). With E14 the books are consistent in both orders: a refund before
  delivery leaves `CUSTOMER_ADVANCES` with a debit balance that is exactly what the customer owes for the goods. (2) **Alarm, not wait, without E1.** **Depends on** PR `refund-entry` (E14): merge after it. **Debts:**
  (a) **[ACCOUNTANT]** a debit balance in the advance account for goods delivered after a refund (a receivable account is not built, TDD_18 §4.2 E3); (b) `payment_refunded` has no way out: a payment cannot leave
  `REFUNDED`, so a "dismiss with a reason" action on the failure list is needed, Step 4B.8b-4 or 7.3 (until then it blocks the close of the organization, as `source_not_ready` did silently); (c) the failure list shows
  the raw reason code (no reason has a translated label in the web yet): Step 4B.9; (d) a cash on delivery order refunded after delivery is decided before this branch (its sale posts against the carrier), and with
  `recognizeSaleOn = shipped` the moment is the shipping, not the delivery: both unchanged.
- [x] **Fix `fix/fiscal-list-receiver-mask` (QA 2026-11-16, HC-206 / FIS-092; rule 12).** The document list and detail showed the full name of the receiver and masked only the tax id; with `fiscal:view` alone a person read the name of every customer. `maskPersonName` (`fiscal-rules.ts`) now shows the first letter of each word (`Maria Receptora` -> `M**** R********`); `complete` is still read from the real name. Proved by `fiscal-rules.spec.ts` and the list and detail case of `tests/api/fiscal-documents.spec.ts`. Decisions: the name is masked in both the list and the detail (the finding named the list; the detail leaked the same), as D-39 of the questions says ("mask the name"); the full fiscal name stays visible only in the customer's fiscal data, behind `fiscal:view_customer_data`. Debt (Step 7.4): the evidence file in the bucket still holds the receiver in the clear until the bucket is encrypted (the other half of D-39) [OWNER].
- [x] **Fix PR `refund-entry` (QA 2026-11-16, HC-105 point 1, AUT-R2-013; no step number: a defect found by reading and by running).** A return completed with `refundAmountCents`
  moved the order's payment to `REFUNDED` and left the books with the customer's advance still owed, and the money already out of the bank. New entry **E14** (`return_refund`, key `return:<id>:refund`, queued by
  `Events.RETURN_REFUND_RECORDED`, published in the commit of the completion): Dr `CUSTOMER_ADVANCES` · Cr the account the order's payment method receives into, for exactly the amount the person
  recorded. Files: `finance-posting-constants.ts`, `return-entry-rules.ts` (`refundLines`), `finance-posting.service.ts` (`loadReturnRefund`, `paymentAccountOf`), `finance-posting.listener.ts`, `finance-books.service.ts` (the returns-not-listed warning skips E14),
  `returns.service.ts`, TDD_18 §4.2 and their specs. **Decisions (rule 12):** (1) **The amount the person recorded is the amount that left,** never a figure computed from the sale: what E8 owed and what was paid can differ
  (a retention) and the books follow the money. Rejected: crediting the bank inside E8 (the refund is recorded when the return is completed, after E8 posts, and may be partial or absent). (2) **The account is the one the payment method
  receives into** (`PaymentMethodAccount`, the store's own over the organization's); cash on delivery has no such account, so its refund is paid from `BANK_DEFAULT`. A missing or inactive account is a failure a person reads
  (`payment_account_missing`, `account_inactive`), never a guess. Rejected: asking the person for the account on the completion screen (a new field and screen for an answer the books already know; it is debt (a) if the accountant wants it).
  (3) **E14 does not wait for E8:** the advance it settles is E1's (a parcel that never became a sale) or E8's, and the account is the same either way. (4) **What the customer keeps back stays in `CUSTOMER_ADVANCES`:** a refund of 800 against 901
  owed leaves 101 credit, never an invented income [ACCOUNTANT]. **Debts:** (a) **[ACCOUNTANT]** which account pays a refund (the method's, as built, or always a chosen one) and whether COD refunds go to the default bank; closes debt (ad) of 4B.6b-2 in the part
  that was the entry, not the account. (b) **[ACCOUNTANT]** what a retention (refund below what E8 owed) is: income, a fee, or a liability until the customer claims it; today it stays in the advance. (c) Whoever paid a refund by hand before this
  change (a transfer or an expense) now has the advance debited twice: a reversal of that manual entry, by the accountant, for each refund recorded since 4B.6b-2. (d) The memo `auto:return_refund` has no translated label in the web yet
  (none of the `auto:` memos has one): Step 4B.9. (e) **E14 is not swept** (no completion date on the return, and refunds from before E14 may be booked by hand: the sweep would post them twice); one that never reached the queue is a failure a person posts again. A column `completedAt` on `OrderReturn` would allow it: Step 7.3.
  (f) E14 type is `sale_return` (no migration); the legal books' warning skips it by memo. A dedicated type needs a migration of the CHECK and its rollback: Step 7.3. (g) A refund above what E8 or E1 left in the advance (the person gives back more than the units returned) leaves `CUSTOMER_ADVANCES` with a debit balance: the books follow the money; a guard in `settle` that ties the refund to the units back is a decision of the owner and the accountant. (h) A refund is read from the row when the job runs: nothing else writes `refundAmountCents`, and a change after posting is the accountant's reversal.
  (i) A refund recorded for a return whose order is `REFUNDED` before delivery leaves E3 as `source_not_ready` (HC-105 point 2) and a prepaid order cancelled after E1
  has no entry (HC-105 point 3): the next PRs of the fix `refund-entry` series, named in this list when they open.

- [x] **Fix of the sale of an order with nothing to collect (QA 2026-11-16, HC-138; rule 12 decisions and debts with their owners).** E1 writes nothing for an order whose total is zero (there is no money to receive), and E3 required that E1 entry for every paid order that is not cash on delivery, so the sale of a replacement of an exchange (delivered, paid, total 0 because the credit of the return covers it) stayed `source_not_ready` for good: no sale entry, attempts growing, and the close of the period refused for the whole organization (`FINANCE_CLOSE_PENDING_POSTINGS`). The same held for any order with a full discount. **Decided (A):** when the total of the order is zero, `loadSale` has no advance to clear and none is missing, so it posts with the rules it already has (revenue, tax and cost as the order recorded them, a zero debit): for a replacement covered by the credit that is only the cost of what left. For any order whose total is zero, paid or not and cash on delivery or not (nobody owes anything: no advance, no receivable, no credit sale); any other total keeps its rule (a paid order with a total and no E1 still waits, an unpaid one is a sale on credit, cash on delivery needs its carrier). **Rejected (B):** consume the advance that the return of the exchange credited and recognize the revenue and the output tax of the replacement (Dr advances 1130, Cr revenue 1000, Cr output tax 130 for a 1130 exchange): it is a decision about the tax of an exchange, which TDD_18 does not make (E8 says only that an exchange has its own credit note, §8), so it is the accountant's. `tests/api/finance-exchange-posting.spec.ts` holds the cases (same value with the tax included and excluded, for less, for more, a full discount, the close guard not blocked) and one that **pins the known residue** so that nobody takes it for right. **Left, each with its owner:** (a) **the residue of an exchange in the books:** after the return (E8) and the replacement, the advances keep +$11.30 that nothing consumes and the output tax nets to -$1.30 for a product the customer was not charged twice for; closing it needs the replacement to record how much of the return credit it used (today only `discountCents`) and the accountant's rule: **question for the accountant: "accounting and VAT treatment of a product exchange"** (which entry the replacement posts, whether the credit consumed is revenue with output tax, and what the fiscal document of the exchange says), owner **Step 4B.8b-4** (the accountant's) with the accountant's answer, and written there too; (b) **the QA cases TAX-600/601 (the replacement has tax 0 and total 0) and TAX-602 (the net output tax of the sale, the return and the replacement is 0) contradict each other** until that answer exists: the first two describe the order as it is stored, the third what the books must show, and both cannot hold without (a); (c) the replacement stays a normal order for E3: nothing marks an order as the replacement of an exchange, which (a) will need; **the close of a period is no longer blocked by this case, and a closed period cannot be corrected, so a month closed before the accountant answers carries the residue of (a) and is fixed by an adjustment in a later period**: the owner is told in the PR, and until (a) is built the exchanges of the month are listed by the returns of type exchange; (d) an order whose total changes after it was paid keeps its advance on the books because the sale debits its new total (already so before this fix), and a total-0 order with no cost writes no sale entry at all, so a return or a write-off that waits for that entry waits for good: both go to Step 7.3 with the case of the order that is edited after payment; (e) the rule is a branch of `loadSale` that reuses the advance collection with a zero debit: a `none` collection in the pure rules (`saleLines`) is the cleaner shape, with its own unit test, left to Step 7.3.

**Fix PR `remittance-fee-guard` (HC-001 of the QA of 2026-11-16, AUT-523/529/530/531; no step number: a defect of E5 found by reading).** E5 credited the
receivable of a guide for what the carrier reported plus what it **kept**, and what it kept was the fee of the file (or the estimate of E4) with no bound: a
file fee of 30.00 on a guide of 25.99 with nothing remitted cleared 30.00 of the 25.99 the carrier had to collect (the receivable ended at -4.01), and the same
happened for a carrier that does not deduct its fee but lists it next to the whole cash, for a guide remitted in parts, and for a cash on delivery smaller than the
guide the sender pays (2.00 collected, guide of 3.50). `settleRemittanceLine` now takes the gross the carrier had to collect and what the earlier confirmed
remittances of the guide already cleared, and splits what the carrier charged (`keptCents`: still all of it expense and payable it settles) into what it could take
out of the cash (`deductedCents`, at most `max(0, gross - cleared before - reported)`, which is what clears the receivable) and the rest (`owedCents`, a credit on the
payable of the carrier, netted with the debit that settles E4's payable: one line). E7 reads `deductedCents` too, so the write-off of a guide never counts a fee the cash
did not cover. Files: `carrier-entry-rules.ts`, `return-entry-rules.ts`, `finance-posting.service.ts` (both call sites), their specs and the two integration suites.
**Decisions (rule 12):** (1) **The charge is accepted and bounded, not rejected.** Rejected: (A) refuse the confirmation of a remittance whose fee or reported amount is
above the cash (it breaks the surplus of E7, TDD_18 §4.2 "as built", and a legitimate case: the sender pays a guide larger than a small cash on delivery, which
`lineExpectedCents` already clamps at zero); (C) A plus a warning in the import preview (same cost, and the line is still unusable). (2) **A surplus by REPORTED amount
is unchanged:** a carrier that reports more than it had to collect is still written off by E7 (a surplus), but with nothing taken out of the cash for its fee, so the
surplus in the spec of E7 went from 4.98 to 0.85 (reported 26.00 on a guide of 25.15). (3) What the cash could not cover is owed to the carrier, exactly as a fee the
carrier did not keep already is (`settleRemittanceLine`, "what it did NOT keep stays owed"): no new account, no invented figure. **Debts and questions (rule 12):**
(av) **[ACCOUNTANT]** a remittance whose fee is above what the carrier collected: is the excess a payable to the carrier (what is built) or something else? (4B.6b-4,
with the charge model and TDD_18 §13). (aw) **[OWNER]** AUT-530: a carrier that reports MORE than it collected is a surplus without limit today (a typed 5,000.00 on a
guide of 25.99 is accepted and left to E7): should the surplus have a ceiling, and what does the import do above it? (4B.6b-4 or 7.3). (ax) The web (Step 4B.9) draws the
fee of the line from the file; it does not say that part of it was not taken out of the cash: the remittance screen and the carrier statement should show the part owed
(4B.9).
(HC-103, fix/remittance-rec-needs-sale) E5 now waits for E3 like E7 (`ordersAwaitingSale`: a sale recognized before the books began never waits); the sale posting re-asks the remittances of the order's guides. Debt: a spec that posts E3 after a waiting E5 and sees it post by itself (needs a full sold order in `finance-carrier-entries.spec.ts`; the order builder of `finance-return-entries.spec.ts` has it): 4B.8b-2c. An order that never posts a sale (cancelled) leaves its remittance on the failure list, visible, until a person resolves it (a cancelled order, or one whose `deliveredAt` is not set, has no E3: the wait is the alarm, and the failure row holds the period close). Known limits: the failure row names the remittance, not the orders that lack a sale; specs for the cancelled and no-`deliveredAt` waits: 4B.8b-2c.
(ay) E5 and E7 replay the current rows of a guide's remittances (confirmed ones, in the order they were confirmed) to know what each cleared; they do not read the
posted entries. A remittance voided or re-confirmed AFTER a later one posted changes what a later write-off replays (the same family as debt (w) of 4B.6b-1): the fix is to
keep per line what E5 cleared, with the remittance entry; 4B.6b-4 or 4B.8. (az) The bound uses the guide's `codAmountCents` as the gross, the assumption E5 and E7 already
made (debt (al) of 4B.6b-2); a guide whose cash was edited after E3 or whose receivable E8 credited (a COD guide that will never be remitted) is not bounded by the ledger's
figure: with (ay), 4B.6b-4. (ba) What the cash could not cover is a credit on `PAYABLE_CARRIERS` with the carrier as the party and no marker of its own (memo or role): a later
invoice or an E4 correction cannot tell it from the estimate; the accountant's choice of account for it is (av), 4B.6b-4.
(bb) E5 entries posted BEFORE this fix stay as they were (the journal is immutable): a guide whose fee was cleared above the cash keeps its negative receivable, and an E7 on it
replays the new rule, so it finds nothing open and posts nothing. The accountant corrects those by hand (a manual entry); this is not repeated for new remittances. (bc) The
replay of a guide's earlier remittances uses the connection's CURRENT `remittanceDeductsFee`, the current E4 estimate and the current `codAmountCents`, not the values in force when
each posted: with (ay), a flag flipped between two remittances of one guide changes what a later one or an E7 counts as cleared (4B.6b-4, with the stored per-line figure of (ay)).
(bd) A guide the carrier remitted in full on a connection that deducts its fee, with no fee column in the file, takes nothing out of the cash (none is left): the estimate stays owed on
the payable, and the guide counts as having had its fee listed, so a later remittance of it does not settle that payable again; it is paid by hand (debt (y) of 4B.6b-1). The `earlier`
query reads the full history of each guide in the file under the lock of the books: fine at this volume, to be replaced by the stored per-line figure of (ay) (Step 7.3).
**Rejected in the review:** to write the part owed as a line of its own next to the payable settled (the entry has one line per account and carrier, not one per guide, so a per-guide
trace is not in the ledger either way; the replay is where it lives, see (ay)); to mark the payable of a guide as not settled when part of its fee was owed (that part cannot be
settled by a later remittance, there is no cash left in the receivable to take it out of: a payable the carrier invoices is paid by hand, debt (y) of 4B.6b-1).

- **The step is delivered in four PRs (decided by the session of 4B.7a and 4B.7b-1, rule 12, because the first plan of ~65 files cannot be reviewed in batches of 8 to 10 for a very-high-risk area):** **4B.7a-1** the libraries and the rule (this PR); **4B.7a-2** the database, the lifecycle of the document of a sale, the queue, the routes and the permissions; **4B.7b** credit notes, the evidence as media and the customer's fiscal data.
- **Built in PR 4B.7a-1 (the port, the simulator and the rule; no database, no route; high risk because it is the contract of fiscal documents):** `libs/fiscal/sdk` (the port `FiscalDocumentProvider`: `validateIssuer`, `build` (pure), `submit`, `consult`, `void`, the manifest with the document types and the fields a type asks of the receiver, an idempotency key on every call), `libs/fiscal/simulator` (the provider for development and test: it accepts, refuses, goes unavailable or loses its answer by the tax id of the receiver; it never talks to an authority) and `libs/fiscal/runtime` (the registry of the providers a deployment has, the pure rules of the lifecycle (`fiscal-rules.ts`: the transition table, what is immutable, who can edit the receiver, masking) and the composition root `official-providers.ts`, the one file that imports a provider package; the simulator is registered only when `NODE_ENV` is not production). The constants of the lifecycle are in `libs/core/domain/fiscal-constants.ts` (statuses, the transition table, environments, `issueOn`, limits, the job options). The contract suite `tests/contracts/fiscal-provider.contract.ts` is what every provider passes, the simulator today and the real one later. `validate:fiscal-agnostic` (CI, pre-push, `validate:all`; `scripts/fiscal-agnostic-baseline.json`, which can only shrink) freezes the knowledge of a country's document, its authority or a provider outside `libs/fiscal/<provider>`. The log redaction list gained the fiscal fields (`taxId`, `registrationId`, their snake_case twins and `certificate`). The boundaries of nx (`scope:fiscal-sdk`, `scope:fiscal`, `scope:fiscal-runtime`) keep core from importing any of them.
- **Decisions of PR 4B.7a-1 (rule 12):** (1) the port lives in its own libs and core never imports them: the runtime joins the port, the providers and core, as the plugins runtime does (rejected: the lifecycle in `libs/core`, which would force core to know the port). (2) The type of a document is the provider's rule applied when it builds; core never branches on it. (3) the idempotency key is per submission, not per document, so a corrected document is never answered with its cached rejection; the answers of the port are one shape per outcome so that an accepted document always has its number; the simulator keeps no state, and is registered only when `NODE_ENV` is development or test. (4) `consult` joins the port of `TDD_18 §8.1`: a submission whose answer was lost is asked about before it is sent again, so it never makes two documents (rejected: relying on the idempotency key alone, which a real authority may not honor). (5) The sentence of rule 13 for fiscal documents is not written in `CLAUDE.md` (it is the owner's file); the ratchet already enforces it.
- **Left by PR 4B.7a-1 (rule 12), with the PR that closes each:** **4B.7a-2:** the migration with its rollback (`fiscal_issuers`, `fiscal_documents` with a `submission` counter that makes the idempotency key (`organization:document:submission`) new when a refused document is fixed and resubmitted, the trigger that makes an accepted document immutable), the order's `discountCents` passed to the provider, the reason of a provider cut to `FiscalLimits.REASON_MAX_LENGTH` and its `response` capped in size before they are stored (a provider may copy the authority's body), the `submission` counter moves only when the authority refused the document (a rejection that core raised before it reached the provider keeps the key), every call to a provider awaited inside a try (a provider may throw before it returns a promise), the job with a `jobId` per document and submission, a check that the lines, the shipping tax and the discount add up to the order's total and tax before a document is built (the provider never sees an inconsistent sale), a receiver that is editable only while the document is refused or has never been sent (`receiverEditable(status, attempts)`), the lifecycle service (document queued on the sale, the claim under a row lock, accepted, rejected, unavailable goes back to the queue, void through the provider), the job `SUBMIT_FISCAL_DOCUMENT` with its retries, the routes `/fiscal/*` with `FISCAL_VIEW` and `FISCAL_MANAGE` (and `fiscal:` out of `PermissionsOfUnbuiltAreas`), the audit actions, the error codes, the `FISCAL_DOCUMENT_REJECTED` event, `VOID_FISCAL_DOCUMENT` (HIGH tier), both coverage maps, the isolation cases with a mutant and the test cleanup. **4B.7b:** the credit note of a return linked to the original; the document and the response as `Media` evidence; the customer's fiscal data on the order and the customer (encrypted); the notification of `FISCAL_DOCUMENT_REJECTED` and its bridge. **Step 4B.8:** the daily check of a document against its entry joins `RECONCILE_FINANCE`, with the sweep of documents left queued. **Step 4B.9 PR D:** the screens. **Waits for the owner and the accountant (debt (c) of 4B.1, unchanged):** the real provider package (`libs/fiscal/sv`), the owner's registration as an issuer, the signing certificate and the credentials of the test and real environments, and the accountant's confirmation of the document types and the format: nothing of that was invented. **Proposal for the owner, not applied (it edits `CLAUDE.md`):** the text of rule 13 for fiscal documents.
- **Built in PR 4B.7a-2 (the database, the lifecycle of the document of a sale, the queue, the routes and the permissions; very high risk: fiscal documents of customers and of the store):** the migration `20261222100000_fiscal_documents` with its rollback (`fiscal_issuers`: provider id as data, credentials sealed like a carrier's, `next_sequence`; `fiscal_documents`: one per order and organization, the sealed receiver, the snapshots of the issuer and of the lines, `submission` and `attempts`, CHECKs of the values and of the amounts, a trigger that makes an accepted document immutable (only the status to voided and the void fields change), refuses its delete and its truncate, and a trigger that ties the order to the store and the organization of the document); `FiscalIssuerService` (the issuer of the organization: validated by its provider, written with the credentials never read back, the audit names the fields only) and `FiscalDocumentsService` (the document made on the sale event, the claim under a row lock, accepted, rejected, back to the queue when the authority does not answer, the receiver fixed by a person, retry, void through the provider) in `libs/fiscal/runtime`; the job `SUBMIT_FISCAL_DOCUMENT` (ids only; job id `submit-fiscal-document-<document>-<submission>`; attempts and backoff of `fiscalJobOptions`) on the heavy queue and its processor branch; `apps/api/src/modules/fiscal` (the listener of `ORDER_STATUS_CHANGED` at shipped or delivered by the issuer's `issueOn`, the queue producer, the routes `/fiscal/providers`, `/fiscal/issuer`, `/fiscal/documents` (list, by id, receiver, retry, void) with `FISCAL_VIEW` and `FISCAL_MANAGE`); `fiscal:` out of `PermissionsOfUnbuiltAreas`; the audit actions, the error codes with their texts in es and en, the event `FISCAL_DOCUMENT_REJECTED`, `VOID_FISCAL_DOCUMENT` in the HIGH tier; both coverage maps; the isolation cases of `fiscalIssuer` and `fiscalDocument` with a mutant; `tests/api/fiscal-documents.spec.ts`, the specs of the rules and of the processor, and the worker module spec that builds the real module.
- **Decisions of PR 4B.7a-2 (rule 12):** (1) **One PR of 40 files**, not two: about 15 of them are one-line constants, maps and messages, and a split would leave the lifecycle service, the part to review hardest, without its routes and its tests (rejected: 4B.7a-2 migration, issuer and routes, and 4B.7a-3 the lifecycle; it cost a second queue turn and a half-built step on `main`). It was reviewed in batches of 10 files at most. (2) **The idempotency key is per submission** (`organization:document:submission`): the counter moves only when the authority refused the document, so a corrected document is a new submission with a new key and a new job id, and a refusal that core raised before the provider was reached keeps the key and the count of attempts. (3) **The provider is asked before it is told again** (`consult` when attempts is above 0) and every call to it is awaited inside a try: what a provider throws is not kept, it may carry the receiver. (4) **The provider never sees an inconsistent sale:** the lines, the shipping tax, the discount and the total are checked against each other (`saleAddsUp`) before it is built; a sale that does not add up is refused with `sale_inconsistent` for a person to look at. (5) **A provider's reason is cut to 500 characters and its response to 16,000** (a note says it was cut, never half of it). (6) **The correlative is configurable and moves forward only** (`nextSequence` of the issuer, one number per document, unique per organization): the format of a legal correlative is the provider's and the accountant's, so core keeps a plain integer and invents nothing. (7) **The receiver is the order's data** (name, email, phone, shipping address) and is editable only while the document is refused or has never been sent (`receiverEditable`); a refused document stays editable after the authority refused it (the new submission gets a new key). (8) **The document keeps the issuer it was made with** (provider, environment, identity): an issuer changed after that is refused with `issuer_changed` and a retry makes the document again with the issuer as it is, and an accepted document is invalidated only with the provider and the environment that accepted it. (9) **The built document is sealed** (`built_payload_encrypted`), because it holds the receiver's name, tax id and address; the authority's `response` is kept as the provider returns it, capped, and a provider must not copy the receiver into it. `providerData` is capped like the response and must not hold the receiver either. What cannot be stored of an acceptance (a cycle, a NUL) is replaced by a note and never makes the acceptance fail. What the authority answers to an invalidation is kept in its own column (`void_response`), because the accepted row cannot change. (10) **A document claimed less than five minutes ago is alive**: another attempt waits (its job fails and the queue asks again) and one whose worker died is taken over; what an attempt that was taken over decides is not written. Every call to a provider is bounded to a minute (well under the lease) and a failure is logged by name only. The invalidation uses a new key each time. A consultation that gets no answer puts the document back in the queue and never counts as "never received". (11) **The issue date is the moment the document was made** (`created_at`), the same on every attempt, so a document built twice is the same document; a provider that wants another date rule (a retry weeks later) says so when the accountant answers. A change of the issuer's identity (tax id, name, registration, establishment, address, environment) is also `issuer_changed`, and a change of environment or provider asks for new credentials. (12) **A refusal that core raised before anything was sent gives its attempt back**, so a document that never left core never reads as one that may be at the authority; a retry of a sale that did not add up reads the order again. The text a provider returns is cleaned of what the database refuses (a NUL, a lone surrogate, in values and in keys). The issuer is read, guarded and written under one lock of its row. (13) **An issuer that issues at SHIPPED also makes the document at DELIVERED** when the order had no shipped event (one document per order). (14) **Rejected foreign keys:** every key of a document is RESTRICT, so a document blocks the deletion of its store, order or organization (legal evidence; the retention rule is with the accountant, Step 7.2).
- **Left by PR 4B.7a-2 (rule 12), with the PR that closes each:** **4B.7b:** the credit note of a return linked to the original; the document and the response as `Media` evidence; the customer's fiscal data on the order and the customer (encrypted); the notification of `FISCAL_DOCUMENT_REJECTED` and its bridge to the api (the event is raised and nothing listens). **Step 4B.8:** the sweep of sales that have no document at all (the listener runs in process and logs its failure: a blip of the database at the moment of the sale leaves none), the daily check of a document against its sale entry, and the sweep of documents left QUEUED (the attempts of the job ran out while the authority was down) or SUBMITTED (the worker died after the claim): today a person retries a QUEUED one from the route, and a SUBMITTED one has no route (the job takes over after the lease); the sale entry is linked when the document is accepted and `journalEntryId` stays null when the entry posts later. **Step 4B.9 PR D:** the screens (the coverage map says so). **4B.7b:** the replacement of a voided document (one row per order and organization today, so a voided document leaves the order with none: the credit note and the replacement are made together). **4B.7b, the port:** `void` has no consultation like `submit` (an invalidation whose answer was lost may already be at the authority, and the document stays ACCEPTED here): the port gains a consultation for it, and the invalidation takes a claim on the row like the submission does; today one key per document and reason keeps a double click one invalidation for a provider that honours the key. **4B.7b, a document that may be at an issuer that was changed** (an attempt was sent and not answered, then the provider, the environment or the identity of the issuer changed) is not moved by a retry (409 with `FISCAL_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`): a person decides it with the accountant. **Known limit, Step 7.3:** a claim has no owner token, so an attempt that was taken over after its lease and then answers late can requeue or skip a decision of the new one; the timeout of a provider call makes it rare, and the skipped decision is logged with the document id. **Step 7.2:** retention of documents and the deletion of a store with documents. **Step 7.3:** the list reads the sealed receiver of every row of a page to mask it (a column for the masked tax id would avoid it at volume). **Waits for the owner and the accountant (unchanged):** the real provider package, the registration as an issuer, the certificate, the credentials of both environments, the document types and the format, and the default of `issueOn` (delivered) until TDD_18 §13 row 3 is answered.
- **4B.7b is two PRs (decided by the session of 4B.7b-1, rule 12; the first plan, credit notes, replacement, evidence as media, customer fiscal data, the notification and two changes of the port, is far over the ~40 files that can be reviewed in batches for a very-high-risk area):** **4B.7b-1** the credit note of a return and the replacement of a voided document (the schema that lets an order have more than one document); **4B.7b-2** the evidence as media, the customer's fiscal data, the notification of `FISCAL_DOCUMENT_REJECTED`, the consultation for `void` and the document that may be at an issuer that was changed.
- **Built in PR 4B.7b-1 (the credit note of a return and the replacement of a voided document; very high risk: fiscal documents of customers and of the store):** the migration `20261223100000_fiscal_credit_notes` with its rollback (additive: `kind`, `return_id`, `parent_document_id`, `replaces_document_id`; every document that exists stays a sale document; the unique index of one document per order becomes partial indexes: one live sale document per order, one live credit note per return, one per order that came back as a whole, one replacement per voided document; CHECKs of what each kind may carry; the immutability trigger now guards the new columns; the scope trigger checks that the return, the original and the replaced document belong to the order, the store and the organization, and also on an update of those columns); the port gained `FiscalBuildInput.kind` and `credited` (the accepted document a note cancels: its type, number, date and the provider's own data), the simulator builds its credit-note type for a note and the contract suite has a case for it; `creditNoteSaleOf` (pure: the units of a return with the revenue and the tax the books gave them, `reversalLinesOf` in `libs/core/finance`, the same running total of units that posts the entry of the return, so the note and the entry agree to the cent) and `originalStateOf`; `FiscalDocumentsService.createCreditNoteForReturn`, `createCreditNoteForOrder` (an order that came back as a whole with no return row) and `replace`; the listener makes the note on `RETURN_RECEIVED` and on the order's change to returned; `POST /fiscal/documents/:id/replace` (`FISCAL_MANAGE`); the audit action `FISCAL_DOCUMENT_REPLACED`; both coverage maps; `tests/api/fiscal-credit-notes.spec.ts`.
- **Fix HC-107 (the cent of a credit note; PR `fix/fiscal-credit-note-split`).** `reversalLinesOf` (the one split of the books that the entry E8 and the credit note read) now splits each line on the running total of what the units stood for (net and tax together) and the tax on its own running total, half up, the net being the rest: 2 units at 10.00 with 15 % included give 10.00 + 10.00 (before: 10.01 + 9.99 in the entry and 10.00 + 9.99 in the notes, a cent short of the sale; this replaces the \"known limit\" of 4B.7b-1 below). Net and tax of each part may differ by a cent from rounding each alone; the whole line still adds up to the cent and the last return absorbs the rest. Decisions: chosen, rounding the gross share (what the customer paid) instead of the net; rejected, letting the note credit a cent over the unit price (a document that does not add up, `saleAddsUp`) and a special last-note adjustment (two rules for one split). **[ACCOUNTANT] C-05 to confirm:** half up per line with the last return absorbing the remainder, a difference of at most one cent between net and tax of a part. A line so small that the new split would give a part a negative net (5 cents of net over 7 units) keeps the old independent split (decided by the line alone, so all its returns agree). **Debt (found in the review):** an order partly returned BEFORE this change keeps the old split in its posted entry and credit note; the return after the change is split with the new rule over the whole line, so such an order can reverse or credit one cent more than the sale (2 units at 10.00: 10.01 posted, then 10.00). Only orders with a return received before this PR and a remaining odd-cent line are touched; the books and the notes already issued are never edited. Owner: the accountant's review of 4B.8b-4 (a one-cent adjustment entry by hand, if one is found). Also left: the sale entry (E3) splits net and tax per line by its own rule, so a per-line comparison with the return side can differ by a cent; only the totals are compared (`entryMismatches`).
- **Decisions of PR 4B.7b-1 (rule 12):** (1) **A credit note is a row of the same table** with `kind` and a link to its original (rejected: a table of its own, which would copy the lifecycle, the lock, the queue, the immutability and the isolation). (2) **A note is made only when the sale has a document that is not voided** (nothing to cancel otherwise; rejected: a note with no original, which no authority accepts), and **goes only after the original is accepted**: while it is on its way the job of the note fails and the queue asks again, nothing is claimed (rejected: sending the note and letting the authority refuse it). A note whose original was voided is refused with `original_voided`, and a retry names the sale document that is live then. (3) **The receiver of a note is the one of the document it cancels**, read when the note is sent and not editable on the note (rejected: a receiver of its own, which could differ from the original's). (4) **The amounts are the books' own** (the same split by line and running total as the entry of the return), and a return that does not fit its sale (more units back than were sold, a sale with no tax snapshot) is made as a REJECTED note with `return_inconsistent`, the event raised and a retry that recomputes, so a person sees it (rejected: skipping it in silence, which the daily check of 4B.8 would only find later). (5) **The shipping fee is not credited**: the books do not give it back either, except in the case of a carrier receivable ([ACCOUNTANT], TDD_18 §13), and a legal document must not say more than the entry. (6) **A sale document with a credit note live at the authority (accepted, or sent and not answered) cannot be voided**: the notes go first, then the sale, then `replace` makes the sale again and **makes a note against it for every return the order has received that has no live note** (the ones voided with the old document and the ones received while the sale had none), so a return is never left without its note. A note that is only waiting or was refused does not block the void (it would make the sale unvoidable, since only an accepted document can be voided): it is refused when sent for a voided original and a person retries it after the replacement. (6b) **`replace` has no confirmation tier** (rejected: a HIGH tier like `void`): it creates a document, the destructive step is the void that came before; a failure to queue the new documents is logged and leaves them QUEUED for a person to retry from their route. (6c) **A note made REJECTED at birth (`return_inconsistent`) takes a correlative** (the column is not null and unique): a gap in the numbering that the accountant may have to explain; the alternative, no row at all, hides the return from the person. (7) **`replace` is for a voided sale document and takes the order as it is now, with the receiver the voided one had**; the new document has a new number (a voided document is never edited, and a number is never used twice). (8) **The foreign keys between documents are NO ACTION**, checked at the end of the statement, so the cleanup of a test or of a retention rule removes a document and its notes in one statement (the rest of the keys of a document stay RESTRICT).
- **Left by PR 4B.7b-1 (rule 12), with the PR that closes each:** **4B.7b-2:** the evidence as media, the customer's fiscal data (the receiver of a sale is still the customer's name, email, phone and the shipping address), the notification of `FISCAL_DOCUMENT_REJECTED` and its bridge, the consultation for `void` and the document that may be at an issuer that was changed (the debts of PR 4B.7a-2, unchanged). **4B.7b-2:** a credit note that was voided while its sale is live has no way to be made again (only `replace` of the sale makes the notes again): a route for it, with the same rules. **Step 4B.8:** the sweep of returns that have no credit note (the listener runs in process and logs its failure) and of notes left QUEUED while they waited for their original (the attempts of the job run out after about half an hour; a person retries from the route today), and the daily check of a note against the entry of its return. **Step 4B.9 PR D:** the screens (the replace button and the notes of a document; the coverage map says so). **Known limit:** a sale document voided by another request while its credit note is in flight makes the note REJECTED with `original_voided` (the route refuses a void with notes, the race is only that one: the void checks the notes before it calls the provider and cannot hold a lock over the call). **Known limit:** a note that was sent and not answered stays QUEUED with an attempt counted, and while it does the void of its sale is refused (`has_credit_notes`): a person retries it from its route (a QUEUED document is retryable), which asks the authority and settles it. **Known limit, 4B.8:** nothing enqueues a credit note that waited for a sale document that took longer than the attempts of its job (six, about half an hour): the sweep of documents left QUEUED re-enqueues sale documents and notes alike, and a person retries one from its route meanwhile. **Known limit (closed by the fix of HC-107 below, except a line of a few cents):** the books rounded the net and the tax of the units back up separately, so a note could credit a cent less than its entry on a line with odd amounts (the note never credits more than the units were sold for); the daily check of 4B.8 compares a note with its entry with a tolerance of one cent per line. **Known limit:** an order made before the tax snapshot has no credit note (the books cannot reverse it either and list it as TAX_MISSING for a person). **Waits for the accountant (unchanged, plus one):** the real provider, its document types and format, and whether the shipping fee is credited by the note of a return.
- **Built in PR 4B.7b-2 (the evidence, the notices and three second thoughts of the lifecycle; migration `20270106100000_fiscal_evidence` with its rollback):** (a) **Evidence as media:** a document keeps, for ever, at most one file of each kind (`FiscalEvidenceKind`: `document` as it was built, `response` of the authority to the acceptance, `void_response`), as a `Media` of purpose `fiscal_evidence`, made by `FiscalEvidenceService` from the row (the sealed payload is opened and written) once the acceptance or the void is committed, put in the bucket under `stores/<store>/fiscal-evidence/<document>/<media>/`, scanned like any file (`SCAN_FILE`, pending until clean) and served only by `GET /fiscal/documents/:id/evidence/:kind` (FISCAL_VIEW, a short-lived signed link, clean files only, audited as `fiscal.evidence_read`, a document or file of another organization is a 404). The database keeps it: the pointer is on the file (`media.fiscal_document_id`, `fiscal_evidence_kind`, restrict), one file per kind (partial unique index), a check on the parents, a trigger that refuses another store than the document's, and a trigger that refuses a delete and any change but the scan's status. A file that could not be made when the document was decided (the bucket was down) is made from the row the first time somebody asks for it (`keep` is repeatable); the stuck-scan sweep of the media cleanup never drops it. (b) **Notices:** `FISCAL_DOCUMENT_REJECTED` (already raised since 4B.7a-2) and the new `FISCAL_DOCUMENT_STUCK` (the last attempt of the job failed and the document is still waiting: nobody retries it any more) cross the worker bridge and tell whoever holds `fiscal:manage` in the organization, once each until read, in the first store they can act in (in-app and e-mail, texts in es and en, no receiver, no amount, no reason in them). (c) **Consultation for `void`:** the port gets an optional `consultVoid`; core asks before it sends a void (the authority may have the document invalidated already: an earlier request whose answer was lost, or a void made elsewhere) and once after a void that got no answer; `VOIDED` settles the document with what the authority answered. The simulator has the rule `VOID_LOST` and the contract suite tests the method when a provider has it. (d) **The document that may be at an issuer that was changed:** `retry` still refuses it (the same number could end at two authorities), now with the reason `issuer_changed_in_flight`; `POST /fiscal/documents/:id/confirm-issuer-change` (FISCAL_MANAGE, HIGH tier `CONFIRM_FISCAL_ISSUER_CHANGE`, a reason) is how a person who checked with the authority (and the accountant) that it is not there makes it again with the issuer as it is now: a new submission, a new key, a fresh count, audited as `fiscal.issuer_change_confirmed`. (e) **A voided credit note made again:** `POST /fiscal/documents/:id/replace` on a voided credit note makes a new one for the same return (or the same whole-order return) against the sale document that is live, queued; refused while the note is not voided, while its return has a live note, while the sale was voided (replace the sale first) and when the units do not fit.
- **Decisions of PR 4B.7b-2 (rule 12):** (1) **The customer's fiscal data is its own PR (4B.7b-3), not part of this one:** it touches the customer module (the erase, the merge, the redaction of customer data, the order snapshot) and is a very-high-risk surface of its own; with it this PR is over 40 files. 4B.7b-3 adds the encrypted tax id, registration id and economic activity to the customer and to the order, a validation each provider declares in its manifest (nothing fiscal is invented in core), and makes the receiver of a new document read them; the receiver of a document that was sent never changes (it is sealed). (2) **The evidence is made from the row after the commit, never inside the transaction of the decision:** the authority has answered and the decision is not undone by a bucket that blinked; the cost is a window with no file, closed by the repeatable `keep` and by the sweep of 4B.8 (below). Rejected: making the files inside the transaction (a failed upload would roll back an acceptance the authority already gave). (3) **The pointer is on the file, not on the document:** an accepted row cannot change, and changing its guard trigger to let a pointer through would loosen the rule that protects the legal evidence. Rejected: a column on the document. (4) **The scan of evidence stays on** although the platform wrote the file: a provider's answer is text from outside and the rule "no link before a clean scan" has no exception by origin. (5) **The confirmation of an issuer change is a person's act with a reason in the audit trail, not a column of the document:** the row of an accepted document is immutable and a confirmation only happens on a document that is not accepted; the audit trail is append-only. Rejected: a core-side consultation at the first issuer (core has only the credentials of the current issuer). (6) `consultVoid` is optional in the port: a provider that cannot tell keeps the behavior of 4B.7a-2.

A provider that declares nothing (the simulator) keeps the correlative of the organization and no row: nothing existing changes and no document is renumbered. A provider that numbers by type implements `resolveDocumentType` (pure, the registry refuses one that does not, the contract suite checks it answers what `build` builds), because the type is chosen by the provider and the number is needed inside the document. (b) **A stable identifier:** `documentUuid`, a UUID v4 derived from the organization and the document, the same at every attempt and submission, so a document sent again after a refusal is the same document for the authority. (d) **The database keeps the numbers:** the guard of an accepted document adds the two columns to what never changes, a counter only moves forward and is never deleted (trigger + `REVOKE DELETE`), a series past the INTEGER of the document refuses the document (`sequence_exhausted`, the counter rolled back) instead of repeating a number. Rejected: a `formatNumber` callback in core (it would put the format of a country in the runtime). (2) **`sequenceNumber` stays the order the documents were made in** (list cursor, unique index, the books' check): the legal number is a separate column. Rejected: replacing it (it would renumber history and break the cursor). (3) **The number is taken when the provider builds, not when the document is made**, because the type comes from the receiver and a refused document may be fixed into another type; the same document keeps its number while its type does not change. Rejected: taking it at creation (the type is not known yet). (4) **A hash as the key of a series, with the readable parts beside it:** a provider's type id has no length limit core can rely on. (5) **`documentUuid` is derived, not stored:** it is a pure function of two ids, so there is nothing to migrate and no document can lose it. Rejected: a column. (6) **Payments are one entry for the whole order** (what the order records), and the condition is two values of core's own; the provider refines them. Rejected: a table of payments (the order has one method). (7) **`itemKind` and `unit` are optional and null today:** the catalog of the store has no such fields yet; a provider falls back on the default it declares (debt (c)). (8) **A counter has no UI and no route in this PR:** its isolation is proved by `tests/api/fiscal-series.spec.ts` and by its composite key, and the model is exempt in `scripts/isolation-exemptions.ts` for Step 4B.7 (debt (f)).

**(c)** the catalog of the store has no unit of measure or kind of item per product: 4B.7c-2 declares the defaults, and a product field (with its web form) is a later step if the accountant wants them per product; **(d)** a sale paid in parts, or on delivery, is read as one payment and by the status only: `TDD_18 §13` rows 3 and 7, the provider refines it; a credit note carries the payment of its order, not of the document it cancels; **(j)** a number is taken when a worker builds the document, so two documents of one series can take their numbers in another order than they were made (a retry, a delayed job): whether the authority needs the dates of a series to run with its numbers is a question for the accountant, and 4B.7c-2/3 answer it (the fix would be to take them in the order of `sequenceNumber` under the issuer lock); **(l)** the contact of the issuer is read from the snapshot of the document and is not part of `sameIssuer`: fixing a typo in it refuses no document in flight, and a document built before the fix goes out with the old contact (the person retries it if that matters).

(b) **The pure construction of the invoice to a final consumer (01), the tax credit document (03) and the credit note (05)** from the sale of the port: integers and the rounding of the authority (eight decimals in the items, two in the summary, half up), prices with the tax inside for the invoice and net prices with the tax apart for the other two, the discount of the order spread over the items by the largest remainder, exempt and not subject sales apart, the shipping fee as a service of its own, the payment and its condition, the control number from the series of core, the identifier in capitals, the date and hour of El Salvador, the amount in words, and a credit note that names the document it cancels in the relation and in each item and credits a part of it with the shares of the books (3 x 3.33: 38, 39 and 38 cents). (c) **Every document generated by the specs is validated against the schemas of the authority** (`svfe-json-schemas` v2 and v4, copied under `libs/fiscal/sv/schemas`; `ajv` as a development dependency), with a test that the check is real. (d) **A sale that cannot be made right is refused with a code, never sent:** a total or a tax that does not add up, a rate other than 13 %, a line with no tax treatment, a tax more than a hundredth from the authority's formula, an incomplete issuer, an invoice for an order whose prices exclude the tax, a credit note of an invoice. Rejected: recomputing the tax from the formula (the document and the books would differ by cents and the customer's total would move). (2) **The discount goes in the items, not in the global fields of the summary:** one rule for the three documents (a credit note has no global discount). Rejected: the global discount per type of sale. (3) **An invoice needs prices with the tax inside:** a store whose prices exclude it gets a refusal and a person decides (debt (c)). (4) **A tax credit document is for a receiver with a registration number**, an invoice for anyone else; the buyer's own tax number without a registration number is an invoice with that number. (5) **The provider is registered in development and test only** (where the simulator is): a deployment cannot choose a provider that cannot send.
