**(f)** the manifest cannot hand the catalogs to the settings screen (departments, municipalities, activities): 4B.7c-5 adds what the form needs; **(g)** the registration of the provider moves from development and test to a deployment that has its credentials when 4B.7c-3 can send; **(h)** the establishment type of the issuer is kept but not asked for (the schemas of these three documents have no field for it; the events do): 4B.7c-4 and 4B.7c-7; **(i)** the tax of the order is the sum of the tax of its lines, each rounded, and the check against the authority's formula over the whole document allows one hundredth: an order of several taxed lines can drift by more and is refused (`tax_outside_tolerance`) instead of being sent: the sandbox says whether the authority is more tolerant, and if so `SvLimits.TOLERANCE_CENTS` changes (4B.7c-6); **(j)** the discount of the order is spread over all the lines by their amount, which is what the books are assumed to do: an order whose books spread it otherwise (only over the taxed lines) gets a different split between taxed and exempt sales than the books, and the check of the tax may refuse it; the port would have to hand the discount of each line (4B.7c-6); **(k)** a shipping fee whose tax rounds to zero cents is declared exempt; **(l)** the identification threshold above which an invoice to a final consumer must name the buyer (art. 119-G of the Código Tributario) is not known to this package: no invoice is stopped for lacking it, and the accountant gives the figure so that it becomes `missingReceiverFields` (`SvConsumerIdentityThreshold`, 4B.7c-5); **(m)** a refusal of `build` reaches the log with the code of the provider (`providerCode`) but the document keeps the generic `build_failed`: core would keep the provider's code as the reason a person reads, 4B.7c-5.
- **Built in PR 4B.7c-3 (the client of the authority: login, signing, reception and consultation; high risk: credentials of a real tax account and retries over an account that locks; against a server of our own, nothing reaches the real authority):** (a) **The token** (`SvAuthenticator`): asked for once and kept in memory per environment, user and password (a new password is a new key), renewed at 80 % of its day (production) or two days (sandbox), one login shared by the documents that wait for it, and **a password the authority refused is not sent again for fifteen minutes** (three wrong logins lock the user until a person changes the password in the site of the authority): the document is `REJECTED` with `credentials_rejected`, never retried by the queue. (b) **The signer is a port** (`SvSigner`) with the adapter of the official signing service (`POST /firmardocumento/`, always HTTP 200, `status` OK or ERROR): its address is `FISCAL_SIGNER_URL` (env schema, `.env.example`, no credentials in it), a password of the private key that does not open the certificate is `REJECTED` (`signing_credentials_rejected`), a service that is down is `UNAVAILABLE` and no login is made for it. (c) **`submit`**: signs, sends the signed document with the token and the generic user agent (8 s of timeout), and maps the answer: processed with a seal -> `ACCEPTED` (number = control number; `providerData` keeps the generation code, control number, seal, date, observations and the **signed document**, the evidence of what was sent), refused -> `REJECTED` with the authority's own code and its answer, a fault of the moment (5xx, timeout, network, codes 22 and 99) -> `UNAVAILABLE`, a token the authority does not accept -> one new login and one new try. (d) **`consult`** by generation code: processed -> `ACCEPTED`, a clear "no such document" -> `UNKNOWN`, anything it could not ask throws, so the queue asks again and a document that may be there is never sent twice. (e) **Registration:** the provider is offered where the deployment gives `FISCAL_SIGNER_URL` (any environment), and the simulator stays where it was (development and test); `officialFiscalProviders(nodeEnv, config)`. (f) **The contract suite of providers runs for this provider** against the fake authority (accepts, refuses, unavailable then accepts, lost answer found by consulting, credit note), with new optional fixtures for providers that credit only some documents and cannot invalidate yet. (g) `scripts/check-sv-certificate.ts`, for the owner to run on their own machine: it says, without printing anything secret, whether the certificate has the format a signer of our own could use (option C below).

- **Built in PR 4B.7c-7a (the contingency of the fiscal documents, the core only; very high risk: the life cycle of legal documents; agnostic, no country, authority or provider named outside `libs/fiscal/<provider>`; migration `20270114200000_fiscal_contingency` with its rollback):** (a) **The port:** the manifest declares `contingencyMode` (the reasons the authority tells apart, the one that stands for "the authority is down", the hours to send the lot once the event was taken, the documents one event takes, and whether the authority asks who answers for the establishment); `build` takes an optional `contingency` (the document is made in the deferred model); `deferDocument` signs and keeps a deferred document; `reportContingency` sends the event with the documents. The registry refuses a provider that declares the mode and cannot do both. (b) **The state:** `fiscal_contingencies` (one OPEN per organization by a partial unique index; OPEN, CLOSED, REPORTED, only forward, never deleted, the report fields frozen once REPORTED) and `fiscal_documents.contingency_id` (part of what an accepted document no longer changes). (c) **The life cycle:** with a contingency OPEN for its provider and environment a document is built in the deferred model, signed by the provider, sealed and kept (QUEUED, held: the claim lets it go only when its contingency is REPORTED), and nothing is sent; a person ends the contingency (and gives who answers for the establishment, sealed in the row) and the report job sends the event; once the authority takes it the window of the provider starts and every document goes out through the queue **as it was kept** (it is not built again: what the receiver was handed is what is sent). When the authority did not answer in three attempts (`FiscalContingencyLimits.AUTO_OPEN_AFTER_ATTEMPTS`) and the provider has the mode, the life cycle opens a contingency by itself and tells a person. (d) **The rest:** routes `GET/POST /fiscal/contingency`, `POST /fiscal/contingency/end`, `GET /fiscal/contingencies`, `POST /fiscal/contingencies/:id/report`, `POST /fiscal/contingencies/:id/abandon` (permissions `fiscal:view` and `fiscal:manage`, a controller of their own), the job `report-fiscal-contingency` in the heavy queue (the worker starts: the module spec resolves it), three alerts (opened by the system, report failed, window closing; one event `fiscal.contingency_alert`, three notification types, texts in English and Spanish), the daily check asks again for a report that is owed and warns when a window is closing, and the check of stalled documents leaves out what waits on purpose. Tests: `tests/api/fiscal-contingency.spec.ts` (16 cases against a provider with the mode), the isolation case `fiscalContingency` (killed by a mutant that drops the organization from the lookup), the registry and listener specs, and the rollback run against a database with and without rows.
- **Decisions of PR 4B.7c-7a (rule 12):** (1) **A held document is a QUEUED document with a `contingency_id`, not a new status:** a new status would touch the list filters, the web, the sweep and the guard of every consumer of the status. Rejected: `DEFERRED` as a status. (2) **A document goes out as it was kept**, never rebuilt, so the copy the receiver has and the one the authority gets are the same bytes; the price is that the receiver of a kept document cannot be edited (409) until the authority refuses it, and a refused one leaves its contingency and is made again in the normal model on a retry. (3) **The authority-down contingency opens by itself after three attempts** (the manual: a call with no answer, a consultation, two retries, then contingency), because a shop that waits for a person to open it stops selling documents; the person is told at once and ends it. Rejected: manual only. (4) **No consultation before keeping a document in contingency** (the authority is what is down): a document that was in fact received is found when it is sent (the duplicate answer starts the consultation). (5) **One event per contingency, with a cap:** a document that finds the open one full is held back (its job fails and is asked again) until a person ends it, and the lifecycle opens the next one by itself if the authority is still down. Rejected: closing and reopening by itself at the cap (it would report with nobody's name for the establishment). (6) **The documents of a lot go one by one through the queue**, with the idempotency of the queue and the consultation before a repeat, not through the batch endpoint of the authority: one path for a document, whatever its model. (7) **The window is not enforced by core:** a document past it is still sent and the authority decides; a person is warned when 25 % is left. (8) **`end` reads the rule from the provider the contingency was opened with**, not from today's issuer, so a contingency can always be ended even when the issuer left that provider. (9) **A report that cannot go through has an exit:** `POST /fiscal/contingencies/:id/abandon` detaches the documents held in an ended contingency (the authority refused the event for good, or the issuer changed) so they are made again the normal way, and the contingency stays as the record; without it they would stay held for ever.
- **Left by PR 4B.7c-7a (rule 12), with the PR that closes each:** **(a)** the provider of El Salvador (the deferred model of its documents, the event of schema `contingencia-v4` checked with ajv, the signature of a deferred document, the report and the fake authority's endpoint): done in **Step 4B.7c-7b**; **(b)** the screens (the state of the contingency, start and end with the person responsible, the report asked again, the alerts' links; the coverage map says so): **Step 4B.9** with the fiscal screens; **(c)** the delivery of the signed document to the receiver while it has no seal of the authority (the evidence files of a held document): **Step 4B.7c-5b**; **(d)** nothing asks the authority whether it is back, so a contingency opened by the life cycle stays open until a person ends it, and no reminder is sent for one that stays open for days: **Step 4B.7c-8**; **(e)** the real codes the authority answers to the event and to a deferred document sent before its event, and the instant its seal carries: **Step 4B.7c-6** (the sandbox); **(f)** a change of the issuer's provider or environment while a contingency is open leaves it unreportable (`issuer_changed`, a person decides with the accountant): the interface has to say so, **Step 4B.9**; **(h)** the provider answers an event it already took (an answer that was lost) with what it holds, never as a refusal: the port says so and the provider of **Step 4B.7c-7b** implements it, the sandbox of **4B.7c-6** settles the real answer; **(i)** a note kept in a contingency blocks the void of its sale document and is not moved by a replacement, with no test of its own yet (the credit-note fixtures of `fiscal-credit-notes.spec.ts` are the place): **Step 4B.7c-7b**; **(g)** a credit note of a document held in contingency waits for its sale document to be accepted (as before), so the note goes out after the lot, inside whatever the authority allows: the accountant confirms the order in **Step 4B.7c-6**.
- **Built in PR 4B.7c-7b (the contingency of El Salvador, `libs/fiscal/sv` only; very high risk: legal documents signed and kept without the authority; against a server of our own, nothing reaches the real authority):** (a) **The deferred model of a document:** `build` takes the contingency and writes `tipoModelo` 2, `tipoOperacion` 2, the reason of CAT-005 as `tipoContingencia` and, for the reason "other" only, the person's words as `motivoContin` (required then); a reason the catalog does not have is refused with a code. (b) **`deferDocument`:** signs the document with the signing service and keeps the signed form in the provider data; it needs no login (the authority is what is down) and refuses a document that was not built for the deferred model. (c) **The event** (`sv-contingency.ts`, schema `contingencia-v4`): the window in the time of El Salvador, the documents by type and generation code (1 to 1000, none repeated, all deferred), the person who answers for the establishment (type and number of the identity document checked as in the invalidation), the issuer's own codes; every refusal is a code and nothing is sent. The spec checks every event and every deferred document against the official schema with ajv. (d) **`reportContingency`:** signs and sends the event to `/fesv/contingencia`, reads the seal and the instant the authority took it (the window of 72 hours runs from the earlier of that instant and our clock, so it is never longer than the authority's), maps an unavailable answer to "ask again", keeps the authority's code on a refusal, and takes an event the authority holds already (code 4: the answer of the first call was lost) as reported, the window from the end of the contingency. It also refuses an event whose documents say another reason or another environment, a window that has not ended, a reason that merely starts with a digit, and a document of another issuer's NIT. (e) **The manifest** declares the mode: the five reasons, reason 1 (the authority's own system) as the one the life cycle uses, 72 hours, 1000 documents an event, the person responsible required. (f) **The fake authority** gets the event endpoint (schema, signature, NIT, repeated event), a switch that takes its reception down, and refuses a deferred document no event listed (code 056 of OUR fake; the real one is the sandbox's).
- **Decisions of PR 4B.7c-7b (rule 12):** (1) **The window counts from the earlier of the authority's time and ours**: never longer than the authority's. Rejected: our clock alone (it could run past the real window). (2) **A repeated event is taken as reported, with the window counted from the end of the contingency:** the port says so and without it a lost answer would leave the lot held for good; the end of the window is the earliest instant the authority can have taken the event, so the window is never longer than the authority's (rejected: counting from now, which could run past the real one). Debt (b). (3) **The reason "other" is the only one with words**, the rest carry none, so a person's text never travels where the catalog has no field for it. (4) **No login to defer a document:** signing is the one thing the authority's outage does not stop.
- **Left by PR 4B.7c-7b (rule 12), with the PR that closes each:** **(a)** the real codes of the event (taken, refused, repeated), the shape of the answer (`estado`, `fechaHora`, `selloRecibido`) and the real refusal of a deferred document sent before its event are read from the manual, not tried: the 5 contingency tests of **Step 4B.7c-6** settle them; **(b)** whether the authority repeats the seal of an event it took and the instant it carries: **4B.7c-6** (until then a repeated event has no seal in the record); **(c)** the event's shipment number is not needed (the event has none), but the `idEnvio` of documents sent after it is the one of a normal document: **4B.7c-6** confirms it; **(d)** production stays closed until the owner authorizes it: **Step 4B.7c-8**.
- **Built in fiscal-D2 (contingency retries and the 24 h of the event, fiscal runtime and the SV declaration):** the job of the report of a contingency is asked again at a fixed delay of 14 minutes (a minute under the 15 of the rule, for the call and the queue) for 24 hours (`fiscalReportJobOptions`, `FiscalContingencyLimits.REPORT_RETRY_DELAY_MS` and `REPORT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` = 103, Normativa DTE v2.0 13.2); the exponential backoff of a document submission was cut to 45 s so its longest wait (12 min) stays under 15 minutes; the provider declares `reportWithinHours` (SV: 24, 13.2.2) and the person is told once (`WINDOW_CLOSING`, `warnedAt`, cleared when the event is taken so the 72 h window warns again) when the 24 h after the end of the situation are closing, by each attempt of the report and by the daily check; `sv-auth.spec.ts` fixes that a refused password is never sent again in a loop (the memory of `REJECTED_MEMORY_MS` already existed: not a defect). No migration. **Decisions (rule 12):** (1) the fixed 15 min interval for the report instead of a custom backoff strategy in the worker: the queue already supports it and no worker setting changes; (2) a report job queued before this PR keeps its 6 attempts; when they end the person is told and the daily check asks again, so nothing is lost; (3) the alert kind `WINDOW_CLOSING` is reused for the 24 h deadline (same notice to the person) instead of a new kind with its own column, notification type and i18n, which would have grown the PR past review size.
- **Left by fiscal-D2 (rule 12), with the PR that closes each:** **(a)** closed by fiscal-D2b (next line). **(b)** Done by fiscal-D2c (branch `fix/fiscal-contingency-open-polling`): an open contingency is probed every 14 minutes (`probeAuthority` of the provider, one BullMQ scheduler for each open contingency, asked again by the daily check), the end can be declared by the person (not in the future, not before the start) and counts the 24 h from it, the technical report of a contingency that lasts more than 3 consecutive days is told once (`technical_report_warned_at`). Left, with the step that owns each: **(b1)** the 24 h of the event still share `WINDOW_CLOSING` and `warnedAt` with the window of the lot (the mark is cleared when the event is taken, so they never run together); a distinct kind only if a person needs to tell them apart. **(b2)** The technical report is only told: the transmission of the event is not held back until a person confirms the report was filed (needs a confirmation field and a screen). **(b3)** The probe of the Salvadoran provider asks for a fresh login, not the reception service, so an outage of reception alone is not seen; a probe at reception needs a call the manual allows without a document. **(b4)** The provider asks who answers for the establishment, so its contingency is not closed by itself: the probe stores the instant of the first answer, tells a person and offers it as the end; closing by itself needs the person to be given when the contingency is entered. **(b6)** After the probe saw the authority answer, the contingency (which a person still has to end) keeps no new document, so if the reception service alone is still down those documents go the ordinary way and fail until the person ends it; opening a new contingency over a restored one needs the end of the first to be possible without the responsible. Only a contingency of the authority being down is probed; one for a fault of the issuer's own is ended by a person. **(b7)** The probe keeps what stops it as a keyed fingerprint (HMAC with a key derived from the key that seals the credentials): a rotation of the key changes it, which costs one more login with the refused credentials; it lives in the contingency, so a new contingency with the same bad credentials makes one more login before it stops; two workers (or a worker and a sending) may each have a login in flight before it is kept, which is two wrong logins at most for the authority's three. The scheduler of a probe is not removed when an organization is deleted (the job is skipped and repeats as a no-op every 14 minutes). A declared end is not checked against the documents already kept in the contingency. **(b5)** The screen of the fiscal settings does not show `restoredAt` or the end time field yet (web owner: the fiscal settings step). All of it owned by Step 4B.7c-7. **(c)** Contingency by batch (D16): `POST /fesv/recepcionlote` (max 100 DTE per lot, 400 lots), the `codigoLote` and `GET /fesv/recepcion/consultadtelote/{codigoLote}`; today the documents go one by one through `/fesv/recepciondte` after the event and `SvContingency.MAX_DOCUMENTS` is 1000: owner: Step 4B.7c-7, session fiscal-D16 (about 8 to 10 files: `sv-constants.ts`, a new `sv-batch.ts` and its spec, `sv-transmission.ts`, `sv-provider.ts`, the SDK interface for a batch submission, `fiscal-contingency.service.ts`, the integration test; plus the QR of the public query in the printed representation, D13). **(d)** The version of the event of contingency stays 4 (the Normativa says 3, the schema says 4) until the authority answers. **(e)** The 24 h retransmission after a rejection of the authority is the fiscal-D14 session, not this one.
- **Fix D2d (the probe of an open contingency asks the reception side, not only the login; PR `fix/fiscal-contingency-probe-reception`, 2026-11-27):** closes (b3) and the first half of (b6) of fiscal-D2. After the fresh login the Salvadoran provider now makes a consultation of a document by a generation code that cannot exist (`SvProbe.GENERATION_CODE`, all zeros in the shape of a version 4 code, for the issuer itself, type 01). It is read-only and carries no document, so it takes no number and no seal and leaves no trace in the books of the authority; any answer that has the shape of the authority's (a document found, or "there is no such document") says the side that receives the documents is up. A 5xx, a 401 or 403 (the token it just gave is not taken), no connection, no answer in time, or a body that is not JSON (a page of a proxy) is `UNREACHABLE`, so the contingency goes on and the documents keep being kept instead of sent. Rule 12: the best alternative, a deliberately invalid POST to `/fesv/recepciondte`, was rejected because it would send something to the endpoint that takes the documents and the authority may count or log it against the issuer. **Left by D2d (rule 12):** **(a)** the consultation and the reception of documents are different paths of the same host (`/fesv/recepcion/consultadte` and `/fesv/recepciondte`); whether one service answers both is confirmed in the sandbox run, and if the consultation turns out to be served apart, the probe still misses an outage of the reception alone; owner: Step 4B.7c-6b; **(b)** the second signal (the last real transmissions that failed in a row keep the contingency) is not built: it needs a count of consecutive failures by organization that nothing keeps today; owner: Step 4B.7c-7, with the end of a contingency declared by a person; **(c)** the probe adds one read-only call every 14 minutes for each open contingency; a rate limit of the authority on the consultation is not known (an answer of 429, 404 or 403, or one that is not in the form of the authority, counts as no answer, so the contingency stays open: if the user of the issuer has no right on the consultation, the contingency is ended by a person, never by the probe; confirmed in the sandbox run, 4B.7c-6b). The answer is believed only with a state of the reception side's own words (`SvProbe.ANSWER_STATES`) and a code of three digits: if the authority answers 404 for "there is no such document", the probe never sees the reception up and the contingency is closed only by hand (closed on failure); it is confirmed in the sandbox run together with (a).
- **Built in fiscal-D2b (retries of the released documents, fiscal runtime, the web and the worker):** a document released after the report of its contingency is asked again at a fixed interval of 14 minutes for the whole 72-hour window of its lot (`fiscalReleasedJobOptions`, `FiscalContingencyLimits.RELEASED_RETRY_HOURS` and `RELEASED_MAX_ATTEMPTS` = 309), no longer the six attempts of an ordinary document; `isStuck` (the second argument says the document is kept in a contingency), the count of the listing of `fiscal-documents.service.ts` and the nightly sweep (`FiscalFinding.released`, which the reconciler of the worker reads to queue the same options) use the attempts of the document's own kind (`fiscalSubmitMaxAttempts`), and the web reads the `stuck` the server sends instead of counting attempts. The registry refuses a provider that declares a transmission window of more than `RELEASED_RETRY_HOURS`, so the retries always cover the window. No migration. **Decisions (rule 12):** (1) the stuck rule keys on `contingencyId`, which a document keeps for ever, instead of a new column or a status: a released document that is refused by the authority and retried by a person leaves the contingency (its `contingencyId` is cleared) and goes back to the ordinary six attempts. Rejected: a new column (a migration with its rollback for what the existing one says). (2) The web uses the server's `stuck` instead of a copy of the rule: the listing already sends it and a second copy would drift. (3) The job gets exactly `RELEASED_MAX_ATTEMPTS` attempts, as the stuck threshold: the attempts the document had before it was kept (at most the three that opened the contingency) only make it stuck earlier by that few, never later. (4) a person's retry of a document that is still kept in a contingency (`retry` answers `released`) queues the same options, so its job and its stuck threshold agree; a contingency given up detaches its documents (`contingencyId` cleared) and queues them with the ordinary options, so their job and their stuck rule are the ordinary six attempts (`enqueueSubmissions` takes `released`, true only from the release after the report). **Left (rule 12):** the window is a ceiling in core (72 hours, `RELEASED_RETRY_HOURS`) and the registry refuses a provider that declares more; a provider with a longer window needs the constant raised (a one-line change in core, with its spec), and the count of the listing is an `OR` over the rows QUEUED of the organization (the index of (organization, status) narrows it, and the queue of an organization is small): both are accepted until a provider or a measure says otherwise, tracked here for Step 4B.7c-7. **Also left:** a job of 72 hours holds a delayed slot in the queue for each released document for up to three days (a lot of 1000 documents is 1000 delayed jobs; note it with the cap of documents per event), and the 72 hour ceiling lives in the registry, not in the type of the SDK: owner, Step 4B.7c-7. **Also left:** the attempt that ends before the document is sent lowers the count of the row by one (an old rule that also holds for the six attempts), so a released document may end its job one or two attempts short of the threshold and show as retrying until a person or the sweep moves it: owner, Step 4B.7c-7, with the next change to `FiscalDocumentsService` that touches the count.

- **Built in PR 4B.7c-6a (the runner of the minimum tests of the sandbox; medium risk: it can send documents to the authority's sandbox, only on the owner's machine and only with the owner's confirmation; it reads no credential file and nothing reaches the authority in any test):** (a) **An agnostic runner in the SDK** (`libs/fiscal/sdk/src/conformance.ts`): a plan is a list of steps (a sale, a credit note of another step, an invalidation of another step with the document that replaces it, a deferred sale, the event of a contingency), run through the port of any provider (`build`, `submit`, `void`, `deferDocument`, `reportContingency`), never through the lifecycle of core, so it needs no database. Its report carries the ids of the plan, the kinds, the outcomes, the codes and the counts (by type of document: planned, built, accepted, refused, not answered; the invalidations; the contingencies; how varied the plan was), and **no document, no number, no seal, no signed text**: a refusal keeps only what has the shape of a code (free text of a provider or an authority is `unreadable`), a thrown error keeps only its name, and before the report is returned it is searched for every secret the caller listed (passwords, tax number, contact, names): one found fails the run with a message that names none. A dry run builds everything and sends nothing. (b) **The plan of El Salvador** (`libs/fiscal/sv/src/conformance/sv-conformance-plan.ts`): 90 invoices, 75 tax credit documents, 50 credit notes of the first tax credit documents (whole or partial), 5 invalidations (two rescissions, two corrections and one other reason, with the replacement accepted first) made on documents of their own, and 5 contingencies (every reason of the catalog in turn, the "other" with words) listing two deferred invoices each; invented data in many shapes (anonymous consumers, with national id or tax number, businesses with a registration number, activity and address of the catalogs; taxed, exempt and not-subject lines; discounts; taxed and exempt shipping; prices with and without the tax; roundings of one cent, a third and a thousandth; credit terms; every method of payment; dates inside the month of the run). Deterministic from a seed; the generation code of a document comes from the batch and the id, so another batch is another set for the authority, and the series start after an offset. The tax of each document is the authority's formula over the taxed part, split over its items, so every document adds up to the cent. (c) **The reader of the owner's environment** (`sv-sandbox-env.ts`): the names (listed there and by `--help-env`), never a value; ready only when every name is set AND `DTE_SANDBOX_CONFIRM=send-to-sandbox`; the only environment it can make is the sandbox. (d) **The script** `libs/fiscal/conformance/src/run-conformance.ts` (`pnpm fiscal:conformance`): `--provider simulator` (default: documents, credit notes and invalidations through the simulator, which has no contingency mode, so those steps are skipped and said so), `--provider sv --dry-run` (builds every document with the provider's rules, needs no environment), `--provider sv` (the real sandbox, only with the environment and the confirmation), `--seed`, `--batch`, `--offset`, `--counts`, `--out`, `--json`; it prints a summary and the gaps to the minimum. (e) **Tests**: the runner against a scripted provider (outcomes, codes, no free text, no error message, credit note and void dependencies, contingency, the leak gate), the plan (counts, determinism, variety, every document built with the rules of the provider and checked against the official schema with ajv, dates inside the term, invented numbers), the plan against the fake authority (90/75/50, 5 and 5 reached; dry run sends nothing; nothing sensitive in the report), the reader of the environment, and the plan through the simulator.
- **Decisions of PR 4B.7c-6a (rule 12):** (1) **The runner goes through the port, not through core's lifecycle:** the lifecycle needs a database, a queue and an order for each document, and what the authority asks to see is documents accepted with a seal, which the port gives. Rejected: seeding orders and running the worker (heavy, and the numbers of the series would belong to the test data). (2) **The documents made for the invalidations and the deferred ones are extra:** nothing says whether an invalidated or a deferred document counts among the 90/75/50, so the minimum is reached without them (8 more invoices for the invalidations, 10 more for the contingencies). Rejected: invalidating documents of the minimum (it could leave the count short). (3) **The credit notes are of the first 50 tax credit documents**, one each: a credit note of an invoice to a final consumer is the accountant's open question (`SvCreditableDocuments`), so no note is made of an invoice. (4) **The secrets are checked at the end, not trusted to the code that built the report:** a second line of defence that costs a search. (5) **The names of the environment are our own** (`DTE_SANDBOX_*`), not those of the owner's file, which was not read: a mapping is one line of the owner's shell. (6) **Real sends need the confirmation as well as the names**, so an environment left set in a shell never sends by accident. (7) **Coverage is judged against the minimum of the authority, by the part of the plan each document was made for** (a bucket), never against what was asked of this run and never counting the extra documents: a reduced run is "incomplete" and 15 extra invoices accepted do not hide 15 minimum invoices refused. (8) **The exit code of a real run is 0 only if the minimum is reached and nothing else failed**; a leak of a secret into the report withholds it, prints only numbers of what was done, and exits 3. (9) **The tool refuses what is ambiguous**: an option it does not know, a value given twice, a count out of its bounds, a signing service on a public host over http, production, and the first half hour of a month (a document could only be dated in the month before). (10) **The summary says the `--offset` the next run must use**: the series of the invoices is shared by the minimum and the documents made for the invalidations and the contingencies.
- **Fix D14 (a document the authority refused is corrected and sent again within 24 hours; PR `fix/fiscal-rejected-retransmit-24h`, 2026-11-25):** the moment the authority's refusal is communicated is kept (`fiscal_documents.rejected_at`, null for a refusal core made before sending), the window is `FiscalRejectionRetry.WINDOW_MS` read with an injectable clock (`rejectionDeadline`), the document view carries `rejectionDeadline` `{ endsAt, state }`, and the daily check tells whoever manages the fiscal documents once for each refusal (`rejection_warned_at`, event and notification `fiscal.retransmit_deadline`) from `WARN_BEFORE_MS` before the end, or after it. The retransmission is the same document: its generation code is `fiscalDocumentUuid(organization, document)`, which does not depend on the submission, so a corrected document goes out with the same code. **Left (rule 12):** **(a)** the check ran once a day, so a refusal could be told after its window ended; **closed by D14b (`fix/fiscal-rejected-events-hourly`):** an hourly job per organization (`WARN_FISCAL_DEADLINES`, twenty past the hour, id per organization and hour) runs the same conditional marks, so the notice leaves in the first hour of the closing stretch; the daily check keeps asking too, as a backstop (the marks make it idempotent); the contingency windows are looked at every hour too (cadence only). D14b also keeps the codes that mean "try again" (22, 99, 101) out of the refusals, so they never start the window, and a test fixes that a credit note is not released while its sale document is refused or has no seal (the runtime already held it); **Left by D14b (rule 12):** **(e)** the hourly job is queued for every organization, with or without fiscal activity (each look is a few indexed queries); a filter to organizations that have a fiscal issuer needs a read outside row security and belongs to the first deployment with many organizations (Phase 2); **(f)** a document that always draws code 101 is retried until its attempts run out and then `reportExhausted` tells the person; whether 101 depends on the content of the document is confirmed in the sandbox run (Step 4B.7c-6b); **(b)** a refusal whose reason is the generation code itself would need a new code: the provider reports no such reason today, and Step 4B.7c-6b (the real sandbox run) closes it; **(c)** the interface that draws `rejectionDeadline` in the document list and detail is Step 4B.9's, and it must show it: the immediate notice of a refusal does not say there are 24 hours; **(d)** this PR covers refused DOCUMENTS only: the rule says "document or event", so a refused EVENT (invalidation, contingency) has no 24-hour window and no notice with a deadline (a refused contingency report already tells the person at once with `REPORT_FAILED`, with no deadline); owner: Step 4B.7c. **Closed in part by D14b-2 (`fix/fiscal-void-rejection-window`, migration `20270204300000`):** an invalidation the authority refuses (`VoidResult.byAuthority`, set by the SV provider only for the authority's own answer) keeps the document accepted and starts the same 24 hours (`fiscal_documents.void_rejected_at`, warned once with `void_rejection_warned_at`, same event and notification as a refused document, text now says "or the invalidation of one"); the view carries `voidRejectionDeadline`, which Step 4B.9 must draw beside the void action. A refusal of the invalidation by core before sending starts nothing. The guard of the table lets an accepted row change only the claim of an invalidation and these two columns. **Left by D14b-2 (rule 12):** **(g)** the local deadline of an invalidation (one calendar day after the seal for a tax credit document or a credit note, `SvInvalidationDeadlineRules`) is still checked before anything is sent, even inside the 24 hours of a refused one: whether the authority counts the corrected event as on time is the accountant's to say (D1), and until then the stricter rule stands; owner: Step 4B.7c with the accountant; **(m)** a window starts at each refusal the authority communicates (the rule counts from the communication of the reason), so a corrected event refused again has a new 24 hours; and the generation code of an invalidation changes with its reason, kind, parties and replacement (its key), so a corrected invalidation is a new event: whether the authority wants the same code for a corrected EVENT is confirmed in the sandbox run (Step 4B.7c-6b), and the text of its notice does not promise it; **(i)** code 4 ("already exists a record with that value") is read as a duplicate and the authority is consulted by generation code; when the repeated value is the control number of ANOTHER document the consult finds nothing and the document stays unavailable until its attempts run out and a person is told, instead of being refused as a duplicated numbering: safe (nothing is lost), confirmed and classified in the sandbox run (Step 4B.7c-6b); **(j)** code 21 ("field cannot be validated") may be a fault of the validation service; it stays a refusal, the safe reading, until the sandbox run says otherwise (4B.7c-6b); the codes of the request or its format (94, 97, 98, 110, 111) also open the window as refusals, a class of their own that warns the technical team is wanted (4B.7c-6b); **(k)** a transitory document or event that was refused is corrected with a new one that gets a seal and asks for the matching accounting adjustment (Normativa 9.3): the books and entries following the corrected document are Step 4B.7c's, not built here; **(l)** the hourly look reads every organization with no global cap (a page at a time): a global cap and a filter by organizations with a fiscal issuer come with the first deployment with many organizations (this is debt (e) of D14b, which that PR recorded); **(h)** the refused EVENT of a contingency has the notice `REPORT_FAILED` and no 24-hour deadline: its report is retried every 14 minutes for 24 hours (D2) and the person is told when that ends, which is the same window counted from the end of the situation; nothing more is added here.
- **Fix D14c (the invalidation event that is corrected and sent again keeps its generation code and its moment; PR `fix/fiscal-void-retransmit-code`, migration `20270210100000` with rollback):** the Normativa DTE v2.0 (apartado 10) asks the corrected event that is sent again to carry the SAME generation code the refused one had, unless the refusal was about the code. Core now fixes `fiscal_documents.void_event_code` and `void_event_at` (both or neither, a check enforces it, accepted documents only) under the row lock when the claim of the invalidation is taken, BEFORE anything is sent, and gives them to the provider as `ProviderContext.voidEvent`; the SV provider uses them as `codigoGeneracion` and as the moment of the event, so the date and the hour of the event (an invoice's date is the day it is made, three months at most) and the local deadline are those of the first attempt, never of the retry (a retry after midnight keeps the date, and a retry is not refused for a deadline that passed meanwhile). The event is reused while the later of its first attempt and its refusal is less than `FiscalRejectionRetry.WINDOW_MS` old and its first attempt is less than `FiscalRejectionRetry.VOID_EVENT_MAX_AGE_MS` (three days) old, so a document refused again and again never sends an event dated weeks back; after that, or when the provider stopped before sending (nothing was refused), or when the authority refused the code itself (`VoidResult.eventCodeRefused`, set by the SV provider when the authority holds a record with the code and the document is still processed, and for codes 4, 6 and 25 when the answer names `identificacion.codigoGeneracion`), the columns are cleared and the next attempt makes a new code and moment. A request with no answer keeps them (the authority may have the event). Both are cleared when the document is voided. The guard of the table lists the columns an accepted row may change in one commented place (the claim, the refusal and warning marks, and these two). **Left by D14c (rule 12):** **(a)** which field the real answer uses to name `identificacion.codigoGeneracion` (`observaciones` and `descripcionMsg` are read) and the exact codes are confirmed in the sandbox run; owner: Step 4B.7c-6b; **(b)** closes (m) of D14b-2 for the invalidation; the local deadline (g) still applies to the first attempt, and the retry is judged at the moment of the first one: whether the authority counts a retransmitted event on time is the accountant's to say (D1); **(c)** a retry whose event is older than the window is a new event by design, and the document keeps no history of earlier events: the audit trail of each attempt is not extended here.
- **Left by PR 4B.7c-6a (rule 12), with the PR that closes each:** **(a)** the run itself, with the owner and the real sandbox (to be done by them on their machine: the counts that Hacienda sees with seal, and the real codes and answers that settle the debts of Steps 4B.7c-2 to 4B.7c-7), and the evidence plan (what to keep: the report, never a document): **Step 4B.7c-6b**, a session of the owner and not a PR; **(b)** whether an invalidated or deferred document counts toward the minimum, and whether the sandbox limits the documents per day or per minute (the run is sequential and has no pause): the first real run says; **(c)** a repeated run with the same batch is not made idempotent by the runner (the provider answers a repeated document by asking the authority, but the plan's invalidations and events are a second ask): use another batch and an offset, as the script says; **(e)** the deferred documents are dated inside the window of their contingency, which near the start of a month can fall in the month before (the tool refuses the first half hour of a month, not the hours after it): the owner does not run it in the first hours of a month; **(d)** the term of two months from the first entry to the sandbox (the owner says the date; about 2027-01-15 by the coordinator's count) is not checked by the code.
- **Built in PR D17 (fix/fiscal-fe-receptor-credit, `libs/fiscal/sv` only, rule 12):** the invoice (01) no longer gets what the Normativa DTE v2.0 Anexo IV validates as null: the receiver carries no economic activity, department, municipality or address (fields 43.1, 44.1, 47.1, 48.1 and 50, pages 106-107; the delivery address is not the receiver's), and an order whose only data is an address has no receiver; a sale on credit (condition 2) declares one payment with no form, $0.00 and no reference, keeping the term (fields 160.5, 161.6, 162.5, 163.2, page 121); a document with nothing to pay is always cash (159.2); a service, and an item of kind 4, take unit 99 (Anexo II, page 64, field 85). The JSON schema of the authority accepts all of these as they were: the rules are Anexo IV's, so the specs assert the payload and the schema together. a credit sale paid in part declares the credit only ($0.00, the deposit is not a line of the document; accepted trade-off, to confirm with the accountant in Step 7.4). **Left (rule 12):** **(a)** the term of a credit (`SvDeferredTerm`, one day) is still a placeholder because the order does not carry its terms and 163.2 keeps it required; it stays **[ACCOUNTANT]** and closes in Step 7.4 with the accountant; **(b)** the identification threshold of the invoice (38.6, 39.3 and 42.3) is not here, it is Step 7.4; **(c)** the receiver of a credit note and the 3-month window are untouched (other lanes).
- **Built in PR D13a (feat/fiscal-graphic-representation; the files the receiver is given, rule 12; Normativa DTE v2.0 11.3, Anexo I 4 and 8):** (a) **A neutral model in the SDK** (`FiscalRepresentation`, optional `represent(doc)` of the provider): plain rows, one table, the totals, the address of the consultation code and the file of the document; core draws it without knowing what a field means. (b) **`libs/fiscal/sv/src/sv-representation.ts`** makes it for the types 01, 03 and 05 with the names of the fields of the Anexos, from the stored document only (its payload and what the authority answered), so it is the same every time; the consultation address carries the environment of the document, the generation code and the date; a document of the test environment says it has no legal value and one of production does not; the file is the structure, `firmaElectronica` and `selloRecibido`, named by the generation code. A type is added by describing it in `LAYOUTS` (04, 06 and 14 need no rewrite). (c) **`libs/fiscal/runtime/src/fiscal-representation-pdf.ts`** draws the model with `pdfkit` (already a dependency) and the code with `uqr`; (d) **two new kinds of evidence** (`dte_file`, `representation`, migration `20270203100000` with its rollback) made by `FiscalEvidenceService` when the document is accepted, scanned, served by the same authenticated link and audited, never deleted.
- **Decisions of PR D13a (rule 12):** (1) **The files are evidence of the document (the existing mechanism), not a new table:** it already has the scan, the signed link, the audit, the store scope and the "never deleted" triggers, and a document keeps one of each kind. Rejected: a table of deliveries (nothing is delivered yet in this PR; the record of a delivery belongs to D13b). (2) **`uqr` 0.1.3 for the code** (MIT, no dependencies, no install script, CJS and ESM, published by the unjs maintainers in 2026), pinned; rejected: writing an encoder (a QR that does not scan is a fine of 30 % of the document) and `qrcode` (pulls `yargs` and `pngjs`). **`jsqr` 1.4.0** (Apache-2.0, no dependencies) is a dev dependency only, to prove in a spec that the code reads back as exactly the address. (3) **The names of the fields are the authority's, in Spanish, not i18n keys:** the document is a legal paper whose names are fixed by the Anexos; the app texts around it (panel labels) are in `es` and `en`. (4) **The PDF carries no instruction text:** the short instruction the Normativa asks for in a download site belongs to the delivery (D13b), which is where a person downloads. (5) **The date inside the PDF is the document's own date**, so the same document gives the same bytes. (6) **The picture is made only for an ACCEPTED document**, not with an "ANULADO" line for a voided one: the receiver is given the files when the document is accepted, so a first drawing after a void has no reason to exist, and the Normativa does not let the picture differ from the document. Rejected: a notice on voided documents (a second layout to keep in step with the authority's). (7) **A bound before drawing:** too large a text or too many rows is refused and logged, never cut.
- **Left by PR D13a (rule 12), with the PR that closes each:** **(a)** **D13b (Step 4B.7, next PR): the DELIVERY to the customer**, simultaneous with the document and never held for lack of payment: as an attachment through the message system of the order (the plugin's declared document capability and file limits, no channel named), by email with attachments when there is no channel or it takes none, and for a customer with neither, an action in the authenticated panel (with permission, audit and a record of the delivery) so the staff downloads both files and hands them over. The owner decided (2026-11-25) that there is NO public download link and that the public routes of rule 5 do not change; a public link, if ever needed, is its own PR with two readers and the owner's decision on rule 5. **(b)** the representation and the file of the events of invalidation and return (Anexo III, with their own layouts) are delivered by the same PR: **D13b**; **(c)** the types 04, 06 and 14 get their layout when **Step 4B.7c** builds them; **(d)** the layout is the one the Anexos' column of graphic representation asks (A and B fields), checked by reading, not against the sandbox: the owner's run of the minimum tests (**Step 4B.7c-6b**) is where the authority's own sample is compared; the "sin valor legal" text is ours, to be matched to the authority's wording there. **(e)** the panel offers the two new files for every accepted document, also one whose provider or type has no representation (the download then answers "not available", the existing text): the api should say which kinds exist: **D13b**; **(f)** the files are made only while the document is ACCEPTED (a voided one keeps the ones it has but never makes new ones, so a picture without a sign of invalidation is never first drawn after the void; the invalidation is its own event with its own representation, **D13b**); **(g)** a file of evidence is never deleted or made again (unique index and triggers): a defect of the picture or a change of layout is fixed with a new kind or version of file, never by regenerating, so the layout of a type must be read against the authority's sample (**Step 4B.7c-6b**) before the first real document; **(i)** the district (Anexo II fields 28 and 49, A) is shown by the CODE the document carries (`Dirección Distrito`), not by its name: the catalog of the repository (CAT-008) gives no municipality for a district code and the code repeats, so the name cannot be told; the complement carries the district name by the rule of field 29, and the full catalog closes it (**Step 4B.7c**, with the catalogs of 04 and 14); the receiver of an invoice shows no address (C); **(j)** the total of a cash-on-delivery order voids its guide even when a payment already covers it (the rule reads the method, not `codAmountFor`), and lines split or merged without a change of units count as a change: a void too many costs a click, a missed one costs money, so the rule stays conservative until **Step 4.14** (the edit form) refines it; the other things a plugin may send (a scheduled delivery date, a declared value) are not compared, which is safe only while no plugin sends them: **Step 4.15** checks it with the real carriers; **(k)** a void that fails on rejected credentials ends as a plain `CANCEL_FAILED` and does not flag the connection: **Step 4.15**; **(m)** left on purpose from the last review pass (one pass, not repeated): a connection that is not `active` when the job runs reads as a carrier that cannot void and leaves `not_supported` (`TDD_17 §4.8`, a disconnected connection), so a connection that comes back is settled by the agent; the move that leaves a guide `CANCEL_PENDING` with `not_supported` after a disconnect writes no line of history of its own; a pickup whose carrier call failed keeps its lowered count with the note and no retry (**Step 4.11**); a payload that does not fit its schema, or a job that dies of a database fault, leaves the guide `CANCEL_PENDING` until the sweep of **Step 7.6**; **(l)** two things the review of the engine found and the PR does not do on purpose: the duplicated 409 helper and the hand-written `Row` of `ShipmentCancellation` (a `GetPayload` type is not exported by the database lib yet): **Step 7.1**; **(h)** the order view and the create dialog that say "this order's guide was voided, make another" and show the warning of a guide that is `cancel_failed` are **Step 4.14**. Closes (a) and (c) of PR C1, the `CANCEL_SHIPMENT` job that (b) of PR C2b left, and (d) of PR C1 for `shipment.cancel_failed`. **PR D3** (coordinator's decision) closed this step: the labels of every active shipment of a split order in a bulk run (debt (e) of PR D1); asking the carrier again for a label that was not kept (debt (i) of PR D1, (g) of PR C1) moves to **Step 4.15**, which needs a real carrier adapter.
- **Built in PR D13b-1 (feat/fiscal-delivery; the delivery of the DTE and its graphic representation to the receiver, rule 12; Normativa DTE v2.0 section 11):** (a) **The event `FISCAL_DOCUMENT_ACCEPTED`** (ids only, bridged worker to api) is published in the same transaction that accepts the document, so a crash after the commit never loses it. (b) **`FiscalDeliveryService` in `apps/api/modules/fiscal`**: for an accepted document it makes sure both files exist (`FiscalEvidenceService.keep`, safe to repeat), then goes by what the customer's channel DECLARES (the plugin's document capability, the types and the size it takes, an open window; no channel is named): two documents of the conversation, or, when no channel takes both, one email (`ORDER_MESSAGE`) with both files attached and a fixed text (i18n `fiscalDelivery.text`, no advertising, no survey), or, when neither can carry them, a row `not_sent` with a reason code and an in-app and email alert to the people who hold `FISCAL_MANAGE` in the store. A provider that draws no files owes none (nothing recorded). A credit note is delivered like a sale. (c) **The table `fiscal_deliveries`** (one row for each document, unique by document; organization policy; migration `20270205100000` with its rollback) records the route and the reason, never an address; the audit entries are `fiscal.delivery_sent` and `fiscal.delivery_not_sent`. (d) **`OrderMessagesService.channelFor`** exposes its channel decision, so the two features cannot decide differently.
- **Decisions of PR D13b-1 (rule 12):** (1) **A service of its own, not a new `OrderMessageKind`:** the order messages are bound to templates of the store, its dispatch table, the consent to order messages and the "message of an order" pointer that the thread and the erasure read; a fiscal delivery is a legal duty with a fixed text, so none of those apply (rejected: a kind with a locked template; it would have mixed a legal duty with something the store edits). The cost is one more reader of the channel declarations, closed by (d). (2) **The evidence is copied to a file of the order** (`purpose ORDER`, server-side copy) because the evidence of a document cannot hang from a message (`chk_media_fiscal_evidence`); the copy is `CLEAN` because the platform made it from the row of the document. A file the scan found infected or could not scan is never given. (3) **A window that is closed sends no document through the channel:** the email is the way, as in the order messages. (4) **A failed try is retried three times in the listener; after the last one a `not_sent` row with `files_unavailable` is written, so the document never owes its files in silence.** (5) **An erased customer is recorded as `customer_erased` with no alert:** nobody is left to give the files to and nothing went wrong. (6) **The email is queued before the row is written, under a job id made from the document** (as the order messages do): a process that dies in between leaves one job that a second try adds once.
- **Left by PR D13b-1 (rule 12), with the PR that closes each:** **(a)** the action in the panel for the staff to download both files and hand them over (with permission, audit and a record that replaces the `not_sent` row), the events of invalidation and return (Anexo III), the button of evidence for voided documents with none, and the types 04 and 14: **D13b-2**, which also deletes the exemption `FiscalDelivery` of `scripts/isolation-exemptions.ts` and adds its case to `tests/security/tenant-isolation.spec.ts`; **(b)** an accepted document with no delivery row (the api was down when the event came, or the bridge lost it) is found by no sweep yet: **D13b-2** adds the check of the daily sweep that says it, the same one that offers the hand delivery; **(c)** the address used is the customer's of the order, not an address typed in the receiver's data of the document (sealed): the receiver's own address is read by **D13b-2** with the hand delivery; **(d)** the norm asks, for a customer with no means at all, a secure download site or, at the customer's request, the representation on paper: the panel of the issuer is NOT a delivery, so the `not_sent` row is a pending duty, not a closed one; **the owner's decision on paper at request is pending** (no public link, per the decision of 2026-11-25); **(e)** the channel is the first one that decides (`channelFor` returns one conversation): a customer with an open conversation on a channel that takes no documents and another open one that does gets the email instead of the second; **D13b-2** makes the decision list the candidates; **(f)** the email job is kept an hour after it is sent so that a repeat after a failed write does not send twice: a repeat after that hour, or two concurrent tries for one document, can send twice, an accepted trade-off because the event is delivered once; **(g)** a reason code for a failure of the queue or the database (today `files_unavailable`) when the hand delivery of **D13b-2** needs to tell them apart; **(h)** the receiver of the delivery is the customer of the order, not the person the document names: a document for a company with its own tax id is given to the customer who bought, with the company's data in the file (a product decision, written here: it is who the sale was made with); **D13b-2** reads the receiver's own address from the document; **(i)** the copy of the files that a channel carries is a file of the order (`purpose ORDER`) that holds the receiver's tax id, name and address: whoever sees the order's gallery or the conversation sees it, with no `FISCAL_VIEW` and no reach check of the fiscal documents, so it widens who sees fiscal evidence; it is kept by the retention of the order and the sweep of ten years, and the erasure of the data subject touches `purpose MESSAGE` only, coherent with the legal retention; **D13b-2** decides whether the copy is hidden from the gallery; **(k)** orphans of the delivery under `orders/`: the files a try copies for a channel are removed when the try knows it wrote nothing, and after an ambiguous failure of the transaction the ones with no `Media` row are removed too, but a process that dies between the copy and the claim, or a failed delete, leaves an object with no `Media` row; the orphan sweep reads only `uploads/` and `messages/` and the retention of order documents deletes by row, so nothing reaches it, not even the erasure of the data subject, and it holds the receiver's tax id, name and address: **D13b-2** adds `orders/` to the orphan reader (an object under `orders/<orderId>/<mediaId>/` with no `Media` row of that id and older than the TTL, never by a blind prefix); **(j)** the message of a channel shows as a plain file in the thread: a line that names it as the fiscal document comes with the web step of **D13b-2**.
- **Built in PR D13b-2a (feat/fiscal-delivery-events; the hand delivery of the files of an accepted document, rule 12; Normativa DTE v2.0 section 11):** (a) **`GET` and `POST /fiscal/documents/:id/delivery`** (`FiscalHandDeliveryService`): the first says how the files reached the receiver (state `pending` when there is no row, the route and a reason code, never an address) and which of the two files exist (permission `FISCAL_VIEW`); the second records that a person gave them by hand, by the means `download` (both files, taken from the evidence route: signed link, clean files only, audited) or `paper` (the representation alone, printed at the customer's request), with the permission `FISCAL_MANAGE`, the reach of the person (a document out of it is a 404) and the audit entry `fiscal.delivery_handed_over`. No public route and no change to rule 5. (b) **The row** `fiscal_deliveries` gains `hand_means`, `handed_over_by`, `handed_over_at` and the route `manual` (migration `20270208100000` with its rollback): a row `not_sent` becomes `sent` by `manual` and keeps the reason the system could not send, a document with no row gets its row; a repeat is the same record (no second row, no second audit entry); a document the system delivered answers 409 `already_delivered`. (c) **The daily check** has a new kind, `delivery_missing`: an accepted document with a file of the receiver and no delivery row an hour after it was accepted gets its acceptance event published again by the worker (the delivery is idempotent). (d) **The web** offers the files of a voided document only when the api lists them (they are made while the document is accepted and never after), and a section with the state of the delivery and the two buttons to record the hand over. (e) **`orders/` in the orphan sweep** (`parseOrderObjectKey`): an object under `orders/<order>/<media>/` with all three ids in the shape we write, no row of that media id in its store, and older than 48 hours (longer than every retry of the listener). (f) **The exemption `FiscalDelivery` is gone** and `tests/security/tenant-isolation.spec.ts` has its case (read and record by a person who does not reach the document).
- **Decisions of PR D13b-2a (rule 12):** (1) **The record lives in the existing row, not in a second table:** one row for each document is the invariant the delivery and the check rely on; the alternative (a table of hand deliveries) would need a rule to say which of two rows wins. (2) **The hand delivery records a fact a person asserts, it does not prove it:** the system cannot know that the files reached the receiver; the audit trail says who, when and by which means, and the download itself is audited by the evidence route. (3) **Paper needs the representation alone,** the download needs both files, so a provider that draws a file of the document and no picture still gives the paper nothing and a person is not asked to assert what cannot be done. (4) **A voided document owes no delivery** (409 `delivery_not_owed`): its invalidation is its own event (D13b-2b). (5) **The orphan sweep reads `orders/` by the three ids of the key and the id of the media,** never by a prefix, with a TTL of 48 hours against the 24 of an unconfirmed upload. (6) **The check publishes the event again only when a file of the receiver exists,** so a provider that draws none (no row is written for it) never produces a finding that cannot close; a document accepted whose files could not be made at all is the evidence repair's business (it is made when asked). (7) **A hand delivery is refused (409 `delivery_running`) while the document is younger than the grace of the check and has no row,** because the email of the system is queued before its row is written and a person who records at that moment would have the customer given the files twice. (8) **Only a clean file counts as there to be handed over** (the evidence route serves nothing else, and the system delivery refuses an infected or unscannable one). (9) **The first nightly check after the deploy delivers the documents accepted earlier that have files and no row, up to 120 days back:** the files are owed whatever the date, a late delivery closes the duty and an old document left silent does not; accepted on purpose, and the number of findings is in the gauge of the check.
- **Left by PR D13b-2a (rule 12), with the PR that closes each:** **(a)** **D13b-2b, the delivery of the event of invalidation (and the return, when it is built) with its graphic representation** (Normativa v2.0 section 11, page 23): the signed event and the seal of the authority are NOT kept today (the transmission signs the event and keeps only the authority's answer), so the PR adds a sealed column on `fiscal_documents` for the signed event (sealed like the other payloads, with its rollback, its policy and its isolation case), `VoidResult` of the SDK carrying the event, two kinds of evidence (`void_dte_file`, `void_representation`), `representVoid` in the SDK and in the provider of El Salvador (the layout of the functional manual), a bridged event `FISCAL_DOCUMENT_VOIDED`, its listener and the delivery with the same routes as the document. It does not start until the PR that adds the code and the moment of the invalidation event to `fiscal_documents` and rewrites `fiscal_document_guard` is in `main`: both touch that table and that guard. **(b)** **An invalidation recovered by consultation has no event of its own to give:** the file of an event is never made incomplete (rule 12), so such a void is recorded `not_sent` with an alert, and the staff hands over the data the authority's answer holds (the code and the seal) from the panel; owner of this: D13b-2b. **(c)** the receiver of the delivery is still the customer of the order, and the address typed in the receiver's data of the document (sealed) is not read: **D13b-2b** reads it with the delivery of the event; until then the hand delivery covers the customer with no channel and no email. **(d)** the channel is still the first one that decides (`channelFor` returns one conversation): the list of candidates is **D13b-2b**. **(e)** the copy of the files that a channel carries is a file of the order that anybody who sees the gallery of the order sees: whether it is hidden from the gallery is decided in **D13b-2b**, with the line in the thread that names the message as the fiscal document (the web step of the delivery). **(f)** the owner's decision on paper at the customer's request stays open in one point: the system records that paper was given, it prints nothing by itself; the representation is printed from the PDF the evidence route serves. **(g)** the types 04 and 14 have no representation layout yet (they are built with their own PR); **(h)** the delivery before the seal exists (contingency) is not done: the files are made when the document is accepted, as the norm asks for the document with its seal.
- **Debts written at the review of PR D13b-2a (rule 12), with the owner of each:** **(a)** `fiscal_deliveries` has no trigger: `platform_app` and `platform_worker` hold UPDATE and DELETE on it (from D13b-1) although the schema says a delivery is never deleted; a guard like the one of `fiscal_documents` (no delete; an update only from `not_sent` to `sent` by the route `manual`, with who and when) closes it: **D13b-2b-2**, which changes that table anyway (the subject of the delivery and its unique index). **(b)** the check `delivery_missing` publishes the acceptance event again each night for up to 120 days with no cap for each document. Decided under rule 12 that it is enough: the check is paginated and capped by run, the delivery is idempotent, and every terminal outcome writes a row that ends the finding (the listener tries three times and then `recordFailure` writes a `not_sent` row), so only an event that leaves no row (the api down for the whole window, a failure of the write itself) repeats, and that case should repeat until it works; the gauge of the check shows a document that never closes, and a cap that stopped trying would be the silent loss the rule forbids. **(c)** to watch: `orphan-media-cleaner.integration.spec.ts` failed once in a review run ("an unattached avatar was not dropped", a Prisma known request error) and passed 39/39 on the second run; the pass involved is the one of avatars, which this PR did not change; not investigated here: if it fails again it is its own fix PR, with the log of the run.
