- [x] **Metadata of files that are not static pictures (PR strip-image-metadata, rule 12; closed in PR 7.1-I):** a gif, an animated WebP and an animated PNG are no longer left as they came, and a PDF, a docx and an xlsx are cleaned on upload. **Animations** (`animated-image-cleaner.ts`, called by `sanitizeImage`; `image/gif` joined `ImageSanitizing.CONTENT_TYPES`): the encoder is never used, because it would flatten them (#181); the container is walked and the blocks that carry metadata are cut out, every other byte is copied, so the frames, the delays and the loop are the same bytes. Gif: the comment, the plain text and every application extension but the loop count (`NETSCAPE2.0`, `ANIMEXTS1.0`; XMP lives in one); WebP: the `EXIF` and `XMP ` chunks, the flags that announce them and the RIFF size; PNG: `tEXt`, `zTXt`, `iTXt`, `eXIf`, `tIME`. The result is read back before it replaces anything (same format, size and number of frames; no EXIF or XMP; the `acTL` chunk still there) and a file that cannot be walked is refused like a picture that cannot be decoded. `carriesMetadata` answers for an animation by asking whether that walk would cut something, so the sweep of stored pictures cleans stored gifs and animations too. **Documents** (`document-sanitizer.ts`, called by the scan of the media pipeline for every purpose but financial evidence; the worker, inside the same decode slot): a PDF loses its information dictionary and its XMP stream (the objects are deleted too, so the old values are not left in the file; the result is loaded again and checked); a docx or an xlsx is a zip whose `docProps/core.xml`, `app.xml` and `custom.xml` are written again empty, whose thumbnail is removed with its relationship, and which is zipped again with a fixed entry date (two runs give the same bytes; the zip is bounded by `DocumentSanitizing.MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES` and `MAX_ZIP_ENTRIES`). A document is never refused for this: if it cannot be cleaned without risk (an encrypted PDF, a **signed** PDF, whose signature a rewrite would break, a damaged file, a package that is too big once opened) it is kept as it came, logged with the media id only, and the scan goes on. The original is not lost: the new bytes are made and read back in memory, the object is written only then, and a failed write leaves the original and retries (spec `media-pipeline.documents.spec.ts`). Financial and fiscal evidence (`isEvidenceMedia`) is kept as it came, as for pictures. **Left on purpose (rule 12):** (a) documents already stored: closed by the item "Existing documents" below (`ExistingDocumentSanitizer`, PR `strip-document-metadata-sweep`). (b) What a document keeps, because removing it changes the content or the review trail and is not done blind: in a **docx or xlsx** the authors of comments and of tracked changes (`w:author`), the revision ids, custom XML parts, macros and embedded files, and the **paths of the author's machine**: in an xlsx `xl/workbook.xml` `x15ac:absPath` (`C:\Users\<name>\...`), in a docx `word/_rels/settings.xml.rels` `attachedTemplate` (`file:///C:/Users/<name>/...Normal.dotm`) and any external link with a `file:///` target; in a **PDF** the embedded files and the form fields (the XMP of a page or an image, `/PieceInfo` and the information of every earlier revision are removed, and so is any object nothing points to from the catalog; bookmarks and comments stay, and the read-back compares them). A rule per part, with the owner's choice for the author paths, is **Step 7.3, task `office-user-paths-and-embedded-media`: closed by the item "Office user paths and embedded photos" of Step 7.3**. (c) A PDF is written again without object streams, so a PDF that used them may grow (a result over the file limit is kept as it came). (d) Legacy `.doc`, `.xls` and OpenDocument are not accepted types. **The pictures inside a docx or xlsx (`word/media`, `xl/media`) and inside a PDF are not cleaned and may carry EXIF with GPS**: they are the same files as a picture upload, and the sanitizer of pictures does not run on them; cleaning them (decode and re-encode each part, with the memory bound of `withDecodeSlot`) is **Step 7.3, task `office-user-paths-and-embedded-media`: closed by the item "Office user paths and embedded photos" of Step 7.3**. (e) No spec measures the memory or the time of cleaning a PDF or a package at the file limit; it runs inside `withDecodeSlot` (one at a time per process), the inflated size of a package is capped at `DocumentSanitizing.MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES` (64 MB) and 5000 parts, but `unzipSync`, `zipSync` and the parse of pdf-lib are synchronous and block the event loop of the worker while they run: a worker thread with a deadline per document: **closed by the item "Document thread" of Step 7.3** (the parse no longer runs on the event loop); the lists of relationships are capped at `DocumentSanitizing.MAX_RELATIONSHIPS_BYTES` (64 KB) and read without a backtracking regular expression (a list of `<Relationship ` that never closes cost seconds with the first version, now it is refused at once). (f) `docProps/custom.xml` is written empty, so a template that fills a field from a custom property or a sensitivity label shows nothing after the cleaning; accepted, because custom properties are free text the author chose to store. (g) A gif that cannot be walked even with the tolerance of the cleaner (zero padding, a missing trailer and an unknown application block are accepted) is refused like any picture that cannot be decoded and its file deleted; a gif that a browser plays but whose block structure is broken mid-way is the only case, and the count of such refusals (`image_not_sanitizable` on `image/gif`) is to be watched with the alert of Step 7.3. (h) A PDF with a digital signature (`/ByteRange`) or one that pdf-lib cannot load is kept as it came with its properties, and **the cleaning can be evaded on purpose**: a `/ByteRange` put in a PDF on purpose reads as signed, and a zip64 package is not read, so the original stays; that keeps only the metadata of the customer who chose to evade it, never someone else's; so is a docx or xlsx whose zip is zip64, whose parts do not match their CRC-32, or that has more than the cap of parts. (i) The review of the PR found and fixed (the second round, by two independent readers: a PDF cleaner that deleted bookmarks and comments because they looked like an information dictionary, now it deletes only what the trailer names, `/Metadata`, `/PieceInfo` and objects nothing points to, and the read-back compares pages, comments, bookmarks and the count of reachable objects; the quadratic regular expression over the relationships): the date of the zip entries read as local time (a docx was never cleaned west of UTC), old information dictionaries and page XMP that stayed in a PDF as objects nothing pointed to, a part cut short by a wrong size in the zip (now every part is checked against the CRC-32 of the central directory), a gif refused for padding or a missing trailer, a core-properties part under another path, and a row left without its mark when the update failed after the write.

Needs a re-mux without the metadata atoms (ffmpeg in the worker image); owner: this step. **Decision of the owner (2026-11-23): option A, ffmpeg in the worker image; the agent CAN send video and audio; it must be closed before real customers are opened.** Split in three PRs: **J-1 (this PR, 7.1-J-1): the tool and the service, nothing wired.** (1) `docker/node-service.Dockerfile`, stage `ffmpeg-build`: ffmpeg built from the source tarball (8.1.3 at first, 9.1 now: see the bullet of the update below) with the version and the SHA-256 PINNED in two `ARG`s (a download that does not match stops the build; no `apk add ffmpeg`, whose package is GPL and carries every codec and protocol), LGPL 2.1+ (`--disable-gpl --disable-nonfree --disable-version3`, shared libraries so that the relinking right is met by the files), `--disable-everything` plus five demuxers (mov, mp3, ogg, wav, aac), six muxers, the `file` protocol alone, `--disable-network` (the sockets are not compiled in), and one decoder (aac: a raw ADTS file has no sample rate until its first frame is decoded). The compiler stays in the build stage; the runtime image gets `/opt/ffmpeg` (root-owned, read-only for `node`) and, for the worker alone, `util-linux-misc` (`prlimit`); the build stops if the tools do not start on that base. The licence texts travel in `/opt/ffmpeg/share/licenses`. (2) `FfmpegAvCleaner` (`apps/worker/src/media`) runs `ffprobe`, `ffmpeg -c copy` and `ffprobe` again, each as a CHILD process with an empty environment, no shell, no stdin, `detached` (its own process group, killed whole at the deadline and when it closes), cwd a private `mkdtemp` directory (0700, files 0600) that is deleted whatever happens, `prlimit` limits (address space 1 GiB, 20 CPU seconds, file size, 64 open files, no core), a 20 s deadline per child, output of the probe capped at 512 KiB and nothing the tool prints ever logged (only the id and a reason code). The command lines are constants (`av-sanitizer.ts`: the content type picks a row of `AvSanitizing.FORMATS`; the file names are fixed and relative; the formats are NAMED with `-f`, never probed; `-protocol_whitelist file`; `-map_metadata -1`, `-map_metadata:s -1`, `-map_chapters -1`, `-fflags +bitexact`; audio drops the cover with `-vn`; video and audio streams only, so the data tracks of an action camera, where its GPS lives, and subtitles are not carried). (3) The copy is read back before it is handed over (`verifyCleaned`): same video and audio streams in the same order and codecs, same length within 0.25 s or 1 %, no cover, no data stream, no tag outside the ones a muxer writes by itself and with the values it writes (`handler_name` is `VideoHandler` or `SoundHandler`, never a text; a file as it came with any other value is cleaned), no `ISO6709`, `com.apple.quicktime.` or `creation_time` in the bytes, no ID3 tag at the start. (4) It NEVER loses or refuses the original: a file that cannot be cleaned without risk (not what its type says, damaged or cut short, encrypted, over the limit, a deadline, a copy that fails the checks) comes back `untouched` with a reason and the id is logged; an error of the machine (the tools are missing) is thrown so that the queue retries. (5) Agnostic of channel and carrier (rule 13): the types come from `AllowedContentTypes`, and a spec fixes that every video and audio type has its row and no other does. (6) Specs: the pure half (`av-sanitizer.spec.ts`), the process half with two fake tools (`ffmpeg-av-cleaner.spec.ts`: deadline, group kill, empty environment, fixed arguments, directory removed, the original kept in every failure) and the real tools (`ffmpeg-av-cleaner.integration.spec.ts`, ffmpeg installed by the integration job with a step that stops the job if `/usr/bin/ffmpeg` is not there; on a machine without ffmpeg the suite is skipped, because a spec cannot read the environment to tell CI apart). `scripts/smoke-av-image.ts` runs the build the IMAGE ships on the same clips, with `--network none`, in the image job. **Left, with the step that closes it:** **J-2** hooks the cleaner to the scan of what enters and what leaves (the heavy queue, the media pipeline, the agent's upload), and decides what the customer sees of a file that stays as it came; **J-3** sweeps the stored files with the guard of versioning (`ExistingPictureSanitizer` as the model), with the same marks in the row. Until J-2 lands nothing calls the cleaner: video and audio still go out with their metadata. (a) The memory limit is `RLIMIT_AS`; on a host without `prlimit` (a laptop) only the deadline applies, and the image build checks that the worker has it. (b) The bytes of the file are written to the temporary directory of the container (`os.tmpdir()`): a node with a read-only root file system needs an `emptyDir` on `/tmp`; owner Step 7.3 (deployment), with the sizing of the memory limit of the worker container for one decode plus one ffmpeg (measured by the reader of J-2, e3: the parent holds a 25 MB read plus the copy, a peak under about 150 MB, plus the ffmpeg child under its `prlimit` of 1 GiB of address space; the container limit is still not measured, owner 7.3/7.5) (about 1 GiB of address space, far less resident). (c) The check of the copy compares the video and audio streams, not their packets: a hostile container that ffmpeg reads differently from a player is not detected by this; the copy is a new container written by the muxer, so what it holds is what the demuxer found. (d) The unit and integration specs of the cleaner run against the ffmpeg of the CI runner (Ubuntu, GPL, with more demuxers); the shipped build is run by the image job on the same clips; a clip type that only the shipped build reads differently is caught there. (f) **Always rewritten (decision of the coordinator, 2026-11-23, closed in this PR):** the probe sees only what ffprobe shows, so an atom it does not show (the GPS of a dashcam in `free` or `udta`, a wav iXML chunk) would have left as "already clean" with its coordinates; the early return is gone and every file is copied and read back (`hadMetadata` in the result is for the caller's log only). (g) A video with an attached cover picture is kept as it came (`cover_kept`: the copy carries the picture, with its own EXIF); closes in J-2 with a decision (drop the picture stream with `-map 0:v:0`-style maps for video, or keep). (e) Updating ffmpeg: change the two `ARG`s together after reading the release notes and the security advisories of the demuxers in the list; the image job runs the build on the clips on every PR, and the checksum is the one of https://ffmpeg.org/releases/ **Trivy does NOT see this binary** (it reads OS packages and lockfiles, and a ffmpeg compiled by hand in `/opt/ffmpeg` is neither), so the parser of hostile files has no CVE watch from it: the control is `.github/workflows/ffmpeg-version.yml`, weekly and on demand, which fails when `FFMPEG_VERSION` is behind the newest release of ffmpeg.org (a failed run opens an issue (once; `gh issue create`, `issues: write`) that the owner of the repository sees, besides the mail of Actions; owner Step 7.3 dependency review updates the two `ARG`s before real customers are opened; closes when the workflow has run green once on `main` AND a red provoked has produced the issue: `workflow_dispatch` runs the checkout of the branch it is launched from, so it is launched from a branch whose Dockerfile has an old pin. A failure of the bucket, of the database or of the cleaner that is not the missing tool is NOT the file's fault either: the try is given back (`release`: the row holds again what the batch read, only while it still holds this try), the run stops at the first failure of the bucket or the database (the next file would fail the same way) and goes on after a failure of the cleaner alone, so an outage of any length never turns good videos into final ones with their metadata inside (found by two readers of the PR). owner Step 7.3, closes when the CI has ffmpeg and the bucket in one job; (b) an object that changes while it is cleaned leaves the row with its try counted, so a file that keeps changing ends `attempts_exhausted`; accepted (a file that is rewritten by someone else three times in ten minutes is not a stored file), owner 7.3; (c) `platform_av_cleaning_total{result=av_unavailable}` counts runs, not files; (d) about 20 files per run and six runs an hour: a store with thousands of videos takes days, sized on purpose for one file at a time; owner 7.3 measures it on the first real bucket; (f) the batch is ordered by id, so `av_unavailable` rows with low ids come first on every run; while the tools are missing the run ends after the first file (one object read), and once they are back those rows are cleaned and leave the front: accepted, owner 7.3 revisits if the tools flap; (e) (Closed by MED-144: `assertMediaSendable` and `isReadyToSend` in `media-guard.ts` read `avCleaning` and refuse a kept file with `FILE_UNAVAILABLE`; the J-2 check that nothing leaks was wrong, a kept file ends `clean`.) **Condition that stays:** the first feature that forwards or reuses a stored attachment must call `assertMediaSendable`, never `assertMediaServable` alone, and J-3 must write the cleaned mark (`sanitized: true`) when it cleans a file, which is what makes it sendable again; (g) a file that makes the cleaner throw N times in a row while the tools are healthy (a bug, not an outage) is released and taken again on every run without ever becoming final, and as the batch goes by id it can sit at the front and fill it; today `ffmpeg-av-cleaner` throws only `AvToolUnavailable` (three places) and disk or spawn failures, so the risk is low, and the log `could not be cleaned for a reason that is not its own` names the ids; owner 7.3; closes by making the file final (`not_cleanable`) after N repetitions with the tools healthy (a counter of releases per row, separate from the attempts that count); (h) if the write that gives the try back fails because the database itself is down, the number stays: at most one try of one file per run, as the run stops at the first failure.

(j) the worker's IAM role needs `s3:GetBucketVersioning` (and the encryption read the api already uses): without it the answer is `unknown` and both sweeps stop in staging and production with only a warning every ten minutes; Step 7.5 checks the grant when it provisions the bucket, and the gap metric already shows it as a non-zero value. Spec: `existing-document-sanitizer.spec.ts`, three abandoned runs and a fourth that does not open it. (l) the key of a row is used as it is only under `stores/<storeId>/` with no `.` or `..` step (`objectKeysOf`, the check of the deletions of #893); any other key is marked `foreign_key`, logged at error level and never read, written or deleted. (o) the guard is asked at the start of a run, not during it (a run lasts up to 7 minutes): a versioning turned off in the middle is seen on the next run.

(e) the variants (`thumb`, `medium`) were always made by the encoder and carry no metadata, so they are not touched; (g) **owner decision (2026-11-21, closed):** a re-encoded picture cannot be recovered unless the production bucket has object versioning on (`StorageService.inspectProtection` reports it): versioning ON with a 30-day noncurrent expiration is decided and the sweep does not run in production without it (Step 7.5, "Production bucket lifecycle"; the code guard is a task of Step 7.3), and (h) a row that fails three times (a machine short of memory for 30 minutes counts) ends as `failed` and waits for someone to clear its `scan_result`, a metric and an alert for `failed` rows belong to Step 7.3; (f) video, audio, PDF, Office and animated pictures stay as listed in the two items above (owner: this step, a separate PR with `ffmpeg` in the worker image).

The audit viewer of a store does NOT cover them, and nobody should read its silence as "the cleanup did not run". The metadata is `{ counts, more, failed }` (`run-audit.ts`). A run that deleted nothing, stopped on no full batch and failed nowhere writes no entry (one row for each store each night would bury the useful ones; the log line still says it ran). The entry of a run that failed is queued before the job fails (the write is detached, like every audit entry of the worker; a database that is down loses it, with an error log and the `AUDIT_WRITE_FAILURES` count), and a retry of the job writes another entry with the counts of that attempt; a failure of the first read of the retention run, before any category, leaves no entry. The sweep of erased customers reports `more: ["customers"]` when a store filled its page of 50 or the lock margin stopped it, and its `customers` and `skipped` counters never make an entry alone. The 10-minute sweep of stored pictures (#872) is not audited: it is not a nightly run and would write 144 rows a day; its log line stays. **Left on purpose (rule 12; owner Step 7.3):** (a) the platform cleanup mixes categories of every store in one entry: the deletions of the per-store categories (webhook deliveries, hourly rollups, merged customers) are not visible to the store that lost them: give each store its own entry from `perStore` if the owner wants them in the tenant viewer; (b) the viewer shows the three new actions by their raw name: the labels belong to the web table of **PR 7.2-F**'s follow-up (item (f) of 7.2-E), which must list `retention.run` for the store; (c) what remained of the old task moves to the next line.

- [x] **DSR flow, H1a: the public intake and the verification, server side (PR `feat/customers-dsr-flow`, Step 7.2-H; design in `~/qa-reportes-2026-11-16/DISENO-7.2-H-DSR.md`; independent readers: 6b and 57):** migration `20270125100000_dsr_flow` (with rollback): the columns of the review and of the request on `data_subject_requests` (`subject_email_hash`, `subject_customer_ids`, `notify_to_encrypted`, `approvals`, `erasure_due_at`, `reviewed_by`, `reviewed_at`), the public key of a form on `stores.dsr_public_key` (NULL = the store takes no public requests), the permission `customers:dsr_review` (given to the Admin roles that exist; H1b uses it) and two SECURITY DEFINER lookups for the flow that has no tenant context (`resolve_dsr_store`, `resolve_dsr_verification`, the pattern of `resolve_api_key`; listed in `rls-definer-catalog.spec.ts`, proved in `tests/security/rls-dsr-resolvers.spec.ts`). `POST /compliance/dsr` is public and only counts (Redis, per address and per store a day, always, with or without a customer) and queues a job `dsr-intake` whose payload is sealed (AES-GCM) and carries no address in its name or id; it answers the same `202 { accepted: true }` whether the flow is off, the key is unknown, the address belongs to no customer, or the request repeats an open one, and a 429 only by the counts. The worker (`DsrIntakeWorker`) opens the payload, finds the store by its public key, matches the customers of the store by the trimmed lower-case address (exact, never `ILIKE`), writes ONE open request per (store, address hash, kind) under an advisory lock with the address hashed and sealed (never in the clear), a token of 256 bits stored as its SHA-256 hash with the id of the request as subject, and queues the mail (`dsr-verification`, en and es; the token goes in the fragment). `POST /compliance/dsr/verify` claims the token and moves the request to `manual_review` in ONE transaction, with one error for an unknown, used or expired token, a request that no longer waits, or the flow being off; confirming proves the mailbox and nothing more, and nothing is done to any customer. Audit entries hold ids and the kind, never an address. **The flow is OFF:** `DSR_PUBLIC_INTAKE_ENABLED=false` (env schema, `.env.example`), and the schema REFUSES TO START with it on while `dsrExecutorAvailable()` is false (the second lock is in `DSR_CONFIG`).
  **Decisions (rule 12; the coordinator's and the readers'):** (1) the public routes are an exception to rule 5 (no `AuthGuard`/`TenantGuard`: the person who asks for their data has no account) and the store comes from the BODY as a random public key, an exception to rule 2 (it only lets a person ask, never read); both are for the owner to confirm (`PENDIENTES-DUENIO-M7.md`). (2) Erasure respects `ERASURE_GRACE_PERIOD_DAYS` (30 days, cancelable). (3) One approver in the MVP, audited, ready to ask for two (`DSR_ERASURE_APPROVALS_REQUIRED`). (4) Open orders, shipments, returns, remittances or balances block an erasure and the request stays in manual review. (5) A pasted address is trimmed and lower-cased before it is checked. **Rejected:** the id of the store in the body (guessable), a lookup in the api (a 429 or a timing would tell whether the address is a customer).

The list answers the page of the api (`data`, `nextCursor`, `hasMore`; filters `status` and `type`; a cursor of another store finds no position). Approving: only from `manual_review`; `409 DSR_EXECUTOR_UNAVAILABLE` for an erasure while `dsrExecutorAvailable()` is false AND for any kind that is not an erasure (no executor exists for access or portability until H2b); the admin who made the request cannot approve it (403); in ONE transaction, with the row of the request locked and the customers locked in id order, it checks that each customer of `subject_customer_ids` still exists, is not erased or merged away and still has the address (compared by its keyed hash), else `409 DSR_SUBJECT_CHANGED`, and counts the open work of those customers in the store (open orders, guides not at the end of their life, returns in progress, lines of draft remittances, receivables = delivered orders never paid + cash on delivery the carrier has not settled), else `409 DSR_BLOCKED_BY_OPEN_WORK` with the counts; it then writes `in_progress`, `erasure_due_at = now + ERASURE_GRACE_PERIOD_DAYS`, `approvals`, `reviewed_by/at` and the reason in `notes`. The audit entry holds ids and counts, never the reason or an address. Rejecting needs `manual_review`; it queues the closing mail (`dsr-result`, `rejected`) INSIDE the transaction, after the update and before the commit, so a queue that is down rolls the decision back (tested), and the sealed address and its hash are NULL. Cancelling is an `UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'in_progress' AND erasure_due_at > now()` after taking the row lock; a second cancel, an approval against a rejection, or a cancel after the date lose with a 409 (concurrency tests: one winner, one mail). Ended requests answer `409 DSR_ALREADY_COMPLETED`, any other wrong state `409 DSR_NOT_REVIEWABLE`. The sweep `EXPIRE_DSR_REQUESTS` (03:25 UTC, leader lock, `DsrExpireScheduler` → `DsrExpireSweeper`) closes, store by store and one transaction per request, every `pending_verification` request with no unused and unexpired token: `rejected` with `verification_expired`, address and hash NULL, the person told (`dsr-result`, `expired`), `dsr.expired` audited with ids; it touches no customer. Tests: `tests/api/dsr-review.spec.ts` (20 cases through the real app and database: permission, tenancy, every 409, concurrency, the failing queue), `tests/api/dsr-expire.spec.ts` (4 cases against the worker role), the case of `tests/security/tenant-isolation.spec.ts` (`dataSubjectRequest`: read, list, approve; plus `describe('data subject requests')` with approve, reject and cancel by a foreign id), and `DataSubjectRequest` left `scripts/isolation-exemptions.ts`.
  **Decisions of H1b (rule 12):** (1) no `JobNames.DSR_EXPIRE`: the schedulers of the repo that sweep rows run the sweeper directly under a leader lock (like `CLEAN_EXPIRED_EXPORTS`); a job name with no consumer would be dead code. (2) A cancelled request has its own status `cancelled` (the traspaso asked for NULL on "cancelled" and the enum had no such value); the person is told with the `dsr-result` notice, outcome `cancelled` (new text in en and es). (3) Approving something that is not an erasure answers `409 DSR_EXECUTOR_UNAVAILABLE` too: an `in_progress` access with nobody to run it would be the inert approval 6b and 8c refused. (4) The reviewer's text goes in `notes` (the row), never in the audit entry or a log. (5) `rejectionReason` of a reviewer's decision is the constant `reviewer_decision`.
  **Left by H1b (rule 12, owner H2b unless said):** (a) the closing mail goes in the store's default language (`stores.default_locale`), because the request does not keep the language of the form (it is sealed in the job of the intake only); H2b may seal it with `notify_to_encrypted`. (h) An address that does not open (a key that changed) never keeps a request from being decided or expired: it is closed with no mail and an error log by request id (tested in both paths). (i) `approve` of access or portability answers `DSR_EXECUTOR_UNAVAILABLE` and only rejection is possible for them; H2b gives them their approval path. (g) The web of the queue (Settings → Compliance) is H2b.

(f) owner 7.7: the sweep audits per request, not a run entry with the counts of the night (the report is logged). (g) the whole request is one transaction of `DSR_ERASE_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT_MS` (2 min): a request that names very many customers of one address would not fit and would go back to review after its tries; the number of customers with one address in a store is small, no cap is set. (h) a merge into a customer of the request that can still be undone (window 30 d, longer than the 7-day grace) gives the request back to review as `undoable_merge` with no tries spent: the reviewer waits for the window or undoes the merge, then approves again. (i) the sweep checks the merge itself before `erase()` (which also refuses): the two rules must change together. (j) the check of the customers (`checkDsrSubject`) deliberately counts an already erased customer as done (resumable), while the approval of H1b rejects it: when (b) unifies them the approval keeps rejecting. (k) the guard that only the sweep erases is the list of files that import the library plus a pattern on `.erase(` and on the system actor in the api: a syntax-tree guard is Step 7.3. (l) **BEFORE the public form is turned on (owner H2b-3, condition of closing; (o) below shares it):** an erasure whose sealed address cannot be opened (a key that changed) ends with NO mail and the log carries only the request id, so the person is never told that their data was erased (a right of the data subject, TDD_05 §10.3): H2b-3 must give it an alternative notice or a visible mark in the review queue (a row of the ended requests that were never notified). (m) the time budget of the run (28 min) plus one last transaction of 2 min can pass the 30-min leader lock: safe (the claim and `SKIP LOCKED` keep a second run from taking the same request), only noisy. (n) the audit entries of the sweep (`dsr.erasure_completed`, `dsr.erasure_returned`) are written inside the transaction that does the move (`beforeCommit`), so a death after the commit cannot lose them, and a rollback leaves none (tested with the real audit service against the database: a rollback leaves no `customer.erased` row and the completed and returned entries exist). Not pinned by a test: that the `dsr.erasure_completed` call sits inside the transaction (it is the line before the `return`; simulating a death after the commit is not practical and the risk is low). (o) **BEFORE the public form is turned on (owner H2b-2, same condition of closing as (l)):** the closing mail job holds the address in the clear, so it has `removeOnFail: true`; the sealed address of the request is cleared in the SAME transaction that queues the job, and `unsentNoticesOf` only finds requests that still hold it. So a queue that is down when the sweep tries is retried the next night, but a job that is queued and then spends ALL its attempts in the mail queue is dropped and the person gets no notice and no retry. H2b-2 either keeps the sealed address until the mail processor confirms the send, or gives the ended request a visible `notice_failed` state for the reviewer.

The ZIP goes to the bucket as a stream (`putStream`) with a byte counter that stops it past `DSR_EXPORT_MAX_ZIP_BYTES` (512 MiB), at most `DSR_EXPORT_MAX_FILES` (1,000) files; a file that disappears mid-stream fails the try. Closes H2b-2 (c) except the caution mark and (d). **Left by C3 (rule 12):** (a) owner H2b-3 with the adviser, **BEFORE the public form is turned on:** the public download with its own token and the ZIP encrypted by the app (H2b-2 (a), (b)) are NOT done here; `dsrPublicFlowReady()` stays false until they are. (b) owner the adviser: the caution mark and the internal notes stay out of the export on purpose (an opinion of the store, not data the person gave); the adviser confirms it, and the files of fiscal evidence (the answers of the authority, which carry no customer id) are out too; the files of a note of the team, a system line or a deleted or discarded message are out like those messages. (g) owner the adviser, before the public flow opens: the receiver of a fiscal document can be a third party (a company) tied to the order, not the person who asked; the export lists the documents of the person's orders with the receiver's allowlisted fields (name, tax id, address, email, phone), so the adviser decides whether a company receiver of the person's order belongs in the export or is only mentioned; until then it is included, because the order is the person's.

RETURNING` that spends every live link of the request but only when the token it was given is live (exactly one caller wins; a scanner, a second click or a sibling link finds nothing; a dead token burns no live one; two calls that still collide in the database, P2034 / 40001 / 40P01, answer the same uniform 400 as any link that does not open, never a 500, see `isTransactionConflictError`), re-reads the request (completed, export kind, key, date), signs the link and returns `{ url, filename, expiresInSeconds }` (the signed link of `DSR_EXPORT_DOWNLOAD_URL_SECONDS`, 5 minutes; the bytes never pass through the api). (4) Earlier unused tokens are kept, not replaced: replacing one under a job still in flight would send a dead link; rejected one-link-at-a-time. (5) The route is gated by the same `enabled` flag as the intake: with the flow off nobody can use it. (e) owner 7.3: the throttle is per address and counts every call, valid or not; a unit spec pins the profile on the route (`tests/api/dsr-export-download.spec.ts`), but no spec drives the 21st call. (3) The page withdraws the link at expiry and keeps the password (found in the review: the first version withdrew both, and a person who saved the ZIP and read the page slowly lost the password); rejected hiding it behind a second press, because the api shows it once. (4) The schema accepts `http:` and `https:` links: a local bucket (MinIO) signs `http`; requiring `https` in production is not checked here (the env schema of the storage endpoint was not read in this PR): owner 7.7 checks that a production endpoint is `https` (the review flagged it). **Left by H2b-3b (rule 12):** (a) owner **7.7 / QA pass:** the e2e of the page (`apps/web-e2e`, needs the mailbox helper, a finished export and `DSR_PUBLIC_INTAKE_ENABLED`; skipped while the flag is off, as the rest of `dsr-public-flow`); the unit spec drives every state meanwhile. (c) a response lost after the api spent the token (network cut between claim and answer) shows `invalid` on retry; the person asks the store (H2b-3a (c), reviewer re-mint), not closed here. Every request gets its own password of `ComplianceConfig.DSR_EXPORT_PASSWORD_BYTES` (24) random bytes (`newDsrExportPassword`, `libs/core/platform/compliance/dsr-export-password.ts`); the runner seals it with the credentials key (`CredentialCipher.sealText`, AES-256-GCM, bound to the request id as additional data, so a value copied to another request opens nothing) into the new column `data_subject_requests.result_password_sealed` (migration `20270131100000_dsr_export_password` + rollback), in the same UPDATE that sets `result_key`; the purge of an expired export clears both. `POST /compliance/dsr/export/download` now answers `{ url, filename, expiresInSeconds, password }`: the password is opened INSIDE the same atomic claim that spends the links (an advisory lock, one UPDATE), so only the call that spent the link can read it, a second call or a sibling link gets the uniform `400 DSR_EXPORT_LINK_INVALID`, and a password that does not open (another key, an altered row, a value of another request) rolls the claim back (the token is not burned) with the same 400 and a log line that names the kind of error only. The answer carries `Cache-Control: no-store`. The password is never in the mail, a log, the audit log, a metric or an error (specs capture the logger and the audit entries). An export with no sealed password (made before this PR) is refused with the uniform 400 and expires with its date. The names of the entries of a ZIP are NOT encrypted by the format, so the files of the person are numbered `files/0003.png` (number and at most a short extension; the original name stays in `files.json`, inside the encrypted ZIP) instead of carrying the name they were uploaded with. The rotation of `CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` re-seals the column (`SealedTargetIds.DSR_EXPORT_PASSWORD`, `CredentialsResealService`, `sealed-columns.spec.ts`, `CREDENTIALS_KEY_ROTATION_RUNBOOK.md`). No new environment variable: the key is the one the credentials already rotate. Specs: `dsr-export-password.spec.ts`, `dsr-export-zip.spec.ts` (no plaintext of the text, the names of the person's files, the hashes or the bytes of a file in the object; it does not open without the password or with a wrong one; an altered byte is refused; two exports of the same data and password differ: new salt and nonce each time), `dsr-export-download.service.spec.ts`, and the integration specs `dsr-export.spec.ts`, `dsr-export-download.spec.ts`, `credentials-reseal.spec.ts`. **Decisions (rule 12):** (1) the password is handed to the person in the answer of the download, once, not in the mail and not through a reviewer: protects against whoever reads the bucket (a backup, a misconfigured policy, a provider employee), which is the threat the owner named, and needs no second channel or change of the mail; rejected the design written in H2b-3a (b), the reviewer shows the password in the queue and hands it over out of band, because it puts a person in the loop of every export, needs a queue screen and a channel the store may not have, and gives the reviewer a way to open the data of the person; the cost is that who controls the mailbox of the person gets the link and the password together (the same person who could already download the file), so the mailbox stays the proof of identity, as for the verification mail. (2) AES-256 ZIP with a library, not hand-made crypto over the ZIP with AES-GCM: the person opens it with a tool they already have; rejected a custom envelope (nobody could open it) and the "ZipCrypto" of old tools (broken). `@zip.js/zip.js`: BSD-3-Clause, no dependencies, no native code, no install script (checked in the lockfile), last published 2026-11-12. (3) a password of its own per request and sealed with the existing key, rejected a key derived from the platform key and the request id: a rotation would break every export in flight, and the sealed column re-seals with the machinery that already exists. **Left by H2b-3c (rule 12), each with its owner:** (a) **DONE in this PR (the page of H2b-3b merged first, #983):** the page shows the password once with a copy button and says it cannot be seen again (keys `dsrExport.password`, `passwordHint`, `copy`, `copied`) and `dsrExportDownloadResultSchema` in `libs/api-client/src/compliance-api.ts` makes `password` required, so an answer without it is refused and the page shows the failure, never the success (specs in `compliance-api.spec.ts` and `dsr-export-card.spec.tsx`). (b) owner 7.7: the reviewer's link (`DsrReviewService.exportLink`) hands the same encrypted object and the reviewer never sees the password, by design (the reviewer cannot open the data of the person); a person who lost the password after the link was spent (the tab closed before copying it, a scanner that posted the token) needs a new export (a reviewer action that re-runs it, H2b-3b (c)). (c) owner 7.7: the password is shown in the response of the page to anyone who holds the live link; if the owner later wants the password on a second channel (an SMS or the conversation of the customer), it is a change of the answer and of the page, not of the stored format. (d) owner 7.7: a mutation test of `streamDsrZip` (drop the password, use ZipCrypto) is covered by the specs above but not run as a mutation job. (e) the integration specs ran in CI only; the machine that made this PR has no database. (f) owner 7.7: the key of the object is deterministic (`StorageKeys.dsrExport(requestId)`): a run that outlives the lease of `DSR_EXPORT_LEASE_MS` (1 hour) can be taken over by another, and both write the same key with their own password, so the object of the one that finished last can carry a password that is not the one kept in the row (a ZIP that does not open; the person asks for a new export, and the next run starts clean). A random suffix per attempt (the key kept in `result_key`, the dead tries swept by prefix) touches the cleanup of dead tries, the orphan sweep and their specs, so it is its own change; the lease is 4 times the transaction timeout of `DSR_EXPORT_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT_MS` (15 minutes), which is what makes the race rare.

The form (`DsrRequestForm`, its own route: nothing shared grows, the orders budget is untouched) takes the kind (`DSR_PUBLIC_TYPES`: access, erasure, portability, in api-client, never a magic string), the address (checked on the page with the same rule as the api, trimmed; the api lower-cases it) and the language of the page, and sends exactly `dsrIntakeBodySchema` through `submitDsrRequest` (`authenticated: false`). **It branches on the status only**: every 202 gets the one sentence ("if this address belongs to a customer we sent a link", never saying whether it did), a 429 gets one text with **no wait time** (the intake counts per address and per store per day and a number would tell which limit was hit), a network failure keeps what was typed and the key and offers "try again". The panel of C1a now shows the address of the form (`origin + AppPaths.dsrRequest + #key=<key>`) next to the key, with the existing copy button, only when the key exists. Accessibility notes of the readers of C1b-1, applied to both pages: the result is a `role=status` mounted with its content and takes the focus; the button is `aria-disabled` and not `disabled` while it works (a disabled button throws the keyboard focus away) and a second press is ignored; after a failure the focus goes to the message and the button says "try again" (`retry`). Specs: `dsr-request-form.spec.tsx` (body exactly as the api reads it, the kinds offered, no key, bad address with focus and `aria-describedby`, the same markup for a customer and a stranger, network, 429, double press, a body the api refuses), the specs of route access, headers, config and titles, and the changed `dsr-verify-card.spec.tsx`. E2E: `dsr-public.spec.ts` (the page opens with no session, the headers, a bad address, no key) runs in CI with the flag off; `dsr-public-flow.spec.ts` is the **whole flow** (the store makes its key and reads the address, a visitor files an erasure, the worker mails the link, the page of C1b-1 confirms it, the request waits "in review" in the queue; the same address again gives the same answer and no second mail; a stranger gets the same text and no mail) and runs only with `DSR_PUBLIC_INTAKE_ENABLED=true`. **`DSR_PUBLIC_FLOW_READY` stays false in the repo.** The whole-flow spec was written and type-checked and linted, but **not executed**: the e2e stack binds the fixed ports 3000, 8080 and 8081, which are not free on the machine that wrote it; the run with the constant flipped (never committed) is the first thing the PR that turns the flow on does (debt (b)). **Decisions (rule 12):** (1) the key in the fragment and not in the path: rejected the path (`/compliance/dsr/<key>`), which every access log and a Referer would carry. (2) No CAPTCHA and no per-store data on the page (not even the name of the store): the key is all the page has, so a page cannot be used to find out which keys exist (the api answers a 202 for an unknown key too). (3) Three kinds, not six: rectification, restriction and objection need a conversation with the store, and the form has no text field for it; they stay for the store's channels. **Debts:** (a) the panel still says "the form does not take requests yet" while the flow is closed: goes with the flag (the PR that turns the flow on, C1a (c)). (b) the e2e of the whole flow does not run in CI (it needs the flag, which the env schema refuses until `DSR_PUBLIC_FLOW_READY`) and was never executed (see above): the PR that turns the flow on runs it first with the constant flipped, then removes the skip and adds the two variables to the e2e environment. (c) the form has no cooldown after a 429 and no visual pass: **Step 7.7**. (d) `X-RateLimit-Reset` of the 429 of the throttler comes from `timeToExpire` while the wait of the message (`retryAfterSeconds`) comes from `timeToBlockExpire`; no spec has a `blockDuration` different from the `ttl` to tell them apart: **Step 7.3**. (e) the panel shows the address built from `window.location.origin`: behind a proxy that rewrites the host it would show the internal one; a configured public URL of the web would be the fix: **Step 7.7**; the panel also reads `window.location.origin` while it renders, which is safe only because it draws after its query resolves on the client: a server prefetch of the form data would need the origin read in an effect: **Step 7.7**.
- [x] **Consent records and the record of the cookie banner, server side (PR `feat/consent-records`, Step 7.2-D):** no migration: `ConsentRecord` and `CookieConsent` came with the first schema and `consent_records` has its policy since the RLS phase 1 (`cookie_consents` has no store, so no policy). `GET` and `POST /compliance/consent` (`customers:view` reads, `customers:edit` writes) keep the history of a customer **append-only**: a change is a new row and the newest row of a purpose is the answer that rules (what `order-messages` already reads); the same answer again writes and audits nothing; the legal basis is the one of the purpose (`ConsentPurposeLegalBasis`), never a field of the body; the address and browser of the person who clicked are not kept on the row (the audit entry `consent.recorded` holds who and from where); the write runs under the lock of the customer (two at once leave one row) and refuses an erased customer (409); a customer of another store is a 404 on both routes. `POST /compliance/cookie-consent` is public with an optional session (`OptionalSession`, `ThrottleProfiles.PUBLIC`): it records the choice of an anonymous visitor or of a platform user keyed by the `visitorId` the browser made, the account comes from the token and never from the body, the address is kept only as an HMAC (`CompliancePlatformModule`, key derived from `JWT_SECRET` with its own label), the same choice again writes nothing, and a `policyVersion` other than `COOKIE_POLICY_VERSION` is refused. `ConsentRecord` leaves the isolation exemptions and has its case in `tests/security/tenant-isolation.spec.ts`. **Decisions (rule 12):** (1) the permissions of the customer (`customers:view`, `customers:edit`) and no new one, so that no migration has to hand it to the roles that exist; a store that wants consents apart from the profile asks for `customers:consent` later. (3) No immutability trigger yet (below). **Left, each with its owner (Step 7.2, next PRs):** (a) **7.2-D2, web (the banner and its panel are done by the item below; the consent panel on the profile of a customer is still open, see its debt 1):** the banner of the cookies (the choice in the cookie `platform_cc`, `COOKIE_CONSENT_COOKIE_NAME`, a re-prompt when `COOKIE_POLICY_VERSION` changes, the call to the route) and the consent panel on the profile of a customer, with their functions in the api-client and their entries in `scripts/frontend-coverage-map.ts` (`compliance.consent`, `compliance.cookieConsent`); held on purpose: a banner that covers the screen changes every e2e of the app, and whether the platform needs one at all depends on (b). (c) **Owner-only, with (b):** the public registry of cookies (name, category, purpose, duration, provider) of `TDD_05 §10.5`. (d) **Closed by 7.2-K2 (the item below `Documents of orders`).** A retention for `cookie_consents` (a visitor who changes the choice every day adds a row a day): a category of the daily `PlatformCleaner` that keeps the newest row of each visitor and drops the older ones past a window the owner approves; the route is throttled per address but not capped per visitor, and two identical answers at the very same moment (a double click) can both write: the dedupe is best effort, a duplicate row is harmless because the newest row rules. (e) **Closed by 7.2-K2.** A trigger that makes `consent_records` append-only for what a person said (`granted`, `purpose`, `grantedAt`): it must let the customer merge move `customer_id` and the erasure set `revokedAt` and clear `ip_address` and `user_agent`, and leave DELETE for the cascades; Step 7.3. (f) Reading a visitor's choice back (a logged-in person on a second device): no route yet, the browser keeps it in its cookie. (h) **Owner decision, rule 5 of the project `CLAUDE.md`:** `POST /compliance/cookie-consent` is a public route (a visitor has no account) and is not on the list of public routes of that rule; the PR keeps it public because `TDD_05 §10.5` says the banner serves anonymous visitors, and the owner adds it to the list (or asks for a session) when the owner reads this. (i) **From the readers of 7.2-D (Step 7.3):** `customerStop` in `order-messages.service.ts` orders the newest consent by `createdAt` only: add `{ id: 'desc' }` as `ConsentService` does (a tie after a customer merge moves rows is rare but undefined); the key of the address hash derives from `JWT_SECRET`, so a leaked secret lets the IPv4 addresses in `ip_hash` be recovered by brute force: **(closed by 7.2-K2: `CONSENT_HASH_KEY`)** give it its own variable in `libs/core/platform/config/env-schema.ts` and `.env.example`; and `req.ip` is only the client's when `trust proxy` is right in the deployment (Step 7.5 checks it). The banner does not cover the page for good and does not trap the focus; "Only essential", "Choose" and "Accept all" have the same weight; the panel is a `Dialog` (focus returns to its button, Escape closes) with native checkboxes, the essential one always on and disabled, the optional ones off until allowed. Texts are i18n (`cookieConsent` in es and en) with provisional neutral wording. (2) The send is public and tokenless: the alternative of sending the access token to link the choice to the account was rejected because an anonymous browser would make the client ask for a refresh on every page; the link is debt 4. (3) Non-modal banner, not a wall: the app works whatever is answered (the owner's brief). (4) The optional categories gate nothing yet (debt 3). **Left, each with its owner:** (1) **7.2-D3 (or 7.4):** the consent panel on the profile of a customer (`GET`/`POST /compliance/consent`) and its api-client functions; the entries `compliance.consent` in `scripts/frontend-coverage-map.ts` stays on 7.2 until then. (2) **Owner-only, with (b) and (c) of 7.2-D:** the wording of the banner and the panel (`cookieConsent.*` is provisional), the value of `COOKIE_POLICY_VERSION` (a marked placeholder) and the public registry of cookies. (3) **Owner-only, with (b):** what each category switches off. The language cookie and the last store (`StorageKeys.LAST_STORE_ID`) are not gated because whether they are `necessary` or `functional` is the owner's call; `isCategoryAllowed` (`lib/cookie-consent/cookie-choice.ts`) is the check the first optional feature (analytics, 7.x) must use, and a test of that feature must prove it writes nothing without a yes. (4) **7.2-G:** link the choice to the account of a signed-in person (send the token only when the session exists, without the refresh) and read the choice back on a second device (debt f of 7.2-D). (5) **7.4:** the visual pass of the banner (position over the composer on a phone, density), and moving the focus to the page after an answer; and **measure the banner on the first visit** (the `lighthouse` job without the `platform_cc` cookie): the job measures an answered visitor (`answeredCookieConsent`) so that the banner chunk (about 21 KB of script on the login page) is not counted against the ceilings, which hides the cost of the very first visit by design; what is proved today is that the banner does not move the content (`cookie-consent.spec.ts`: fixed position, same boxes and same page height with and without it), not what it weighs. The pass of 7.4 either adds a first-visit measurement with its own ceiling or splits the chunk further. (6) **Still 7.3 (the trigger and the key: closed by 7.2-K2):** the immutability trigger of `consent_records` (debt e of 7.2-D: it is a migration with its rollback and `db:rls:enforce on`, kept out of this web PR to keep it reviewable), the own env variable of the address hash key and `trust proxy` (7.5). (7) **7.3:** a choice the api refuses with a permanent 4xx (a version the api does not know after a deploy) is sent again on every page, with no cap or backoff; tell transient failures from permanent ones. (8) **From the reader 6f, by design:** the choice of a signed-in person is recorded with `userId` null (the POST goes without a session, debt 4 links it); and `ConsentService` and `customerStop` break a tie of two answers at the same instant differently (the service by `id`, the reader refusal-first): there are no real ties because the service writes under the lock of the customer. (9) **From the reader 6f, for 7.3 and 7.5 (the forged prefix: closed by 7.2-K2, `isSettled` now checks the whole shape of the cookie):** a cookie forged with the exact prefix of the current version hides the banner only in the browser of whoever forged it and is fail-safe (`isCategoryAllowed` is strict: an invalid cookie allows nothing), so it is not a bypass; the layout answer depends on the cookie, so `security-headers.spec.ts` pins that `/login` is `private` and `no-store` with and without it, and a CDN or proxy that overrode that is a matter of Step 7.5 (deployment). - [x] **Audit log viewer and export, server side (PR `feat/audit-log-viewer`, Step 7.2-E):** `GET /organizations/current/audit-log` (`org:view_audit_log`, held by the Admin preset only; cursor on `(timestamp, id)`, newest first; filters `action` (exact), `userId`, `resourceType`, `resourceId`, `from` (inclusive) and `before` (exclusive); a field it does not know is a 400, so a `storeId` in the query is refused and never read) `GET /organizations/current/audit-log/:id` (one entry; another store, no store and unknown are the same 404) and `GET /organizations/current/audit-log/export` (same permission, 202 with the export of the center, CSV by the worker with the same `auditLogWhere` rule as the screen, the formula guard of `csv.ts`, `audit_log.exported` written when the file is ready). Both read the rows of the store of `X-Store-Id` only, with the store as the first term of the `where` and as the RLS policy of `audit_logs` (`store_id = ANY(app_store_ids())`). An entry with no store (a login, a guard refusal, the system) belongs to no tenant and is not listed. Reading the log writes `audit_log.viewed` (the filters, no text of a person): once for the first page of a list, and once for each read of one entry by id (`resourceId` is the entry). `AuditLog` leaves `scripts/isolation-exemptions.ts` and has its case `auditLog` in `tests/security/tenant-isolation.spec.ts`. The view adds nothing to the row: ids, action, metadata, ip, user agent, instant (the code writes ids and counts only into the metadata). Nothing writes, updates or deletes in the table (immutable since #575). **Decisions (rule 12):** (1) store scope, not organization scope: the permission is organization-level (TDD_05 §9.3) but the rows are read through their store, as the policy already says; an organization-wide view of all its stores belongs to a later step if the owner asks; (2) one permission for reading and exporting (`ExportTypePermissions` entry `audit_log`), as the TDD lists the CSV with the viewer; (3) `action` is an exact match, never a prefix, so the index of `action` is used; (4) the viewer audits the first page of a reading (`audit_log.viewed`), not every page, so that scrolling does not fill the log with the reads of the log; (5) an export with no `before` gets `before = now` in the row, so the file is the log as it was when it was asked for; (6) the by-id read audits every call (opening an entry is a deliberate act, not a scroll); a viewer that opens many entries writes as many rows, accepted; (7) the CSV is refused with `EXPORT_TOO_LARGE` (400, narrow the dates) when the range counts more than `ExportLimits.AUDIT_LOG_MAX_ROWS` (200 000) at the time of the request, never cut short; (8) the worker never copies the search text `q` of an export into the audit entry of the export (`hasText: true` instead), because the entry is immutable and an erasure of a customer cannot reach a name typed there; (9) `org:view_audit_log` implies reading the `metadata` of every entry of the store, including the ones of finance and costs (ids, counts and amounts, no free text): it is the right of an auditor and the Admin preset holds it; a per-resource redaction was rejected as a second permission model inside one log. **Left by PR 7.2-E (each with its owner):** (a) the system actor entry of the nightly retention deletions: **done by PR 7.2-G** (line above); (b) the viewer reads the hot rows only; the cold parts (`audit-logs-part-N.jsonl.gz`, older than 2 years) are read by a restore, not by the screen; **PR 7.2-G did not take it** (it only writes the entries of the nightly runs): **closed by PR 7.2-K** (the viewer reads the parts and deduplicates by `id`); (c) a request for an audit export leaves no entry of its own, only the worker writes `audit_log.exported` when the file is ready (like every other export): an attempt that fails or is refused by the ceiling leaves no trace; owner Step 7.3 together with the other exports; (d) no index fits a filter by `resourceId` or `resourceType` alone: the keyset reads in `(store_id, timestamp)` order and scans the 2 years of the hot window of the store; decide with real volumes whether `(store_id, resource_type, resource_id, timestamp DESC)` is worth its writes (a migration with rollback), owner Step 7.3; (e) the exports center of the web (`apps/web/lib/exports/export-state.ts`: `ExportPermissions`, `FILTERABLE_TYPES`) does not know the `audit_log` kind: a member whose role holds only `org:view_audit_log` cannot open the center and the kind falls under "Other"; closed by PR 7.2-I (`ExportPermissions` and `FILTERABLE_TYPES` know the `audit_log` kind); (f) the web: the table with filters and the "Export CSV" button on Settings, with the actor shown by name from the team list, the labels of the actions and their i18n, and the exports center already lists the kind; closed by **PR 7.2-I**, except the labels of the actions (see its debts) (`organizations.auditLog` and `organizations.auditLogExport` in `scripts/frontend-coverage-map.ts` point to Step 7.2); (h) a late entry (written after a reading began, with an earlier timestamp than the cursor) can fall outside the pages of a reading in progress: inherent to a cursor on the instant, the next reading shows it; (i) `audit_log.viewed` is written after the answer (like every audit of the api, Step 7.4 owns writing them in the transaction), so its order against the read is not guaranteed; (j) the worker holds no ceiling of rows of its own for the audit CSV (the request counts them; the rows that arrive between the request and the job, hours at most, are few against 200 000), a time limit of the job is owner Step 7.3; (g) the `metadata` of every action was not read key by key for personal data: the convention of the code is ids and counts (checked for `member.invited`, which carries role ids and no address), and the viewer shows what the row holds; a sweep of every `audit.log` call for an address or a free text, replacing it by an id, is owner Step 7.3.

The grace is fixed, not a store setting (the retention settings of TDD_05 §10 do not list invitations); no migration (the worker role already deletes from the table). **Known limits (rule 12; owner the DSR flow of this step):** an accepted or revoked invitation keeps the invitee's email for ever (a revoked one belongs to someone who never joined, whom no customer erasure reaches): give those rows a long bound or scrub the email in the DSR erasure; and the link of an invitation deleted after the grace answers "not valid" (`TENANT_INVITATION_INVALID`) instead of "expired"; the text for the first could say that a new invitation can be asked for.
- [x] **Retention of the documents of orders, the sweep and the guard (PR `feat/order-documents-retention`, Step 7.2-J; from the retention fix, OPS-SET-268):** a new category `orderDocuments` of the nightly retention of a store (`StoreRetentionEnforcer`, so the same store filter, batches, `more`, failure handling and the ONE audit entry `retention.run` with counts that PR 7.2-G made) deletes a document of an order (`Media` with `purpose = order`, an order, no finance transaction, no fiscal document) when BOTH the document and its order were made before `orderDocumentCutoff(now)` (`libs/core/platform/compliance/order-document-retention.ts`: `OrderDocumentRetention.LEGAL_YEARS`, in calendar years so a leap year can only keep a document a day longer). **Ten years since the PR `fix/retention-tax-ten-years` (D15, owner 2026-11-25; first written as a 7 year proposal): the Codigo Tributario art. 147 keeps the books, the vouchers and the electronic tax documents ten years from their issue.** **Never deleted, whatever its age:** a document of an order that has a fiscal document of any status, and one whose sale entry (`sourceType` order) is in a period with a legal book taken (`finance_book_snapshots`; the database refuses to change a taken book, so it is held for ever); the selection is in SQL, so held documents never fill a batch and block the sweep. The customer being erased changes nothing (the rule reads the order, not the person). The bucket is deleted first and the row after: a bucket that fails keeps the row (skipped for the rest of the run, tried again the next night); a row whose object is already gone is finished by the next run (deleting a missing object is not an error); the sweep is idempotent and resumes by itself (what was deleted no longer matches). No id, key or filename goes in a log or in the audit entry: counts `orderDocuments` (deleted) and `orderDocumentsHeld` (past the period and kept by the books; it does not make an entry by itself). The `media` category (files of messages older than `mediaDays`) now names the three owner columns (`FILE_WITHOUT_OWNER`, shared with `filesOfConversationsWhere`) in its select and in its delete. Tests: `tests/api/retention-run.spec.ts` (then 6 years 11 months kept and 7 years and a day deleted with its object, now 9 years 11 months kept and 10 years and a day deleted; the later of the two dates rules; erased customer; fiscal document; sealed book vs open period; bucket failure and retry; idempotent with the object already gone; another store untouched; owner guard of `media`; the count in the audit entry), `order-document-retention.spec.ts`, `conversation-files.spec.ts`; breaking the fiscal hold or the owner guard fails them. **Known limits (rule 12; owner Step 7.2 / 7.7):** (a) a held document (fiscal document or sealed book) is kept for ever: if the books must be kept for a period and then go, the accountant gives that second period and the sweep gets it (10 years is the usual one for fiscal documents, and the period of the sweep now); (b) only the sale entry of the order (`sourceType` order) is looked at, not the entries of its returns or shipments, which have their own source ids: if the accountant wants those to hold the order too, extend the SQL; (c) a period that is closed but whose legal book was never taken does not hold its orders: the accountant says if a closed period must hold too (the SQL is one predicate, `eligibleOrderDocumentIds`, to be changed with the held count beside it); (d) the hold is read again for each document right before its objects go, but a fiscal document or a book taken in the milliseconds of that one call to the bucket still loses the object (the row stays pointing at nothing): accepted, because the bucket must go before the row so a crash leaves a row that the next run finishes; (e) the audit entry of the run says how many were deleted, not which: the order keeps its own history. **Scope of the period (reader 6b, owner Step 7.2):** (i) it counts from `orders.created_at` (and from the upload of the document), never from the last movement of the order (a return, a remittance, a reopening); (ii) nothing holds a document for a return, a remittance or an open dispute: only a fiscal document and a sealed legal book do; (iii) the deletion leaves only counts in the audit, no trace of each document. **More limits (reader 9b, owner Step 7.2, nothing is deleted before about 2036 since the ten years):** (f) `Order.paymentProofMediaId` and `Order.proofOfDeliveryMediaId` are plain columns with no foreign key, so after the sweep they point at a row that is gone: check that the view of an order does not fail when its medium no longer exists (or null them in the sweep); (h) the two predicates of the sweep on `financeTransactionId` and `fiscalDocumentId` of the file are a second guard: the database already refuses an order file with either owner (`chk_media_fiscal_evidence` and `chk_media_finance_parent`), so no valid row can reach them and a test can only pin the check (`retention-run.spec`); (g) with the bucket down each file retries and warns, up to `MAX_BATCHES` times `BATCH_SIZE` times in a run: bounded, but the run could stop at the first bucket failure.

Proved in `tests/security/consent-records-append-only.spec.ts` (the customer erasure and merge suites run through it too). (2) **Its own hash key:** `CONSENT_HASH_KEY` (env schema, `.env.example`, `ci.yml`) replaces the key derived from `JWT_SECRET` for `cookie_consents.ip_hash`. A deployed environment must set it (at least 32 characters, not `JWT_SECRET`, not the placeholder: the schema refuses to start); a laptop or a test run may leave it out and the key is derived from `JWT_SECRET` as before. **Rotation and the hashes already written:** they live together and are NOT rehashed, because the address is not kept (that is what the hash is for), so it cannot be. A hash made by the own key is `<key name>:<hex>`, where the name is `k` and 8 hex characters of an HMAC of a fixed label under the key (domain separation, NOT a hardening: like any one-way function of the key it lets whoever holds a row try candidate keys against its 32 bits, so the real protection is the entropy of the key, at least 32 characters generated with `openssl rand -hex 32`, which the deployment runbook of Step 7.5 must say; there is no deployment yet, so no hash with another name exists outside a laptop) (so a rotated key can never go on under the old name, and no second variable has to be remembered); a bare 64-character hex is the old derived key (`consentHashKeyIdOf`, `libs/core/platform/compliance/consent-hash.ts`). Rotating means only a new value; rows before keep the name of the old key. A value that is `JWT_SECRET`, `CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` or the placeholder is refused in a deployed environment, and an empty value counts as not set. The hash proves where a choice came from and identifies nobody, and nothing compares across rows, so a rotation costs nothing but the ability to check an old row with the new key. (3) **Retention of `cookie_consents`, OFF BY DEFAULT:** `COOKIE_CONSENT_RETENTION_ENABLED=false` (env schema, `.env.example`): with it off the sweep deletes nothing and the category reports 0 (a case in `tests/api/retention-run.spec.ts` pins it, and shows the same row going once it is on); this PR authorizes no deletion. (4) **The forged prefix of the cookie (reader 6f of #881):** `isSettled` (`apps/web/lib/cookie-consent/cookie-settled.ts`) no longer takes `platform_cc=<version>.1.` followed by anything; it checks the whole shape (`<version>.1.<one bit per category>.<visitor id>`) with one fixed-length regex, so a cut or forged cookie shows the banner again and the page and `isCategoryAllowed` agree. **Decisions (rule 12):** the window is a PROPOSAL (two years: a year of choice plus a year for a complaint about it), for the owner and whoever answers for the policy to confirm; `customer_id` moves only to a customer of the same store, `revoked_at` is never before the grant or more than an hour ahead of the clock, and the cascade exemption of DELETE also needs the customer or the store to be gone (found by the review; a trigger of another table that deletes a row is refused); the DELETE is refused by the trigger and not by `REVOKE` because the application roles hold the blanket grant and a cascade must keep working; the own key is optional outside a deployed environment so that no suite or laptop needs a new secret (the alternative, required everywhere, was rejected for that cost). **Left (rule 12):** (a) the key of the public data requests (`dsrHashKeyOf(JWT_SECRET)`, H1a debt f) is still derived from `JWT_SECRET`: its own variable and the rotation of secrets stay with Step 7.3; (b) the runbook of a rotation of `CONSENT_HASH_KEY` and the secret itself in the deployment checklist: Step 7.5; (c) **Owner-only, closes with the owner's decision:** the window `COOKIE_CONSENT_RETENTION_DAYS` (730 is a proposal) and turning on `COOKIE_CONSENT_RETENTION_ENABLED` in each environment; the sweep destroys evidence of consent for good, so until the owner decides it stays off (owner list `PENDIENTES-DUENIO-M7.md`); (a) **Accepted limit, not "inviolable":** the trigger stops DML by every role, but whoever owns the table (the migration credential) or a superuser can `DISABLE TRIGGER` or set `session_replication_role = replica`; (b) **Owner action BEFORE the release:** `CONSENT_HASH_KEY` (exactly that name, at least 32 characters, not `JWT_SECRET`, not `CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, not the placeholder) is REQUIRED in staging and production: without it api and worker do not start; it has no default in the schema. (c) `cookie_consents.user_agent` (clear text, up to 512) and `ip_hash` stay for ever while `COOKIE_CONSENT_RETENTION_ENABLED` is off: owner, who sets the window and turns it on, before the first public deployment (Step 7.5 checklist; the window of 730 days is a proposal). A conversation of an erased customer: a reply, note, resend, reaction, edit or deletion is refused with `CUSTOMER_ERASED` (409) from the person's routes and the plugin API alike; the messaging window of an erased customer reads as closed with no template, so the closing message, the away reply and the messages of an order send nothing; a reply queued before the erasure fails with `CUSTOMER_ERASED` in the worker, and typing indicators and read receipts to the erased handle are dropped. **Still open (rule 12, owner Step 7.2):** (b) the personal data copied into orders (owner/accountant decision: nothing in the TDD says what the books need of `recipientPhones`, `shippingAddress` and the customer notes of an order); the TEXT and TEMPLATE messages that an order writes (`metadata.orderMessage`) are NOT in that debt: their text (it carries the name and the address) and the variables of their template are cleared, and only the pointer `{ orderMessage }` stays, so the thread keeps drawing the line of the order;
