Done in 7.2-C after the readers: the clearing runs again 15 minutes after the erasure (a second delayed job) and the daily sweep takes the customers marked in the last two days again (`ComplianceConfig.ERASED_DATA_RECHECK_*`), so what such a write left is found; the media fetcher refuses a file of an erased customer. NOT done on purpose: a lock on the customer in the paths that write (`requireCustomerNotErased` reading `FOR SHARE`), because they hold the lock of the conversation first and a merge holds the customers first and then moves the conversations, so the two orders would deadlock; a message that lands after the last recheck stays until the next change of that customer, a window of minutes that the readers accepted or can reopen; (s) the sweep tries the customers never tried first and then the one tried longest ago (`erased_data_attempted_at`), so a customer that always fails does not starve the rest, but it is still tried every night until a person looks at the log; (q) the sweep takes 50 customers a store a night and each run does 40 batches of 500 rows a category, so a customer with more than 20 000 messages takes more than one night (the job retries first). Two minor limits of the sweep found by the review of 7.2-C (rule 12, owner Step 7.3, Hardening; **closed by PR `fix/erased-customer-sweep-limits` (7.3-S8): see "Done in 7.3-S8" below, which also closes (q)**): (v) `ErasedCustomerData.clear` checks the time budget of the daily run only between customers (`ErasedCustomerSweep.run(until)`), so one customer with a very large thread can run past the five minutes of margin before the leader lock (30 minutes, not renewed) expires; check `until` between the batches of each category, or give the sweep its own lock and TTL; (w) `ErasedCustomerSweep` reads the pending customers of every store inside `inEachStoreStrict`, which aborts the stores after the first one whose read fails (a store that cannot be entered stops the night's sweep for the rest): catch the failure per store, log it by store id, and go on with the next one, as the platform cleanup does for its per-store categories. **Done in 7.3-S8 (closes (v), (w) and (q)):** `ErasedCustomerData.clear(storeId, customerId, until)` asks the time budget of the sweep before every batch of every category and before every batch of files (`inBatches` takes a `shouldStop`), so a customer with a very large thread ends between two batches and never outlasts the leader lock; with a budget the batch cap of a job (40 batches of 500 rows) does not apply, so a thread of more than 20 000 messages is finished in one night as far as the time allows, and what is left is found by the next run (the customer is tried, not marked as cleared). The report says `unfinished` (rows left, nothing failed), which the sweep counts apart from `failed` and lists in `more` of its entry; the job of the erasure (no budget) keeps its cap and the queue retries. The sweep goes store by store with its own loop: a store that cannot be entered is logged by id at error level and the others go on; at the end the run writes its entry with `failed: ['stores']` and throws, so the failure is not quiet. It differs from `inEachStoreStrict` on purpose: that loop is for sweeps that decide by what they do not find, and this one acts only on customers that carry `erased_at`, so a store it cannot read deletes nothing and waits. A store reached after the budget is over is not started (`more: ['stores']`). One customer takes at most 5 minutes of the night (`CUSTOMER_BUDGET_MS`), so a huge thread does not starve the customers and stores after it; the files of a batch are checked against the budget between files, not only between batches. **Limits left on purpose (rule 12, owner Step 7.3):** the stores are visited in id order, so if every night the first stores hold enough heavy threads to use the whole budget, the later stores wait (rotate the order by the oldest `erased_data_attempted_at` of each store when that is seen in the `more: ['stores']` of the entries); a customer with a bucket failure and a budget stop at once counts as `failed`, not `unfinished` (the bucket failure is what an operator must see); the worst case of one bucket call is not bounded by the budget, only by the 5 minutes of margin of the lock. Tests (real database, enforced row security, role `platform_worker`): budget over before the first batch touches nothing and a later run finishes it, a thread of 1 200 messages in one run, a store that fails does not stop the other, no store and no customer after the budget, `unfinished` is not `failed`. **#31 of the breakdown (the secrets of a revoked plugin installation) is Done in PR `fix/revoked-plugin-secrets-sweep` (7.3-S8b), see debt (l) of Step 5.6.** Note (b) of the reader of 7.3-S8: `inBatches` with a `shouldStop` answers `more: true` when the budget ended even if nothing was left, which costs one extra harmless retry of that customer; accepted. **Done in PR `feat/customer-erasure-web` (Step 7.2-F; closes (d) and the web half of (c)):** the profile (drawer) offers "Erase customer data" to whoever holds `customers:erase` (`ClientPermissions.CUSTOMERS_ERASE`) in a dialog that lists what is erased and what is kept (orders, invoices and the books, with the data they already copied) and asks the agent to type a word (`customers.erasure.confirmWord`) before the button works; it is not closed while the call runs and shows the api refusal. `GET /customers/:id` now answers `erasedAt` and a conversation answers `customer.isErased`; an erased customer shows the chip "Data erased" in the profile (read only: edit, merge, identities, tags, addresses and caution controls are not drawn), in the row and the header of the conversation, and the composer is replaced by a text that says why nothing can be sent (`CUSTOMER_ERASED` has its text in en and es for a reply that was already in flight). `eraseCustomer` and `useCustomerErasure` (api-client and web) read the customers, conversations and orders again; the e2e `customer-erasure.spec.ts` covers the dialog, the read only profile and the thread. the message actions of the thread (edit, delete, react, resend) are not drawn for an erased customer (the viewer of the rules sees no permission and no capability); `isErased` and `erasedAt` are required in the api-client schemas, so a payload without them fails loudly instead of drawing the controls of a live customer; the plugin API does not tell `erasedAt` of a customer (the view of the customer is field by field), while a key that holds `customers:read` is told `customer.isErased` of a conversation with the rest of the customer (it can read the placeholder anyway, and its own writes answer `CUSTOMER_ERASED`). **Left (rule 12, owner Step 7.4, visual polish):** one pass of design over the dialog and the chips; the list of notifications, the search results, the orders list and the order detail show the placeholder name of an erased customer without the chip; the create-order drawer opened from the thread of an erased customer is not disabled (the api refuses the order with 409 `CUSTOMER_ERASED` on submit): disable the button there; the erase action is only in the profile drawer (a role that holds `customers:erase` without `customers:view` has no entry point: the drawer needs view; give the action a place of its own if the owner wants that role).

### Step 7.3 — Hardening
Added by the owner on 2026-11-21: the numbers of Milestone 7 follow the order the steps run, and the hardening and the visual polish come BEFORE the deployment (7.1 Security, 7.2 Compliance, **7.3 Hardening**, 7.4 Visual polish, 7.5 Deployment, 7.6 Monitoring; 7.7 Load validation and 7.10 Internal admin console are deferred to Phase 2; 7.8 and 7.9 are done). Before this step the plan said "Step 7.3" for the hardening debts (robustness, limits, concurrency, tests that do not yet prove a behavior) and for the deployment alike; the debts kept their label 7.3 and the deployment tasks (Railway, the proxy, the production bucket, the release flow) became **Step 7.5**. The criteria of the split are in the description of the PR that renumbered (`refactor/plan-renumber-m7`).

**Goal:** every debt labeled Hardening (7.3) is closed, or ACCEPTED by the owner IN WRITING (a line in the plan that says who accepted it and when), before the first deployment.

**Done when:** (1) the index below has no open line that is neither closed nor accepted in writing; (2) every debt of the plan that says "Step 7.3", "owner 7.3" or "to 7.3" (`grep -n -E "(Step|owner|to|and|or) 7\.3" docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`) is closed or accepted; (3) the unit and integration suites, the security suites and the isolation suites are green with enforcement ON (`RLS_CONTEXT`); (4) **Step 7.5 (Deployment) does not start before this one is done.**

**Where the debts live (rule 12: each keeps its place).** A debt stays in the block of the step that left it, with its owner; this step only labels it. Many sit inside the block of Step 7.5 (the old "Step 7.3 — Deployment" block held the first ones); they are hardening all the same. The families, to find them by name in the plan:
- Security headers left by Step 7.1 (owner 7.3): a CSP `report-uri`/`report-to` endpoint, tied to the Sentry setup, and the securityheaders.com grade A check against the deployed host (see the Helmet/CSP task of Step 7.1); the Bull Board page has no header case of its own (`apiSecurityHeaders` runs first on every answer, the board only replaces its CSP).
- [x] Exports with the requester read when the file is written (Step 7.3-C, the debt (a) above; closed by Step 7.3-S1, PR `fix/export-requester-read`): the worker now asks for an installation whose plugin is APPROVED (`currentPermissionsOfRequester`; a plugin withdrawn or suspended holds nothing); the permissions are read again after the file is written and before the row turns READY (`fileStillCovered`: the kind's permissions and every permission of the view the file was made with), and a requester who lost any gets the row failed with `PERMISSION_DENIED` and the file deleted; and the scheduled report runner `stillAllowed` calls `currentPermissionsOfRequester` and `accessOfRequester` (ACTIVE membership, `revokedAt` null). Left on purpose (rule 12): the gap between the second read and the `READY` update is one query wide and the download is gated live, so it is not closed; a report whose person loses the right between `stillAllowed` and the generator makes the job fail unrecoverable and stays `enabled` until its next run turns it off with the audit entry (Step 7.3 nit, no data leaves); the orphan file when the delete fails on a FAILED row and the two tests owed are **closed by PR 7.3-S16 (`fix/export-file-orphans`)**: `discard` of the generator counts the failure (`platform_export_file_discard_failed_total{stage}`, `ExportDiscardStages`), logs it with the id of the export only, and leaves the key of the lost file on the row (never on a READY row); the cleanup now sweeps the FAILED and EXPIRED rows by the prefix of the export (a row that holds a key at any age; one with no key for `ExportLimits.FILE_SWEEP_DAYS` days after a grace of `FILE_SWEEP_GRACE_MINUTES`), the object first and the key of the row after, so a run that dies in the middle finds the row again, and the expiry of a READY row also deletes the whole prefix, not only its key; a view shows no filename on a row that is not READY; tests: a bucket that refuses (retried on the next run, counted), the age window, the rows of every store, and enforced-RLS cases in `tests/security/rls-phase1.spec.ts` for the sweep reads and writes and for the relational filter `plugin: { status }`; the `MEDIA_ZIP` branch with `viewer.held` in `export-generator.service.spec.ts`. Left on purpose by S16 (owner Step 7.3): a FAILED row with no key that settled more than `FILE_SWEEP_DAYS` ago, whose file the bucket still holds and whose key could not be written to the row either (the database down at the same time as the bucket), is left to the lifecycle of the production bucket (Step 7.5); the sweep lists the prefix of each unmarked row of the window on every run (at most `CLEANUP_BATCH` per store per run, one list call each, in sequence, so a very large number of stores and failed rows can outlast the 600 s lock of `expired-exports.scheduler.ts`; the deletes are idempotent, so an overlapped run only doubles the load), which a marker column (a migration) and a lock sized to the run would avoid; in the branch `settled.count === 0` of the generator, a job duplicated by a stalled worker can write the SAME key on the same day, and `discard` would delete the file of the row that did become READY (it existed before S16; reader 6b; owner Step 7.3; criterion: the key of the file carries the id of the row or of the attempt, or `discard` checks that the key does not belong to a READY row); the rows that keep a key because the bucket keeps refusing are taken first by id, up to `CLEANUP_BATCH` per store, in a list of their own so they never take the places of the rows of the window; more than that many refusals in one store repeat the same hundred until the bucket answers, and the counter `platform_export_file_discard_failed_total` is what raises the alarm (Step 7.6 alert rule); the `accessOfRequester` check inside `fileStillCovered` is redundant on purpose (defense in depth); the plugin status is read through the context of the store, so a plugin that the policy of `plugins` hides from it (another organization's) answers no row and is refused (fails closed, no function `SECURITY DEFINER` was added: installing a plugin of another organization is not allowed, so a legitimate case does not exist; Owner 7.3 if it ever does). A cancelled export (`PERMISSION_DENIED`) is notified to an ACTIVE member whatever their role, to nobody else, and its row is hidden from the list by the permission it lost. Owner Step 7.3 (security). Owner-only: what personal data an export may carry and how long a ready file is kept (debt (b) of the Step 7.1 task "Exports leave the platform with personal data").

(2) *Pages (c):* no report is one unit any more: the margin reads a page of sale entries and their orders per unit, the VAT reads the ids of the range, each page of orders and the sums of the books in their own units, the aging reads the lines by keyset in pages and ages a party as soon as its lines end (memory: one party's lines, not all), the books read the sales and the receipts by keyset pages; every page is a `FinanceReportGate.unit` (the 60 s `READ_UNIT_TIMEOUT_MS` is now per page). (3) *Freeze (d):* the freeze of a closed month's book (a write, with its audit row) is its own unit after the build, so the freeze no longer shares a unit (and a timeout) with the reads of the build; a failed freeze still fails the request and the next one builds again. A whole report at the cap is about 200 pages, so 70 to 100 s of database time spread over units of under 1 s each (the unit timeout is 60 s). **Limits of the figure:** the fixture is not in the repository (it was made with `generate_series`: 200 000 entries with consecutive numbers and one line each, one organization, 2 000 suppliers, in a private copy of the schema) and it ran as the owner role, with no row security. **Criterion to reopen:** a page above 5 s on the real data, or the cost of the full report with row security enforced (not measured here: the fixture ran as the owner). - [x] **Document thread (PR `fix/document-parse-worker-thread`, rule 12; sensitive: denial of service by a customer's file; closes debt (k) of the existing-documents item of Step 7.1 and (e) of 7.1-I):** the parse of a PDF, a docx or an xlsx (`pdf-lib`, `fflate`: synchronous) no longer runs on the main thread of the worker. `DocumentCleaner` (`apps/worker/src/media/document-cleaner.ts`, the token; `MediaPipeline` and `ExistingDocumentSanitizer` receive it) is provided by `ThreadDocumentCleaner` (`thread-document-cleaner.ts`), which starts **one thread per document** (`worker_threads`), inside the same decode slot as the picture decoder (one at a time per process), with `resourceLimits` (`DocumentSanitizing.THREAD_MAX_OLD_GENERATION_MB` 384, young 32, stack 4), an **empty environment, no argv and no node options** (no database address, no storage key reaches it), and `workerData` that is a copy of the bytes: it holds no storage client, no database and nothing shared. A **hard deadline** (`THREAD_TIMEOUT_MS`, 30 s) stops it with `terminate()`, which ends even a loop that never yields; the timer is cleared and `terminate()` is called on every exit path and **waited for** (up to `THREAD_STOP_TIMEOUT_MS`, 5 s) before the slot is freed; a thread that is inside a synchronous native call cannot be interrupted until it returns, so it may outlive its document for a moment, and while it is alive (`live`) the cleaner takes no new document and throws (the queue retries): two threads are never alive together. The answer is **one message** whose shape and size are checked by the parent (a body over the limit, a body that is not bytes or sits on a `SharedArrayBuffer` (memory the thread could still change while the parent uploads it), a body that does not begin and end as the type says (a PDF: `%PDF-` first and `%%EOF` in the last KiB; a zip: `PK\x03\x04` first and the end record `PK\x05\x06` in the last 64 KiB; **only the two ends are read, no parse**, so a thread that was taken over can still return any body with both ends right and up to `maxBytes`: the parent trusts the thread for the content of a document it cleaned, and the isolation protects the process, not the text of that file; re-parsing the result in the parent would put the parse back on the main thread), anything unknown is refused; the body is copied before it is checked and the check is on the copy; the text of an error of the parser is never sent, because it can carry a piece of the file). What each end means: an answer is as before (`sanitized` / `untouched`); the **deadline** is `untouched` with `why: 'timed_out'` and the **memory limit** (`ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY`) is `not_cleanable`. The document is never refused. In the **scan of an upload** both keep it as it came (the scan goes on, `why` in the log with ids only). In the **sweep** a memory limit is marked `not_cleanable`, but a **deadline is not a verdict** (a busy worker can cut a good file): the row is left unmarked with its attempt already written (#897), so the next run takes it again, and after `MAX_ATTEMPTS` it is given up and the alert of the rows given up with no mark counts it; a poison document is therefore parsed at most three times and never again; a thread that cannot start, fails, or ends with no answer, and a bundle without the thread file, **throw** (the machine's, retried by the queue; the sweep counts them against `MAX_ATTEMPTS`). `sanitizeDocument` of `libs/core/storage` was renamed `sanitizeDocumentInline`: it runs on the thread that calls it, only the entry of the thread (`document-thread.reply.ts`) and the specs call it, and `document-cleaner-isolation.spec.ts` fails if a service does. `isEnvironmentError` moved to its own file (`environment-error.ts`, re-exported by `image-sanitizer`) so that the thread does not load `sharp`. **The thread file is a second entry of the rspack bundle** (`tools/rspack/nest-bundle.cjs`, third argument; `apps/worker/rspack.config.cjs`): `dist/apps/worker/document-thread.js` next to `main.js`, resolved from `process.argv[1]`; the image copies the whole `dist/apps/worker/` so the Dockerfile did not change. Specs: `thread-document-cleaner.spec.ts` (a document that spins ends at the deadline and the event loop keeps ticking, one that eats memory, an oversized or malformed answer, a thread that crashes or exits, a missing thread file, nothing of the process visible to the thread, no thread left behind, one at a time), `document-thread.reply.spec.ts` (the real cleaner through the answer of the thread), `document-cleaner-isolation.spec.ts`. Mutants that fall: no deadline (the spinning spec never ends), no `terminate` (the leftover-thread check), `env` shared with the thread, no size check of the answer, a service that calls the inline cleaner. **The bundle is checked in CI** (`scripts/smoke-document-thread.ts`, in the step "The api and the worker start and answer" of `ci.yml`: it cleans a real PDF on the thread of the built `dist/apps/worker`); the integration specs that compile the real worker module override `DocumentCleaner` with the inline one (`InlineDocumentCleaner`, `testing/`), because under ts-jest there is no bundle. Review of the PR (`/code-review` high, 6 findings, all answered): the integration specs override, the deadline in the sweep and the log filter above, the literals moved to `DocumentSanitizing`; the other two are debts below. **Left on purpose (rule 12):** (g) **What happens to a document that passes the deadline (owner: Step 7.3; closes when the sweep has cleaned or given up every such file and Step 7.6 counts `timed_out`).** *Upload scan:* the file is kept as it came, served with its properties, and the scan goes on (never refused, never retried: a hostile file must not hold the queue). *Sweep:* the row is `clean` with no `sanitized` mark, so the sweep takes it (purposes message, origin, product, order); each run that hits the deadline leaves it unmarked and uses one attempt; after `MAX_ATTEMPTS` (3) it is **given up with no mark and stays uncleaned for good** (the alert of rows given up with no mark counts it; clearing its `scan_result` takes it again once the cause is known). So a file that always hangs stays with its properties: accepted, because it is either hostile (its own metadata, the customer's) or the 30 s deadline is wrong for the real load, which is what the count of `timed_out` shows. A file that only hit a busy worker is cleaned by a later run. (h) `isEnvironmentError` (`environment-error.ts`) matches the words `resource` and `thread` in the message of an error, so a parser error that says "Missing resource dictionary" is read as a failure of the machine and retried instead of kept as `not_cleanable` (it was so before the thread; the retries are bounded by the attempts of the sweep and the attempts of the queue): tighten it to the codes of Node (`ENOMEM`, `EMFILE`, `ERR_WORKER_*`) with its own spec, **Step 7.3** (owner). (i) The memory limit bounds the heap of the thread, not its `ArrayBuffer`s: the zip is bounded by `MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES` and `MAX_ZIP_ENTRIES`, but the decoded size of the streams of a PDF has no bound of its own (a compressible 10 MB PDF can inflate far past it); a cap on what `pdf-lib` decodes, or a memory guard of the process, is **Step 7.3** (owner). (a) the picture sweep and the scan of pictures still decode on the libuv pool through `sharp` (native, not synchronous on the loop); counting the attempt of the picture sweep BEFORE the decode, for a decoder that kills the process natively, is a task of this step that stays open (owner 7.3, with the same spec as the documents). (b) A thread starts per document (about 120 to 250 ms measured on a laptop for the start of the thread and the cleaning of a one-page PDF), which is nothing against the 10-minute cadence of the sweep; a pool of threads is not worth its state until a metric shows the start-up dominating (Step 7.6). (c) The limits are constants in `DocumentSanitizing`, not settings: change them in the code if the owner's measure of a real worker says so. (d) **Memory ceiling of one document (reader's note, PR 921).** `resourceLimits` bounds the V8 heap of the thread (384 MB old generation + 32 MB young), **not** its `Buffer`s and `ArrayBuffer`s, which live outside the heap. The real ceiling of one cleaning is therefore: the input (copied into the thread, at most `UploadLimits.MAX_FILE_SIZE_BYTES`, 10 MB, and the copy the caller keeps: 20 MB) + the inflated package of a docx or xlsx (`DocumentSanitizing.MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES`, 64 MB, enforced by the `filter` of `unzipSync` before anything is inflated, and the written-again copy, at most that again) + the output (at most `maxBytes`, 10 MB, checked by the thread and again by the parent) + the heap limit above: about 0.7 GB for one document (heap 416 MB + input copies 20 MB + inflated 64 MB + rezipped 64 MB + output 10 MB + overhead), and never two (the decode slot and `live`; the spec `survives a thread that holds gigabytes of buffers` shows that the heap limit does not stop buffers, and that the parent lives on). **The memory of the container of the worker must hold that on top of the rest of the worker; Step 7.5 sizes it with this number.** A PDF has no bound of its own on what `pdf-lib` decodes (a compressible 10 MB file can inflate past the heap limit, which then stops the thread with `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY`, but a stream inflated into an `ArrayBuffer` is not counted): a cap on the decoded size of PDF streams is **Step 7.3** (owner), closed when a spec feeds a PDF whose streams inflate past a set bound and sees `not_cleanable`. **Stopping a thread:** `terminate()` cannot interrupt a thread inside a synchronous native call (inflate) until it returns; the cleaner waits for it up to `THREAD_STOP_TIMEOUT_MS` (5 s) before it frees the slot, then fails (the queue retries) and, while that thread is alive (`live`), takes no new document, so two threads of memory are never alive together (specs: `stops the thread on every way out`, `does not start another thread while one that could not be stopped is alive`). (j) **A thread that cannot be stopped (`live` stays above 0) leaves the cleaner of that worker unusable until it restarts**: every upload scan throws and is retried by the queue, and the sweep **stops its run without using an attempt** (`isBusy()`, checked before `begin`, with the log `the sweep of documents stopped...`; spec `uses no attempt while a thread that could not be stopped is alive`). The metric `document_thread_still_running` (a gauge of `live`) and an alert on it above 0 for 10 minutes are **Step 7.6** (owner), closed when the alert exists and a game day with a thread inside a native call shows it firing; until then the log is the only trace. **Accepted race:** between `isBusy()` and `clean()` the sweep awaits the database and the bucket, so a thread of the upload scan that gets stuck inside that window still costs one attempt of the sweep's row (bounded by `MAX_ATTEMPTS`, 3); closing it needs the check inside `clean()` and a distinct answer, which is not worth the code for a window of milliseconds. A restart of the worker clears it, and the worker has a health check that does not look at the thread: tie it to the metric there. (e) A metric and an alert for documents that end `timed_out` or by the memory limit are with the one for `not_cleanable` (Step 7.6, the alert of item (e) of the existing-documents item above). (f) `findActivePdfNames` (the inspection of the PDF of a financial document, TAX-436) still runs on the main thread; it is a bounded scan of bytes, and the isolated process of the inspection is the task of "Files and media" below.
- [x] **Office user paths and embedded photos (PR `feat/office-user-paths-media`, task `office-user-paths-and-embedded-media`, rule 12; sensitive: it rewrites customers' files; closes the part of (b) and (d) of "Metadata of files that are not static pictures" that names the paths of the user and the photos inside a document):** `document-sanitizer.ts` (version 2 of the cleaning, `DocumentSanitizing.CLEANING_VERSION`) now also cleans two things inside a docx and an xlsx, and one inside a PDF; it runs on the document thread, so the contract of PR "Document thread" holds (the ends of the file are checked by `ThreadDocumentCleaner`, `isBusy()` is asked before a document is taken, the thread does not touch storage or the database). **(1) Paths of the author's machine, one rule per part, the most careful that leaves the document openable: the value is replaced, never removed.** In every list of relationships of the package (`_rels/.rels` and every `*/_rels/*.rels`: the attached template of Word, a linked workbook of Excel, a link to a file) a relationship with `TargetMode="External"` whose target is a local place (`file:` in any case, a drive `C:\` or `C:/`, a network share `\\server`, a character reference of XML for one of those, read before the judgement) gets `DocumentSanitizing.NEUTRAL_LOCAL_TARGET` (`file:///local-file`) as its target; the relationship stays, with its id and type, because the part that uses it refers to it by id and a document whose template is missing opens as it does on any other machine. A web address, a mail address, `//host/...` and a path relative to the package are the customer's content and stay. In `xl/workbook.xml` the `url` of each `x15ac:absPath` element (any prefix) is replaced by `NEUTRAL_LOCAL_PATH` (`C:\local-file\`); the element stays, because Excel may require its attribute. The elements are read one at a time with a bounded look back for the `<` (a part made of the word `absPath` repeated is read in linear time; spec). **(2) Photos inside a docx and an xlsx** (`word/media/` and `xl/media/`, the type taken from the bytes and never from the extension): a photo that carries EXIF, XMP, IPTC or the Photoshop block (`carriesMetadata`, header only) goes through `sanitizeImage`, the cleaner of pictures that the uploads use, inside its decode slot and one at a time (a still picture is decoded and encoded again; a gif or an animation is cut in its container); a photo that carries nothing is left bit for bit, so a clean document is `already_clean` and the sweep does not rewrite it. The type and the name of the part do not change, so `[Content_Types].xml` is the same. The photos get the time budget `EMBEDDED_IMAGES_BUDGET_MS` (12 s of the 30 s of the thread): past it the photos that are left stay as they came, and the properties and paths are cleaned all the same. **(3) Photos inside a PDF** (a decision that differs from the first plan, written here: the lossless cut and not a new encoding): an image whose only filter is `DCTDecode` is a JPEG file inside the PDF, and the image dictionary (width, height, colour space, decode, the `Adobe` transform) describes those bytes; encoding it again would mean rewriting the dictionary for every colour space and would change the pixels. `cutJpegMetadata` (`jpeg-metadata-cutter.ts`) walks the segments up to the scan and removes only `APP1` (EXIF and XMP), `APP3`, `APP10` and `APP12` (the text of Kodak, picture info and Ducky), `APP13` (IPTC, Photoshop) and `COM`; every other byte is copied, the pixels are the same (spec compares the decoded raster), the object keeps its number and `/Length` is set. A file that cannot be walked is not cut. **Never refused, never lossy in structure:** a part that cannot be cleaned (a photo that does not decode, a list of relationships past `MAX_RELATIONSHIPS_BYTES` or that never closes, a photo after the budget) is kept as it came and counted in `keptParts`, which the scan of the media pipeline and the sweep log with the ids of the media and the store (never the text); the document is cleaned of everything else. The same bounds as before hold (parts, uncompressed size, CRC-32 of every part). **Read-back before anything is replaced:** the package is unzipped again, has exactly the parts it should, **every part that the cleaning did not mean to change is the same bytes**, the parts it rewrote are fixed points of the same rule (no path left), and every cleaned photo carries no metadata; a PDF is loaded again with the same pages, comments, bookmarks and reachable objects and no block of properties (a JPEG with metadata counts as one). **The sweep of stored documents takes again the documents that the first version finished (point 6 of the assignment):** the marks of version 1 are `{sanitized: true}` and `{sanitized: true, sanitizeSweep: already_clean}`, with no version. The mark of version 2 is `{sanitized: true, cleaningVersion: 2}` (with `sanitizeSweep: already_clean` when the file had nothing to remove), written by the sweep and by the scan of the pipeline (`DocumentSanitizing.CLEANING_VERSION_KEY`). `ExistingDocumentSanitizer` takes, besides the unfinished rows, a row whose whole `scan_result` is one of the two marks of version 1 (matched whole, because a missing key cannot be matched by a path filter) or whose `cleaningVersion` is below the current one (so version 3 needs no new list). The same compare-and-swap protects the first write (`beginGuard`: the row must still be exactly the value that was read). A document marked `not_cleanable` or `failed` is not taken again (what kept it is still true of it), and a row with a higher version (a rollback of the code) is left. A document that the new version finds clean only gets its mark (no write). **One extra parse of every stored document, once**, bounded by the existing budget (10 per store, 40 per run, every 10 minutes); the sweep still does not run without versioning (`VersionedBucketGuard`). Specs: `jpeg-metadata-cutter.spec.ts`, `document-sanitizer.paths-and-media.spec.ts` (docx and xlsx built with the paths and the position of a made-up person: template, six kinds of local target, links that stay, relationships of the package and of every part, idempotence, hostile lists, the workbook under any prefix, the word as a name or as text, linear time, the photos in `word/media` and `xl/media` as jpeg, png and webp, a clean photo untouched, a damaged one kept and counted, type by bytes, the time budget, a PDF with a geotagged JPEG: dictionary, length, same pixels, clean once), `existing-document-sanitizer.spec.ts` and `.integration.spec.ts` (the rows of version 1 are taken once, the others are not, against the real database), `thread-document-cleaner.spec.ts` (the count crosses the thread and is not believed unless it is a whole number). **Debts, each with an owner (rule 12):** (a) The paths that live inside the text of other parts stay: `xl/connections.xml` (`Data Source=`), `xl/queryTables`, field codes of Word (`INCLUDETEXT`, `LINK`) and defined names that point to a local workbook; they are free text with syntax of their own, and replacing them blind would break a query or a field: **Step 7.3, a rule per part with the owner's choice** (closes when the owner lists which parts he wants). (b) A PDF image under another filter (`FlateDecode` is raw pixels and holds nothing; a chain `[FlateDecode DCTDecode]`, `JPXDecode` with XMP boxes, `CCITT`) is not read: **Step 7.3, closes with a measure of how many stored PDFs carry such an image** (the log of the sweep by `keptParts` does not count them: they are not parts it meant to reach). (c) The photos of a docx or an xlsx are decoded and encoded again like a picture upload: the quality 92 first, the orientation of EXIF applied to the pixels (a photo whose orientation tag Word showed rotated is now upright in the pixels), and a lossy change of pixels for a photo that carried metadata; accepted for the same reason as in the uploads. A lossless cut for JPEG, as in the PDF, would keep the pixels and is possible (`cutJpegMetadata` is there) but does not remove the metadata of a png or webp: **owner's choice, Step 7.3**. (d) The raster of a photo of up to 50 million pixels is native memory of the thread and is not counted by `resourceLimits`; it is bounded by the decode slot (one at a time per thread, one thread at a time per process) and by `MAX_INPUT_PIXELS`, as for a picture upload, and no spec measures the peak of a package with such a photo: **Step 7.3 with debt (e) of 7.1-I** (closes with a measure of the peak memory of the worker on a 10 MB docx with one 50 MP photo). (e) `keptParts` is only a log line: it has no metric and no alert; it joins the alert of the rows `failed` or `not_cleanable` (**Step 7.3**, same item). (f) A document the new version cleaned with `keptParts` above zero is marked as done: its kept parts are not retried (a photo that does not decode will not decode next time; a photo after the budget could be, with a slower deadline): **closes when (e) shows the case is real**. (g) The review of the PR (`/code-review high`, correctness and security) found and fixed: the search for the end of an `absPath` element was repeated for each one (quadratic on a part of elements that never close; now once per stretch, spec with 60 000 of them), a readback that threw for one photo and so threw away the whole cleaning (the photos are the bytes the cleaner of pictures made and checked, compared by value), a rooted target `/x` taken for a path of a machine (a link rooted at the site; removed from the rule), a drive or scheme written as a character reference that kept the path (read before the judgement) and the segments `APP3`, `APP10`, `APP12` left in a PDF JPEG. Rejected as a false positive: that a document thread breaks the bound of one decode per process (the parent holds `withDecodeSlot` around the thread, `thread-document-cleaner.ts`). **Left on purpose:** (h) a row cleaned with `keptParts` above zero is marked with the current version and not retried, and a package whose only unfinished work was kept parts is `already_clean` and the count is not carried: the budget of photos is load-dependent, a photo that does not decode is permanent, and a retry on the first would loop on the second; **closes BEFORE real customers (as the video and audio item, 7.1-J): the position of a photo that stayed over the budget stays in the stored file for good, so (e) the alert on `keptParts` and a bounded retry by attempt count must exist first** (owner: Step 7.3, with (e)); (i) the budget of 12 s is checked between photos, so one very large photo that starts at the end of it can pass the 30 s of the thread and the document is then left as it came for a later run: closes with the measure of (d); (j) a row of version 1 that is taken again and fails, or ends `not_cleanable`, loses its old `{sanitized: true}` mark (the begin of the sweep writes the attempt over it, as for every row); the file in the bucket is untouched and was cleaned by version 1: **Step 7.3 sweep metrics item**; (k) the `JFXX` thumbnail in `APP0` of a JPEG and `APP11` (content credentials) stay in a PDF picture; (l) A list of relationships of a part other than the package's that passes the cap is left as it came and counted; the one of the package itself still keeps the whole document as it came, as before: **no owner needed unless (e) shows it happens**.

Only a photo that cannot be walked, or whose cut still carries metadata, stays and is counted in `keptParts`. **A document an agent uploaded (`uploadedBy` set, on its way OUT) with `keptParts` above zero is refused**: the row ends `unscannable` with `MediaRejectionReasons.DOCUMENT_NOT_CLEANABLE`, the partly cleaned file is not written, the file is deleted (a financial document is never in this path), and it is never sent, served or attached (the gate that already exists for a refused picture; `refuseUnscannable` is `rejectImage` made general). What a customer sent is kept as it was cleaned and logged, as before. The cut is a LIST OF WHAT STAYS, not of what goes: a jpeg keeps its structural markers, JFIF, the colour profile (`APP2` that says `ICC_PROFILE`) and Adobe's transform, and loses every other application segment and comment (the telemetry with a position that a camera of action writes in `APP6`, a C2PA manifest in `APP11`); a png keeps `PNG_KEPT_CHUNKS` (critical, colour, transparency, background, resolution, animation) and loses every other chunk, private ones included; a photo that holds such a segment is taken for cleaning even when the header read (EXIF, XMP, IPTC) sees nothing. The cut is not used for a photo held turned by its orientation tag (the cut would drop the tag and not turn it: it is kept and counted) or for a jpeg that holds data after its end (a trailer, a multi-picture or gain-map image with an EXIF block of its own, which the header read back does not see); and a package whose text and properties are already clean still reports the photos it kept (before, `already_clean` dropped the count and the gate could be passed). `DocumentSanitizing.CLEANING_VERSION` is 3, so the sweep takes again every stored document cleaned at version 2 (not only those that kept a photo): each is read once through the document thread and rewritten only if something changes, at `MAX_PER_RUN` per run. **Decisions:** the container cut instead of re-encoding in a second pass (no raster, no quality loss, same pixels) and instead of removing the photo (the document would lose content); refusing the upload instead of a new `not_cleanable` state for the row (the existing `unscannable` gate is already the one that "is sendable" reads, so nothing new to coordinate with MED-144). **Debts:** (a) a stored document of an agent that the sweep finds with `keptParts` above zero is logged and not refused (the row is `clean` and may have been sent; refusing it deletes a file customers may have): **Step 7.3, with the alert on `keptParts` and the retry by attempt count of (e) and (h) above**; (b) a document an agent uploads that is `not_cleanable` as a whole (a damaged package, `timed_out`) is still kept as it came and sent, with its photos untouched: **Step 7.3, owner's choice** (an encrypted PDF the agent must be able to send is the same path); (c) a photo that the cut leaves (orientation, data after the end) goes to `keptParts` and refuses the agent's upload instead of being re-encoded in the container's place: a second pass with the re-encoder for those photos is **Step 7.3**; (e) `uploadedBy !== null` is the sign of "on its way out" (the same test as the rest of the pipeline, not introduced here): a plugin upload or any path that sets `uploadedBy` for a file that is not outgoing is refused too, and one that leaves with `uploadedBy` null is not: the owner of plugin-media decides a field that says the direction, **Step 7.3**; (f) the list of what stays is still wide in three places, **Step 7.3**: `APP0` passes whole (a JFXX segment holds a JPEG thumbnail that could carry EXIF: require the `JFIF\0` prefix), the walk stops at the first scan (an `APPn` between the scans of a progressive jpeg is not seen), and the png list drops `mDCV`, `cLLI`, `sPLT` and `hIST` (HDR mastering and palette hints that some viewers use); (d) the header read-back of the cut has no spec that kills it today (no cutter leaves metadata that `carriesMetadata` sees); it stays as a guard for a future cutter.

During a re-sweep for a newer `CLEANING_VERSION` the row KEEPS its `sanitized: true` (`begin` spreads the marks the row holds and adds only the number of the try), so a file that an older version cleaned stays sendable while it lasts (it is not the "not sendable while it lasts" that this note said); a file with no mark stays not sendable at every step (the cleaning, the write of the bytes, and every way the run can end without a verdict); the size and the mark are written by ONE `updateMany`, guarded by the number of the try, so no step has one and not the other and a late run writes no mark over the verdict of another; two runs that overlap end with one rewrite (the slow one finds the object changed). **Decision (not changed):** when the new version cannot clean a file that an older one had cleaned, the row goes to `kept` and stops being sendable: the new version exists because the old one is not trusted. **One hole found and closed (defensive; no writer produces it today):** the list of the sweep (`TAKEN`) took a row with no `scan_result` or with a number of tries or an older version, but not a `scan_result` that held none of those keys (the note `unavailableSince` of a scanner that was down, which the move to `clean` leaves on the column); such a video was neither swept nor ever sendable. `TAKEN` now takes a row with no version key and not at its last try (`path: [cleaningVersion], equals: DbNull`, which the database answers for a key that is not there, a null column AND the JSON null; the begin of the try therefore guards a row read as `null` with `AnyNull`, or a JSON-null row would be taken in every run and never begun), and `tests/api/av-sweep-selection.spec.ts` runs the filter on a real PostgreSQL over ten shapes of the column (SQL NULL, JSON null, `{}`, the note of the scanner, tries, exhausted, `av_unavailable`, old, current cleaned, current kept). A run that overlaps another may still read a row at its last try before `closeExhausted` ran: excluded by the same filter. **Left, owner Step 7.3 (dependency of hardening):** `ExistingPictureSanitizer` and `ExistingDocumentSanitizer` keep the same shape of list (`NOT_FINISHED`: null column or number of tries) and do not take a clean file whose `scan_result` holds only that note; no writer produces it today (the note is newer than their cleaning and the scan replaces the column), and for a picture there is no allow-list at the exit, so a spec on the same case is owed there. (3) **CLOSED by the same PR:** `tests/api/outbound.spec.ts` has the worker send a video with no `scan_result`, with only the note of the scanner and with only the number of a try (it fails with `FILE_UNAVAILABLE` and never opens the file), a video that loses its mark after the message was picked up (the bytes and the link are refused), and one with the mark (it goes). The cases of `tests/api/outbound.spec.ts` were written against the pattern of their neighbours and run by CI; they were not run locally (the test database and Redis are not started in this session); `av-sweep-selection.spec.ts` was run against a PostgreSQL 17 of its own. **Known limit:** no spec pins that the service passes `AnyNull` in the begin of the try (a mutant that puts `DbNull` back lives); the filter semantics are pinned, and the effect is a JSON-null row that nothing writes (no column of the schema holds the JSON null) taken in every run; Step 7.3 if it is ever seen.
- [x] **Sealed mail queue for the mails of a data request (PR `fix/mail-queue-sealed-payload`, rule 12; closes debt (a) of the retry of lost mail (#962) for the DSR half, the condition before `DSR_PUBLIC_INTAKE_ENABLED` is turned on).** The four producers of a DSR mail (`DsrIntakeWorker` verification mail, and the closing notice of `DsrReviewService`, `DsrNoticeSender` and `DsrExpireSweeper`) now queue `sealMailJob(cipher, mail)` (`libs/core/email/src/sealed-mail-job.ts`): the whole mail (address, link, token, data) is one text sealed with `CredentialCipher` (`CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, no new secret), bound by AES-GCM associated data to `mail-job:<template>:<requestId>`; the job keeps only the template, the ids of `dsrNotice` and the correlation id. `EmailProcessor` opens it (`openMailJob`, current key, then the previous one while a rotation is on, so a rotation of the credentials key does not lose a waiting mail) and checks it again with `sendEmailJobSchema`. **Decisions:** (1) a sealed job that does not open (another key, altered, moved to another template or request) fails closed: `JobRejectedError` with fixed text ("the sealed mail job is unreadable"), no retry, nothing of the content in the error, the log or the dead-letter copy (the job name is already redacted), and a closing notice is marked `mail_failed` on its request so the reviewer reaches the person. (2) A job queued IN THE CLEAR by the previous release is still served and removed as it is sent (`removeOnComplete`): refusing it would lose the closing notice of a request, and its exposure already existed; the clear path in `EmailProcessor.mailOf` is removed one release after the api and the worker run this code (note for whoever cuts that release). The `auth-email` queue is unchanged. **Left (rule 12):** (a) owner Step 7.3, the magic link token (queue `auth-email`) and the other mail producers (order messages, scheduled reports, digests, whose data is the store's own and not a one-time secret) still queue in the clear; the retry of the magic link reads `data.url` from the job (`stillUseful`), so sealing it needs the processor to open first. (b) an integration case that reads the job from the real Redis and checks it holds no address is not added: the unit specs prove the payload handed to the queue; the first run of the flow with the flag on (H2b-3 end-to-end case) must read Redis. (c) **deploy order: the worker before the api.** A worker still on the previous release rejects a sealed job as not fitting its schema (`removeOnFail`, no `noticeFailed`). The sweeps run in the worker, so an old instance still alive in a rolling deploy can take a sealed job of a new one: that notice is not lost, because `DsrNoticeSender.pendingOf` asks again every night once the lease (`DSR_NOTICE_LEASE_MS`, 1 h) ends while `noticeSentAt` is empty and fewer than `DSR_NOTICE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (3) were counted, and `giveUpStale` marks it `mail_lost` after `DSR_NOTICE_STALE_HOURS` (24 h) when the tries run out. Only the notices of `DsrReviewService` (api: rejection, cancellation; the address is cleared when queued and the sweep does not ask again, H2b-2 (i)) are dropped unmarked if the api is deployed before the worker.  (d) the seal of the verification mail is bound to its template only (it has no request id yet when it is queued), so a sealed verification job copied into another job of the same template would open and send the same mail again; copying a sealed job does not reveal the token, it only lets someone with write access to Redis make the mail go out once more. Binding it to a per-job id is Step 7.3. (e) **What the seal is and is not:** it protects the content against whoever READS Redis; it is NOT authenticity against whoever WRITES to it: that person can queue a `send-email` job in the clear and the mail goes out (as before this PR). The clear path of `EmailProcessor.mailOf` stays for the jobs of the previous release; condition to close the injection too: one release after the old jobs drained (the queue empty of clear jobs of the DSR templates), `mailOf` refuses a `dsr-verification` or `dsr-result` job that is not sealed (`JobRejectedError`); the integration helper `tests/helpers/mail-seal.ts` records every DSR job a queue stand-in receives in the clear and fails the test after it (an `afterEach`, because the producers catch the error of their queue), so a producer that stops sealing is caught by the suites that queue a notice; the guard lists the two templates and its spec fails if a `dsr-*` template is added without it. Owner: whoever removes the clear path, Step 7.3. (f) the lost mail of a sealed job moved to another key by an emergency rotation without `CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS` is refused, by design; the runbook (`docs/CREDENTIALS_KEY_ROTATION_RUNBOOK.md`) now lists the mail job among what the previous key still opens.

The El Salvador provider (`sv-tax-id.ts`) accepts a NIT of 14 digits, a DUI of 9 with its check digit (modulus 10, the public rule) or an NRC of 2 to 8 digits; hyphens and spaces are ignored and the value is stored as typed, not normalized. The same provider now also holds the check digit of a national id in `validateReceiver` (a customer's fiscal data, when saved). Nothing already stored breaks: building a document from saved data does not hold the digit, a supplier tax id that is not changed is never checked, and a customer's tax id that is not changed is not judged again when another field is edited. NIT and NRC are checked for shape only. #### Gates before serving real customers (owner, 2026-11-23)

"Real customers" are the people who write to the owner's own business through the channels (the v1.2 MVP serves one owner and their stores); it is NOT the SaaS (Phase 2). Every gate below is met BEFORE the business starts serving people with an agent:

- [ ] 7.1-J-2 and 7.1-J-3 merged (the cleaning of the metadata of video and audio on what comes in and goes out, and the sweep of what is stored): until then the GPS of a video still leaves.
- [x] The `keptParts` debt of #941 closed for what leaves (a photo out of budget is cut in its container; an agent upload that keeps a part with its metadata is refused): PR `fix/media-uncleanable-parts`; what is left is in its debts (a) and (b).
- [ ] The red of the ffmpeg version workflow provoked once on purpose (`workflow_dispatch` from a branch with an old pin) and the issue or the email seen to arrive.
- [ ] The public data request flow switched on with its conditions: public download with a token (server side done by H2b-3a; its web page by H2b-3b), ZIP encrypted by the app (H2b-3c), the alternative notice (attachments and fiscal data in the export: done by C3) , and the case that reads the mail job from the REAL Redis and proves it holds no address, link or token (debt (b) of the sealed mail queue, PR `fix/mail-queue-sealed-payload`) (`dsrPublicFlowReady()` stays false until then).
- [ ] Versioning of the bucket on. **Mandatory, not a nicety (PR `fix/dsr-b9-debts`):** `StorageService.put` is not conditional (no `If-None-Match`, it overwrites the key), so what protects a file from an overwrite or a delete is the versioning of the bucket; that is why `VersionedBucketGuard` stops the sweeps while versioning is not `on`, and why the deploy does not go out with it off (`docs/BUCKET_PROTECTION_RUNBOOK.md`).
- [ ] New keys loaded in staging and production, generated at the first deploy and never reused from the test environment: `CONSENT_HASH_KEY`, `UNSUBSCRIBE_TOKEN_KEY`, `CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. `UNSUBSCRIBE_TOKEN_KEY_PREVIOUS` stays EMPTY at the first deploy (it is only for a later rotation).
- [ ] `pnpm check:plugin-manifests` run, and every `NOT VALID` constraint validated.

#### Owner decisions 2026-11-23

- "Real customers" means the people who write to the owner's business through the channels, as above; the gates are met before the business serves them.
- There is NO real data: everything so far has been a test environment. Consequence: `CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is NOT rotated (there is nothing to re-seal); the production keys are generated NEW at the first deploy and the test ones are never reused. The rotation procedure waits until there is real data.
- The public one-click unsubscribe of the notification emails (B6b-3b2b part 2): YES. It is an exception to rule 5, like the public routes of the data requests. PENDING, the owner's own edit (an assistant does not change `CLAUDE.md` on a colleague's request): rule 5 of `CLAUDE.md` lists the one-click unsubscribe, `POST /api/v1/notifications/unsubscribe`, and the public routes of the data requests that already exist and are not in the rule today (`POST /api/v1/compliance/dsr` and `POST /api/v1/compliance/dsr/verify`), each with "owner, 2026-11-23".
- S10 (ledger E) and S15 (VAT of purchases): postponed until the accountant answers.

The steps of Milestone 7 are numbered in the order they run (renumbered by the owner, 2026-11-21): 7.1, 7.2, 7.3 (Hardening), 7.4 (this step), 7.5 (Deployment), 7.6 (Monitoring); 7.8 and 7.9 are done; 7.7 (Load validation) and 7.10 (Internal admin console) are deferred to Phase 2.

- [ ] **From the cookie banner (PR 7.2-D2, rule 12):** measure the banner on the first visit: the `lighthouse` job runs with the answered `platform_cc` cookie, so the banner chunk (about 21 KB of script on the login page) is never counted, which hides the cost of the first visit by design. This pass adds a first-visit measurement (no cookie) with its own ceiling or splits the chunk further, and also does the visual pass of the banner (over the composer on a phone, density) and moves the focus after an answer. That the banner does not move the content is already proved by `cookie-consent.spec.ts`. **The JS budget of the `lighthouse` job has no margin:** `orders` was at 299.86 KB of 300 before the cookie gate and the gate costs about 0.8 KB on every page (the first run of the PR read 300.67), so the next PR that adds a line of script to a page can break the job by surprise; the login page went from 247.5 to 268.7 of 260 only because the banner chunk was loaded (fixed by measuring the answered visitor). The pass of 7.4 reviews the weight of the bundle and leaves a margin under every ceiling. **Numbers of the `lighthouse` job (KB of script; ceiling; main after #886 / PR 7.2-D2 at 5f63ca64c):** login 247.56 / 260 / 248.13; inbox 319.08 / 340 / 319.50; products 292.95 / 300 / 293.37; orders 299.93 / 300 / 300.28 (the only one over); inventory settings 306.12 / 350 / 306.57. Orders has 0.07 KB of room on main, so any script added to the shared chunk of the root layout breaks the job: the cookie gate cost +0.28 KB as a static import, about +0.35 KB behind `next/dynamic`, and moving its constants out of the `domain` barrel did not recover it (the same three shared chunks change in every try: 4.27→4.69, 7.61→7.73, 9.64→9.45 KB). **Options (decision of 2026-11-22, coordinator f3):** (A) raise the ceiling of `orders` (one line in `budgets.ts`, the owner's call, not done: rule 12); (B) a separate PR cuts at least 1.5 KB from the shared chunk of the root layout, and PR 7.2-D2 is merged after it (**chosen**); (C) move the banner out of the root layout to the public layouts, which leaves a signed-in person without the re-prompt of a new policy until their next login (changes the product, not done). If B turns out impossible, A or C goes to the owner with these numbers. **Cause found in the PR (rule 12):** `@platform/core/domain` is a barrel with no `sideEffects: false`, so every constant added to it travels whole in the script of every route (the cookie constants cost about 0.3 KB on each route until they moved to the file alias `@platform/core/cookie-consent`, like `store-preferences` and `env-rules`); the pass audits the barrel (mark it side-effect free, or move the constants the web reads to file aliases) and looks at the recent additions (7.1-7.3) that also travel.

- [ ] **From Step 5.3 (PR B): list views on the read replica.** The lists of `TDD_08 §2.5` that PR B left on the primary (conversations, customers, orders, products, inventory, exports, scheduled reports, `my-performance`) and every search (message, customer, order, product) because the web refetches them right after a write and a search applies erasure and visibility rules: add a read-your-writes rule (a short-lived per-store marker of the last write that sends the read to the primary, or a replication lag check) and move them one at a time, each one named in `scripts/replica-readers.ts` and proved in `tests/api/read-replica-routing.spec.ts`. Until then `DATABASE_REPLICA_URL` stays unset in every environment, and it is only set with a replica fed by streaming replication. The worker never calls `replica()`: its heavy reads (exports, reports) can use one when the replica exists, and `HttpPlatformModule` could stop opening the idle pool for it.

Each one, with what it needs: (a) `conversation.counts`: the key must carry the viewer (the figures depend on `visibleTo(viewer)`), and the archive, spam, snooze and bulk sweeps (api and worker) publish no event, so they must publish one (bridged to the api when the worker does it) before the `CONVERSATION_*` cases are added to `CacheInvalidationListener`; (b) `customer.byIdentity` and `channel.connection` are read and written by the worker's inbound pipeline: add their events to `BridgedEvents`, or give the key a short TTL only; (c) `product.search` stays on the primary and uncached until the search is cached for good (see the replica task above); (d) `TenantContextService.invalidateUser/invalidateStore` are still called by the services that change a membership or a role: emit `MEMBER_*` and `ROLE_UPDATED` (they exist in `Events` and nothing emits them) and move the calls behind the listener; (e) the readers of `StoreSettings` that go straight to the database (`orders`, `returns`, `widget`, the worker) are not cached, and the inbox, inventory, returns and carrier settings emit no event; (f) accepted limits of PR A stay: a Redis failure while a change is announced leaves the old entry for its TTL, and a read in flight when a change commits is shared with the next read of the same key (key the loads by generation if k6 says it matters). (g) The worker is not run through PgBouncer by a suite of its own: its role is checked through the pooler (`core-database` integration), the jobs that take advisory locks (`analytics-rollup`, `carrier-event-applier`) are: **checked by PR 7.3-B1, nothing to add:** `tests/jest.pooler.config.cts` lists `api/analytics-rollups.spec.ts` (it builds `AnalyticsRollupService`, `AnalyticsRollupScheduler`) and `api/carrier-event-processing.spec.ts` (it builds `CarrierEventReplay` and `CarrierEventResolver`; the applier is `CarrierEventApplier`) since commit `4f2a3fe4e` (#503), and `ci.yml` job `pooler-tests` runs `pnpm test:pooler`.
- [x] **Lighthouse over its ceiling on orders and inventory settings (PR fix/web-lighthouse-orders-inventory, rule 12):** closed. Before: `orders` 300.29 of 300 KB and `inventory settings` 356.04 of 350 KB. After: `orders` 285.39, `inventory settings` 290.11, login 239.49, inbox 303.73, products 278.25 (all under their ceilings, none raised). Causes found with a throwaway per-chunk breakdown in CI (used and reverted before the merge): the barrel `settings/pages.ts` re-exported 14 `'use client'` pages, so every settings route shipped all of them (now one module `<name>-page.ts` per page, never a shared barrel); and the untree-shaken barrel of `@platform/core/domain` put zod and every schema in the first load of each page (now `libs/core/domain/package.json` with `type: module` and `sideEffects: false`; the domain has no import-time registration, audited). Debts: the barrels `app/s/[storeId]/orders|remittances|returns/pages.ts` have the same shape and are not touched here (owner: this task, Step 7.4; split them the same way when a route of them nears its ceiling); a lint guard against page barrels would stop the regression (Step 7.4); the lazy `CarriersPanel` was not re-measured without the barrel (Step 7.4). `sideEffects: false` on `libs/core/domain` is a standing rule, not enforced by a check: a future import-time registration there (zod error map, registry) would be dropped from the web bundle but run on the api, so none may be added; a lint or test guard that fails on a top-level registration in the domain is owed (Step 7.4).

- [x] Draw the discard of a failed reply — **done (PR `feat/discard-failed-reply`, web; the api is #232)**: `failureStateOf` (`lib/inbox/failure-state.ts`, tested) reads `failureDefinitive`: `true` is a definitive failure (red, "Send again" and "Discard" for who may send, or send templates for a template), anything else, `undefined` included, is "could not confirm" (amber triangle and note, only "Send again", which first asks and warns that the customer may receive it twice); "Discard" asks in one step (`DiscardMessageDialog`, lazy) and calls `POST /messages/:id/discard`; success or a 409 (`MESSAGE_DISCARD_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` and any other: the screen was out of date) read the thread again, and the realtime `message.deleted` already reads it for the other agents; the discarded reply is not in the list, so it is never drawn as a deleted message. The reason the channel gave (`deliveryError`) is said in both states (`failureNotesOf`, tested): the amber state adds "could not confirm" to it, it does not replace it. A failed reply that the api does not mark definitive (`false`, `null`, or an older api that sends nothing) is shown as "could not confirm" with the duplicate warning and cannot be discarded, even if the channel plainly refused it long ago: the contract says so, and a failure from before `failureDefinitive` stays that way. The two confirmations share one dialog (`ConfirmFailedReplyDialog`), which closes itself if the reply is no longer in the state it was opened for. An e2e (`discard.spec.ts`) covers both states through the screen and the api: a definitive failure is red, "Discard" confirms and the reply leaves the thread with no trace of a deleted message; a failure that may have gone out is amber, has no "Discard", and "Send again" asks first with the duplicate warning. It writes the states in the database (`failureDefinitive`); the failure itself (a refusal of Meta, a timeout) is covered by the integration suite of the api (`message-discard.spec.ts`), and the manual script of the QA (`guion-descarte.md`) is the check against a fake Graph. Left: no component test of the dialogs (no DOM environment; the rules are tested as functions). Original text of the task: (PR feat/discard-failed-message): the view of a message answers `failureDefinitive: true | false | null` (set only for a reply that failed). For a failed reply of the team: `failureDefinitive === true` shows "Discard" beside "Send again" (for who holds `MESSAGES_SEND`, or `MESSAGES_SEND_TEMPLATE` for a template; confirm it in one step, nothing is lost: the text is kept 30 days); otherwise (`false`, `null`) only "Send again", with the warning that the customer may already have the message and may get it twice. `POST /messages/:id/discard` answers 204 (also when it was discarded already); 409 `MESSAGE_DISCARD_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` ("this reply may have reached the customer, so it cannot be discarded; check with them or send it again", already in the error catalog, en and es) means the screen was out of date: show it and read the thread again; any other 409 is a message that is not a failed reply (read the thread again too). The realtime event `message.deleted` of the thread already arrives for the other agents; after it, read the thread again: a discarded reply is not in the list (do not draw it as the tombstone of a deleted message). Words in en and es; no emojis.
- [ ] Known limits of discarding (PR feat/discard-failed-message, rule 12): the failures of before this change read `null` and cannot be discarded; whether a failure is definitive depends on each plugin affirming a refusal (`refused`) (the Meta plugins do; a third party's must also affirm a refusal with `refused`); the files of a discarded reply leave the bucket with the hourly sweep of stray files (within a day), not at once, and their rows (scan state) go with the reply; the text stays 30 days like a deleted one; a discarded reply still counts for `firstResponseAt`, `lastOutboundAt` and `lastMessageAt` of the conversation, as a reply that failed and was not discarded already does (they are written when the reply is queued); the audit entry is written after the commit, as every audit entry of the api, so a process that dies between the two loses it (the row keeps who and when in `deletedById` and `deletedAt`). Two jobs that work on one message at the same time (a stalled job that is run again while the first is alive) could still write the mark over each other; they would also send the message twice, which is the hazard the idempotency key of the provider already answers, and it is not made worse here. Whoever may send a reply may throw away a failed one of another agent, as they may send it again (the decision of the owner: the same permission as to resend); the row keeps who did it.
- [x] **Residual limits of HC-106 (PR `fix/books-store-day`, closed by PR `fix/books-store-day-limits`):** the legal sales books read the documents of a month by the month of the store; the other readers of the fiscal documents were checked and none compares `issued_at` with a server-clock month. **Closed:** (1) a store whose zone the database does not know still reads as UTC, as its entries do (the zone is validated when the store is saved, so only data written by hand reaches it), but no longer in silence: the book logs a Pino warning with the organization and the zones (`splitStoreZones` and `reportUnknownZones`, unit spec; one line per process for the same organization and zones; the zone is matched in any case, as the VAT report and Postgres do; the warning is a log, not a field of the answer, because a new field would touch the api-client, the screen, the texts and the frozen layout of the book, which is not worth it for data written by hand); the integration case pins the UTC reading. (2) the east side of the border is pinned too (a store east of UTC: the first local hour of April is April, not March). **Accepted, not changed:** `AT TIME ZONE` resolves a midnight that a clock change repeats or skips by the rules of Postgres (a local time that does not exist or exists twice is read with the standard-time offset), which was not run against a real zone for this note, so a document made inside that single hour can fall on either side; it needs a zone that changes its clock exactly at the midnight that opens a month, and the effect is one document of one hour, on the side the sale date of its entry already marks. Owner if it ever shows: Step 4B.8b-4.
- [x] **The web asks only for what the role can read (QA VERIF-31 WEB-1/3, VERIF-cd WEB-1/2/3/4; PR `fix/web-role-aware-requests`, rule 12).** A screen that loaded for a role also read data beside its own that the role cannot see, and the console filled with 403s (the inbox ×6 for a role without conversations, the channel directory on the customers screen for a customers-only role, `GET /settings/preferences` on the remittances screen for a Viewer or an accountant). Fixed at the root, not per route: `apps/web/lib/auxiliary-reads.ts` says which permission each such read needs (`AuxiliaryReads`, `mayRead`: the directories of people and channels, the tags and the counts need `conversations:view`; the preferences need `settings:view`, as their routes do), the four directory hooks of `use-inbox-data.ts` ask it (every screen that uses them is covered, the customers one included) and the overdue threshold of the pending panel too; a screen waits with `isAwaiting` (on its way or paused), never on `isPending` alone, which a read that is not made keeps forever (the composer, the bulk pick, the routing rule, the agents panel of the analytics, the channel list of the inbox). `auxiliary-reads.spec.ts` holds the matrix by role (Viewer, an accountant, a customers-only role, Admin) and fails when one of the hooks stops asking. **Not a defect, by design (WEB-3 / WEB-4):** `GET /settings/business-hours` answers 404 for a store that never set them, and `tests/api/settings.spec.ts` ("answers 404 for a store that never set them") pins it; the screen draws the empty state from it. The browser logs a 404 it cannot hide; changing the answer to a 200 would change a contract that the tests and the plugin routes read, for a line in a console. **Debts:** (a) **closed by PR `fix/web-landing-by-role`:** the landing of a role with no inbox (`/` and `/s/{S}` went to the inbox: WEB-2, 5 × 403 for an accountant). `storeLandingPath` (`lib/store-landing.ts`) gives the first screen of the navigation, in its order, that the person may open (the inbox for who has it; the settings last, which open their first allowed page); `chooseStartPath` uses it with the permissions of each membership, tries the store used last and then the others, and goes to `/no-access` when no store has a screen; `/s/{S}` is a client redirect (`StoreRootRedirect` with `storeRootTarget`: the landing of that store, else of another store of the person, never back to itself; the server does not know the permissions). Cases by role in `store-landing.spec.ts` and `start-path.spec.ts`. Debts: the list of screens of `storeLandingPath` and the entries of `StoreNav` are two lists in the same order, held by hand (one list that both read: Step 7.4); an address typed by hand (`/s/{S}/inbox`) still opens the screen that says the person has no permission, as before; a member whose role opens nothing in any store goes to `/no-access`, whose text is written for no store or a suspended one (a message for "your role opens nothing": Step 7.4); the reason of a provider login is told in the channels of the store of the person even when its role has no other screen (as before). (b) the matrix is a spec of the web, not of the routes: a route that changes its permission is not seen by it (a spec that reads the controllers would close it: Step 7.3); (c) the screens that read other auxiliary data with their own `enabled` (the order drawer already does) were not swept again: Step 7.4; (d) a role that reads remittances but has no `settings:view` gets no overdue marker (the threshold is a store preference; it was null for it before, with a 403 in the console): the pending answer could carry `overdueAfterDays` for it, owner Step 4.13 leftovers; (e) the screens that use the directories without `conversations:view` (the identity link form of a customers-only role, the order templates, `useChannelName`) read nothing now, as they did with the 403: a directory route with the permission of those screens, owner Step 7.4; (f) the hooks are held by their text (the web tests have no renderer): a `renderHook` spec would prove the query is idle, Step 7.3.

- [ ] **Media scan that never got a verdict (PR fix/media-scan-early-return, rule 12; owner's dev, 2026-11-09):** the cause was two stacks on one Redis with two databases, both on the BullMQ prefix `bull`: a worker with no row for the media took the `scan-file` job, found none and ended it as a success (50 ms, `returnvalue` null), and the file stayed `pending`. Done: the prefix of the queues is derived from the name of the database (`queuePrefixFor`, `QUEUE_PREFIX` overrides; name only, not host or port, because the api and the worker may reach the database in different ways and a prefix that differed would leave every job unread; two servers with one database name on one Redis share the queues and must set `QUEUE_PREFIX`; the suites that start a worker or an api against Redis must use a database name or a `QUEUE_PREFIX` of their own per session), the api and the worker log the prefix at start, a job with no row logs a warning, and a failed file that is stored shows "check again". Left on purpose: (a) jobs that were waiting under the old prefix `bull` when this lands are not seen by the new workers (dev only; the hourly cleanup queues the pending files again) and any tool that reads the queues (Bull Board, Step 7.x) must use the same prefix; (b) focus goes to the page body when the `Check again` button disappears as the file goes back to `checking` (move it to the chip), and a test of the button needs the DOM environment (there is no component test of the tray yet: `canRecheck` is covered, the button is not); (c) a job with no row still ends as a success, because a row dropped while the job waits is a valid end and the worker cannot tell it from a foreign database; the prefix is what prevents the second case. Closes with: Step 7.4 (b), Step 7.3 (a).

Only the rows that update really changed are announced, and only the worked ones (open, pending, snoozed); the finished ones also leave with the member but without an event. The tests listen to the events on the in-process emitter and read the notifications; the existing realtime listener tests cover the fan-out to sockets, so there is no new test with a real socket. Left: the unassignment leaves no system line in the thread (a manual unassign writes one), and the departing member's still-open socket may receive the event in the instant before it is closed (the payload carries ids, not text); the notification is raised only for OPEN conversations, as the queue rule always was. Original text:** suspending a member (and removing one) leaves their open, pending and snoozed conversations unassigned and back in the queue in the database, but the inbox lists of the other agents do not hear it and show the old assignee until their next read. Emit the reassignment event (`CONVERSATION_ASSIGNED`, `libs/core/domain/realtime/realtime-events.ts`) for each conversation the suspend and remove paths unassign, with a test that a second agent's socket receives it. The same event also closes the second half of this debt (QA round 2, EQ-14 and EQ-15): the notification `conversation.unassigned_queue` ("a conversation went back to the queue", `notifications-inbox.listener.ts`, which listens to `CONVERSATION_ASSIGNED` with `assignedTo: null`) is not raised either when a member is suspended (`members.service.ts`, `updateMany` of the suspend path) or removed (the same call in the remove path), so the team is not told that those conversations are waiting. The test must also assert that notification for the other members who can take them, and that the person who is suspended or removed does not get it.
